2191     @_preprocess_data() 
2192     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
2193     def bar(self, x, height, width=0.8, bottom=None, *, align="center", 
2194             **kwargs): 
2195         r""" 
2196         Make a bar plot. 
2197  
2198         The bars are positioned at *x* with the given *align*\ment. Their 
2199         dimensions are given by *width* and *height*. The vertical baseline 
2200         is *bottom* (default 0). 
2201  
2202         Each of *x*, *height*, *width*, and *bottom* may either be a scalar 
2203         applying to all bars, or it may be a sequence of length N providing a 
2204         separate value for each bar. 
2205  
2206         Parameters 
2207         ---------- 
2208         x : sequence of scalars 
2209             The x coordinates of the bars. See also *align* for the 
2210             alignment of the bars to the coordinates. 
2211  
2212         height : scalar or sequence of scalars 
2213             The height(s) of the bars. 
2214  
2215         width : scalar or array-like, default: 0.8 
2216             The width(s) of the bars. 
2217  
2218         bottom : scalar or array-like, default: 0 
2219             The y coordinate(s) of the bars bases. 
2220  
2221         align : {'center', 'edge'}, default: 'center' 
2222             Alignment of the bars to the *x* coordinates: 
2223  
2224             - 'center': Center the base on the *x* positions. 
2225             - 'edge': Align the left edges of the bars with the *x* positions. 
2226  
2227             To align the bars on the right edge pass a negative *width* and 
2228             ``align='edge'``. 
2229  
2230         Returns 
2231         ------- 
2232         container : `.BarContainer` 
2233             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars. 
2234  
2235         Other Parameters 
2236         ---------------- 
2237         color : scalar or array-like, optional 
2238             The colors of the bar faces. 
2239  
2240         edgecolor : scalar or array-like, optional 
2241             The colors of the bar edges. 
2242  
2243         linewidth : scalar or array-like, optional 
2244             Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges. 
2245  
2246         tick_label : str or array-like, optional 
2247             The tick labels of the bars. 
2248             Default: None (Use default numeric labels.) 
2249  
2250         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
2251             If not *None*, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the bar tips. 
2252             The values are +/- sizes relative to the data: 
2253  
2254             - scalar: symmetric +/- values for all bars 
2255             - shape(N,): symmetric +/- values for each bar 
2256             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
2257               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
2258               errors. 
2259             - *None*: No errorbar. (Default) 
2260  
2261             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
2262             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
2263  
2264         ecolor : scalar or array-like, default: 'black' 
2265             The line color of the errorbars. 
2266  
2267         capsize : scalar, optional 
2268            The length of the error bar caps in points. 
2269            Default: None, which will take the value from 
2270            :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
2271  
2272         error_kw : dict, optional 
2273             Dictionary of kwargs to be passed to the `~.Axes.errorbar` 
2274             method. Values of *ecolor* or *capsize* defined here take 
2275             precedence over the independent kwargs. 
2276  
2277         log : bool, default: False 
2278             If *True*, set the y-axis to be log scale. 
2279  
2280         orientation : {'vertical',  'horizontal'}, optional 
2281             *This is for internal use only.* Please use `barh` for 
2282             horizontal bar plots. Default: 'vertical'. 
2283  
2284         See also 
2285         -------- 
2286         barh: Plot a horizontal bar plot. 
2287  
2288         Notes 
2289         ----- 
2290         The optional arguments *color*, *edgecolor*, *linewidth*, 
2291         *xerr*, and *yerr* can be either scalars or sequences of 
2292         length equal to the number of bars.  This enables you to use 
2293         bar as the basis for stacked bar charts, or candlestick plots. 
2294         Detail: *xerr* and *yerr* are passed directly to 
2295         :meth:`errorbar`, so they can also have shape 2xN for 
2296         independent specification of lower and upper errors. 
2297  
2298         Other optional kwargs: 
2299  
2300         %(Rectangle)s 
2301         """ 
2302         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mpatches.Patch) 
2303         color = kwargs.pop('color', None) 
2304         if color is None: 
2305             color = self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color() 
2306         edgecolor = kwargs.pop('edgecolor', None) 
2307         linewidth = kwargs.pop('linewidth', None) 
2308  
2309         # Because xerr and yerr will be passed to errorbar, most dimension 
2310         # checking and processing will be left to the errorbar method. 
2311         xerr = kwargs.pop('xerr', None) 
2312         yerr = kwargs.pop('yerr', None) 
2313         error_kw = kwargs.pop('error_kw', {}) 
2314         ezorder = error_kw.pop('zorder', None) 
2315         if ezorder is None: 
2316             ezorder = kwargs.get('zorder', None) 
2317             if ezorder is not None: 
2318                 # If using the bar zorder, increment slightly to make sure 
2319                 # errorbars are drawn on top of bars 
2320                 ezorder += 0.01 
2321         error_kw.setdefault('zorder', ezorder) 
2322         ecolor = kwargs.pop('ecolor', 'k') 
2323         capsize = kwargs.pop('capsize', rcParams["errorbar.capsize"]) 
2324         error_kw.setdefault('ecolor', ecolor) 
2325         error_kw.setdefault('capsize', capsize) 
2326  
2327         orientation = kwargs.pop('orientation', 'vertical') 
2328         cbook._check_in_list(['vertical', 'horizontal'], 
2329                              orientation=orientation) 
2330         log = kwargs.pop('log', False) 
2331         label = kwargs.pop('label', '') 
2332         tick_labels = kwargs.pop('tick_label', None) 
2333  
2334         y = bottom  # Matches barh call signature. 
2335         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2336             if y is None: 
2337                 y = 0 
2338         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2339             if x is None: 
2340                 x = 0 
2341  
2342         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2343             self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=height, kwargs=kwargs) 
2344             if log: 
2345                 self.set_yscale('log', nonposy='clip') 
2346         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2347             self._process_unit_info(xdata=width, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
2348             if log: 
2349                 self.set_xscale('log', nonposx='clip') 
2350  
2351         # lets do some conversions now since some types cannot be 
2352         # subtracted uniformly 
2353         if self.xaxis is not None: 
2354             x0 = x 
2355             x = np.asarray(self.convert_xunits(x)) 
2356             width = self._convert_dx(width, x0, x, self.convert_xunits) 
2357             if xerr is not None: 
2358                 xerr = self._convert_dx(xerr, x0, x, self.convert_xunits) 
2359         if self.yaxis is not None: 
2360             y0 = y 
2361             y = np.asarray(self.convert_yunits(y)) 
2362             height = self._convert_dx(height, y0, y, self.convert_yunits) 
2363             if yerr is not None: 
2364                 yerr = self._convert_dx(yerr, y0, y, self.convert_yunits) 
2365  
2366         x, height, width, y, linewidth = np.broadcast_arrays( 
2367             # Make args iterable too. 
2368             np.atleast_1d(x), height, width, y, linewidth) 
2369  
2370         # Now that units have been converted, set the tick locations. 
2371         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2372             tick_label_axis = self.xaxis 
2373             tick_label_position = x 
2374         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2375             tick_label_axis = self.yaxis 
2376             tick_label_position = y 
2377  
2378         linewidth = itertools.cycle(np.atleast_1d(linewidth)) 
2379         color = itertools.chain(itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(color)), 
2380                                 # Fallback if color == "none". 
2381                                 itertools.repeat('none')) 
2382         if edgecolor is None: 
2383             edgecolor = itertools.repeat(None) 
2384         else: 
2385             edgecolor = itertools.chain( 
2386                 itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(edgecolor)), 
2387                 # Fallback if edgecolor == "none". 
2388                 itertools.repeat('none')) 
2389  
2390         # We will now resolve the alignment and really have 
2391         # left, bottom, width, height vectors 
2392         cbook._check_in_list(['center', 'edge'], align=align) 
2393         if align == 'center': 
2394             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2395                 try: 
2396                     left = x - width / 2 
2397                 except TypeError as e: 
2398                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters x ({x.dtype}) ' 
2399                                     f'and width ({width.dtype}) ' 
2400                                     f'are incompatible') from e 
2401                 bottom = y 
2402             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2403                 try: 
2404                     bottom = y - height / 2 
2405                 except TypeError as e: 
2406                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters y ({y.dtype}) ' 
2407                                     f'and height ({height.dtype}) ' 
2408                                     f'are incompatible') from e 
2409                 left = x 
2410         elif align == 'edge': 
2411             left = x 
2412             bottom = y 
2413  
2414         patches = [] 
2415         args = zip(left, bottom, width, height, color, edgecolor, linewidth) 
2416         for l, b, w, h, c, e, lw in args: 
2417             r = mpatches.Rectangle( 
2418                 xy=(l, b), width=w, height=h, 
2419                 facecolor=c, 
2420                 edgecolor=e, 
2421                 linewidth=lw, 
2422                 label='_nolegend_', 
2423                 ) 
2424             r.update(kwargs) 
2425             r.get_path()._interpolation_steps = 100 
2426             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2427                 r.sticky_edges.y.append(b) 
2428             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2429                 r.sticky_edges.x.append(l) 
2430             self.add_patch(r) 
2431             patches.append(r) 
2432  
2433         if xerr is not None or yerr is not None: 
2434             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2435                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info 
2436                 ex = [l + 0.5 * w for l, w in zip(left, width)] 
2437                 ey = [b + h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)] 
2438  
2439             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2440                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info 
2441                 ex = [l + w for l, w in zip(left, width)] 
2442                 ey = [b + 0.5 * h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)] 
2443  
2444             error_kw.setdefault("label", '_nolegend_') 
2445  
2446             errorbar = self.errorbar(ex, ey, 
2447                                      yerr=yerr, xerr=xerr, 
2448                                      fmt='none', **error_kw) 
2449         else: 
2450             errorbar = None 
2451  
2452         self._request_autoscale_view() 
2453  
2454         bar_container = BarContainer(patches, errorbar, label=label) 
2455         self.add_container(bar_container) 
2456  
2457         if tick_labels is not None: 
2458             tick_labels = np.broadcast_to(tick_labels, len(patches)) 
2459             tick_label_axis.set_ticks(tick_label_position) 
2460             tick_label_axis.set_ticklabels(tick_labels) 
2461  
2462         return bar_container

2465     def barh(self, y, width, height=0.8, left=None, *, align="center", 
2466              **kwargs): 
2467         r""" 
2468         Make a horizontal bar plot. 
2469  
2470         The bars are positioned at *y* with the given *align*\ment. Their 
2471         dimensions are given by *width* and *height*. The horizontal baseline 
2472         is *left* (default 0). 
2473  
2474         Each of *y*, *width*, *height*, and *left* may either be a scalar 
2475         applying to all bars, or it may be a sequence of length N providing a 
2476         separate value for each bar. 
2477  
2478         Parameters 
2479         ---------- 
2480         y : scalar or array-like 
2481             The y coordinates of the bars. See also *align* for the 
2482             alignment of the bars to the coordinates. 
2483  
2484         width : scalar or array-like 
2485             The width(s) of the bars. 
2486  
2487         height : sequence of scalars, default: 0.8 
2488             The heights of the bars. 
2489  
2490         left : sequence of scalars, default: 0 
2491             The x coordinates of the left sides of the bars. 
2492  
2493         align : {'center', 'edge'}, default: 'center' 
2494             Alignment of the base to the *y* coordinates*: 
2495  
2496             - 'center': Center the bars on the *y* positions. 
2497             - 'edge': Align the bottom edges of the bars with the *y* 
2498               positions. 
2499  
2500             To align the bars on the top edge pass a negative *height* and 
2501             ``align='edge'``. 
2502  
2503         Returns 
2504         ------- 
2505         container : `.BarContainer` 
2506             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars. 
2507  
2508         Other Parameters 
2509         ---------------- 
2510         color : scalar or array-like, optional 
2511             The colors of the bar faces. 
2512  
2513         edgecolor : scalar or array-like, optional 
2514             The colors of the bar edges. 
2515  
2516         linewidth : scalar or array-like, optional 
2517             Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges. 
2518  
2519         tick_label : str or array-like, optional 
2520             The tick labels of the bars. 
2521             Default: None (Use default numeric labels.) 
2522  
2523         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
2524             If not ``None``, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the 
2525             bar tips. The values are +/- sizes relative to the data: 
2526  
2527             - scalar: symmetric +/- values for all bars 
2528             - shape(N,): symmetric +/- values for each bar 
2529             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
2530               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
2531               errors. 
2532             - *None*: No errorbar. (default) 
2533  
2534             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
2535             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
2536  
2537         ecolor : scalar or array-like, default: 'black' 
2538             The line color of the errorbars. 
2539  
2540         capsize : scalar, optional 
2541            The length of the error bar caps in points. 
2542            Default: None, which will take the value from 
2543            :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
2544  
2545         error_kw : dict, optional 
2546             Dictionary of kwargs to be passed to the `~.Axes.errorbar` 
2547             method. Values of *ecolor* or *capsize* defined here take 
2548             precedence over the independent kwargs. 
2549  
2550         log : bool, default: False 
2551             If ``True``, set the x-axis to be log scale. 
2552  
2553         See also 
2554         -------- 
2555         bar: Plot a vertical bar plot. 
2556  
2557         Notes 
2558         ----- 
2559         The optional arguments *color*, *edgecolor*, *linewidth*, 
2560         *xerr*, and *yerr* can be either scalars or sequences of 
2561         length equal to the number of bars.  This enables you to use 
2562         bar as the basis for stacked bar charts, or candlestick plots. 
2563         Detail: *xerr* and *yerr* are passed directly to 
2564         :meth:`errorbar`, so they can also have shape 2xN for 
2565         independent specification of lower and upper errors. 
2566  
2567         Other optional kwargs: 
2568  
2569         %(Rectangle)s 
2570         """ 
2571         kwargs.setdefault('orientation', 'horizontal') 
2572         patches = self.bar(x=left, height=height, width=width, bottom=y, 
2573                            align=align, **kwargs) 
2574         return patches

2576     @_preprocess_data() 
2577     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
2578     def broken_barh(self, xranges, yrange, **kwargs): 
2579         """ 
2580         Plot a horizontal sequence of rectangles. 
2581  
2582         A rectangle is drawn for each element of *xranges*. All rectangles 
2583         have the same vertical position and size defined by *yrange*. 
2584  
2585         This is a convenience function for instantiating a 
2586         `.BrokenBarHCollection`, adding it to the axes and autoscaling the 
2587         view. 
2588  
2589         Parameters 
2590         ---------- 
2591         xranges : sequence of tuples (*xmin*, *xwidth*) 
2592             The x-positions and extends of the rectangles. For each tuple 
2593             (*xmin*, *xwidth*) a rectangle is drawn from *xmin* to *xmin* + 
2594             *xwidth*. 
2595         yrange : (*ymin*, *yheight*) 
2596             The y-position and extend for all the rectangles. 
2597  
2598         Other Parameters 
2599         ---------------- 
2600         **kwargs : :class:`.BrokenBarHCollection` properties 
2601  
2602             Each *kwarg* can be either a single argument applying to all 
2603             rectangles, e.g.:: 
2604  
2605                 facecolors='black' 
2606  
2607             or a sequence of arguments over which is cycled, e.g.:: 
2608  
2609                 facecolors=('black', 'blue') 
2610  
2611             would create interleaving black and blue rectangles. 
2612  
2613             Supported keywords: 
2614  
2615             %(BrokenBarHCollection)s 
2616  
2617         Returns 
2618         ------- 
2619         collection : A :class:`~.collections.BrokenBarHCollection` 
2620         """ 
2621         # process the unit information 
2622         if len(xranges): 
2623             xdata = cbook.safe_first_element(xranges) 
2624         else: 
2625             xdata = None 
2626         if len(yrange): 
2627             ydata = cbook.safe_first_element(yrange) 
2628         else: 
2629             ydata = None 
2630         self._process_unit_info(xdata=xdata, 
2631                                 ydata=ydata, 
2632                                 kwargs=kwargs) 
2633         xranges_conv = [] 
2634         for xr in xranges: 
2635             if len(xr) != 2: 
2636                 raise ValueError('each range in xrange must be a sequence ' 
2637                                  'with two elements (i.e. an Nx2 array)') 
2638             # convert the absolute values, not the x and dx... 
2639             x_conv = np.asarray(self.convert_xunits(xr[0])) 
2640             x1 = self._convert_dx(xr[1], xr[0], x_conv, self.convert_xunits) 
2641             xranges_conv.append((x_conv, x1)) 
2642  
2643         yrange_conv = self.convert_yunits(yrange) 
2644  
2645         col = mcoll.BrokenBarHCollection(xranges_conv, yrange_conv, **kwargs) 
2646         self.add_collection(col, autolim=True) 
2647         self._request_autoscale_view() 
2648  
2649         return col

2651     @_preprocess_data() 
2652     def stem(self, *args, linefmt=None, markerfmt=None, basefmt=None, bottom=0, 
2653              label=None, use_line_collection=False): 
2654         """ 
2655         Create a stem plot. 
2656  
2657         A stem plot plots vertical lines at each *x* location from the baseline 
2658         to *y*, and places a marker there. 
2659  
2660         Call signature:: 
2661  
2662           stem([x,] y, linefmt=None, markerfmt=None, basefmt=None) 
2663  
2664         The x-positions are optional. The formats may be provided either as 
2665         positional or as keyword-arguments. 
2666  
2667         Parameters 
2668         ---------- 
2669         x : array-like, optional 
2670             The x-positions of the stems. Default: (0, 1, ..., len(y) - 1). 
2671  
2672         y : array-like 
2673             The y-values of the stem heads. 
2674  
2675         linefmt : str, optional 
2676             A string defining the properties of the vertical lines. Usually, 
2677             this will be a color or a color and a linestyle: 
2678  
2679             =========  ============= 
2680             Character  Line Style 
2681             =========  ============= 
2682             ``'-'``    solid line 
2683             ``'--'``   dashed line 
2684             ``'-.'``   dash-dot line 
2685             ``':'``    dotted line 
2686             =========  ============= 
2687  
2688             Default: 'C0-', i.e. solid line with the first color of the color 
2689             cycle. 
2690  
2691             Note: While it is technically possible to specify valid formats 
2692             other than color or color and linestyle (e.g. 'rx' or '-.'), this 
2693             is beyond the intention of the method and will most likely not 
2694             result in a reasonable reasonable plot. 
2695  
2696         markerfmt : str, optional 
2697             A string defining the properties of the markers at the stem heads. 
2698             Default: 'C0o', i.e. filled circles with the first color of the 
2699             color cycle. 
2700  
2701         basefmt : str, default: 'C3-' ('C2-' in classic mode) 
2702             A format string defining the properties of the baseline. 
2703  
2704         bottom : float, default: 0 
2705             The y-position of the baseline. 
2706  
2707         label : str, default: None 
2708             The label to use for the stems in legends. 
2709  
2710         use_line_collection : bool, default: False 
2711             If ``True``, store and plot the stem lines as a 
2712             `~.collections.LineCollection` instead of individual lines. This 
2713             significantly increases performance, and will become the default 
2714             option in Matplotlib 3.3. If ``False``, defaults to the old 
2715             behavior of using a list of `.Line2D` objects. 
2716  
2717         Returns 
2718         ------- 
2719         container : :class:`~matplotlib.container.StemContainer` 
2720             The container may be treated like a tuple 
2721             (*markerline*, *stemlines*, *baseline*) 
2722  
2723         Notes 
2724         ----- 
2725         .. seealso:: 
2726             The MATLAB function 
2727             `stem <http://www.mathworks.com/help/techdoc/ref/stem.html>`_ 
2728             which inspired this method. 
2729         """ 
2730         if not 1 <= len(args) <= 5: 
2731             raise TypeError('stem expected between 1 and 5 positional ' 
2732                             'arguments, got {}'.format(args)) 
2733  
2734         if len(args) == 1: 
2735             y, = args 
2736             x = np.arange(len(y)) 
2737             args = () 
2738         else: 
2739             x, y, *args = args 
2740  
2741         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y) 
2742         x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
2743         y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
2744  
2745         # defaults for formats 
2746         if linefmt is None: 
2747             try: 
2748                 # fallback to positional argument 
2749                 linefmt = args[0] 
2750             except IndexError: 
2751                 linecolor = 'C0' 
2752                 linemarker = 'None' 
2753                 linestyle = '-' 
2754             else: 
2755                 linestyle, linemarker, linecolor = \ 
2756                     _process_plot_format(linefmt) 
2757         else: 
2758             linestyle, linemarker, linecolor = _process_plot_format(linefmt) 
2759  
2760         if markerfmt is None: 
2761             try: 
2762                 # fallback to positional argument 
2763                 markerfmt = args[1] 
2764             except IndexError: 
2765                 markercolor = 'C0' 
2766                 markermarker = 'o' 
2767                 markerstyle = 'None' 
2768             else: 
2769                 markerstyle, markermarker, markercolor = \ 
2770                     _process_plot_format(markerfmt) 
2771         else: 
2772             markerstyle, markermarker, markercolor = \ 
2773                 _process_plot_format(markerfmt) 
2774  
2775         if basefmt is None: 
2776             try: 
2777                 # fallback to positional argument 
2778                 basefmt = args[2] 
2779             except IndexError: 
2780                 if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
2781                     basecolor = 'C2' 
2782                 else: 
2783                     basecolor = 'C3' 
2784                 basemarker = 'None' 
2785                 basestyle = '-' 
2786             else: 
2787                 basestyle, basemarker, basecolor = \ 
2788                     _process_plot_format(basefmt) 
2789         else: 
2790             basestyle, basemarker, basecolor = _process_plot_format(basefmt) 
2791  
2792         # New behaviour in 3.1 is to use a LineCollection for the stemlines 
2793         if use_line_collection: 
2794             stemlines = [((xi, bottom), (xi, yi)) for xi, yi in zip(x, y)] 
2795             if linestyle is None: 
2796                 linestyle = rcParams['lines.linestyle'] 
2797             stemlines = mcoll.LineCollection(stemlines, linestyles=linestyle, 
2798                                              colors=linecolor, 
2799                                              label='_nolegend_') 
2800             self.add_collection(stemlines) 
2801         # Old behaviour is to plot each of the lines individually 
2802         else: 
2803             cbook._warn_external( 
2804                 'In Matplotlib 3.3 individual lines on a stem plot will be ' 
2805                 'added as a LineCollection instead of individual lines. ' 
2806                 'This significantly improves the performance of a stem plot. ' 
2807                 'To remove this warning and switch to the new behaviour, ' 
2808                 'set the "use_line_collection" keyword argument to True.') 
2809             stemlines = [] 
2810             for xi, yi in zip(x, y): 
2811                 l, = self.plot([xi, xi], [bottom, yi], 
2812                                color=linecolor, linestyle=linestyle, 
2813                                marker=linemarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2814                 stemlines.append(l) 
2815  
2816         markerline, = self.plot(x, y, color=markercolor, linestyle=markerstyle, 
2817                                 marker=markermarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2818  
2819         baseline, = self.plot([np.min(x), np.max(x)], [bottom, bottom], 
2820                               color=basecolor, linestyle=basestyle, 
2821                               marker=basemarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2822  
2823         stem_container = StemContainer((markerline, stemlines, baseline), 
2824                                        label=label) 
2825         self.add_container(stem_container) 
2826         return stem_container

2828     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "explode", "labels", "colors"]) 
2829     def pie(self, x, explode=None, labels=None, colors=None, 
2830             autopct=None, pctdistance=0.6, shadow=False, labeldistance=1.1, 
2831             startangle=None, radius=None, counterclock=True, 
2832             wedgeprops=None, textprops=None, center=(0, 0), 
2833             frame=False, rotatelabels=False): 
2834         """ 
2835         Plot a pie chart. 
2836  
2837         Make a pie chart of array *x*.  The fractional area of each wedge is 
2838         given by ``x/sum(x)``.  If ``sum(x) < 1``, then the values of *x* give 
2839         the fractional area directly and the array will not be normalized. The 
2840         resulting pie will have an empty wedge of size ``1 - sum(x)``. 
2841  
2842         The wedges are plotted counterclockwise, by default starting from the 
2843         x-axis. 
2844  
2845         Parameters 
2846         ---------- 
2847         x : array-like 
2848             The wedge sizes. 
2849  
2850         explode : array-like, default: None 
2851             If not *None*, is a ``len(x)`` array which specifies the fraction 
2852             of the radius with which to offset each wedge. 
2853  
2854         labels : list, default: None 
2855             A sequence of strings providing the labels for each wedge 
2856  
2857         colors : array-like, default: None 
2858             A sequence of colors through which the pie chart will cycle.  If 
2859             *None*, will use the colors in the currently active cycle. 
2860  
2861         autopct : None or str or callable, default: None 
2862             If not *None*, is a string or function used to label the wedges 
2863             with their numeric value.  The label will be placed inside the 
2864             wedge.  If it is a format string, the label will be ``fmt%pct``. 
2865             If it is a function, it will be called. 
2866  
2867         pctdistance : float, default: 0.6 
2868             The ratio between the center of each pie slice and the start of 
2869             the text generated by *autopct*.  Ignored if *autopct* is *None*. 
2870  
2871         shadow : bool, default: False 
2872             Draw a shadow beneath the pie. 
2873  
2874         labeldistance : float or None, default: 1.1 
2875             The radial distance at which the pie labels are drawn. 
2876             If set to ``None``, label are not drawn, but are stored for use in 
2877             ``legend()`` 
2878  
2879         startangle : float, default: None 
2880             If not *None*, rotates the start of the pie chart by *angle* 
2881             degrees counterclockwise from the x-axis. 
2882  
2883         radius : float, default: None 
2884             The radius of the pie, if *radius* is *None* it will be set to 1. 
2885  
2886         counterclock : bool, default: True 
2887             Specify fractions direction, clockwise or counterclockwise. 
2888  
2889         wedgeprops : dict, default: None 
2890             Dict of arguments passed to the wedge objects making the pie. 
2891             For example, you can pass in ``wedgeprops = {'linewidth': 3}`` 
2892             to set the width of the wedge border lines equal to 3. 
2893             For more details, look at the doc/arguments of the wedge object. 
2894             By default ``clip_on=False``. 
2895  
2896         textprops : dict, default: None 
2897             Dict of arguments to pass to the text objects. 
2898  
2899         center : (float, float), default: (0, 0) 
2900             The coordinates of the center of the chart. 
2901  
2902         frame : bool, default: False 
2903             Plot axes frame with the chart if true. 
2904  
2905         rotatelabels : bool, default: False 
2906             Rotate each label to the angle of the corresponding slice if true. 
2907  
2908         Returns 
2909         ------- 
2910         patches : list 
2911             A sequence of :class:`matplotlib.patches.Wedge` instances 
2912  
2913         texts : list 
2914             A list of the label :class:`matplotlib.text.Text` instances. 
2915  
2916         autotexts : list 
2917             A list of :class:`~matplotlib.text.Text` instances for the numeric 
2918             labels. This will only be returned if the parameter *autopct* is 
2919             not *None*. 
2920  
2921         Notes 
2922         ----- 
2923         The pie chart will probably look best if the figure and axes are 
2924         square, or the Axes aspect is equal. 
2925         This method sets the aspect ratio of the axis to "equal". 
2926         The axes aspect ratio can be controlled with `Axes.set_aspect`. 
2927         """ 
2928         self.set_aspect('equal') 
2929         # The use of float32 is "historical", but can't be changed without 
2930         # regenerating the test baselines. 
2931         x = np.asarray(x, np.float32) 
2932         if x.ndim != 1 and x.squeeze().ndim <= 1: 
2933             cbook.warn_deprecated( 
2934                 "3.1", message="Non-1D inputs to pie() are currently " 
2935                 "squeeze()d, but this behavior is deprecated since %(since)s " 
2936                 "and will be removed %(removal)s; pass a 1D array instead.") 
2937             x = np.atleast_1d(x.squeeze()) 
2938  
2939         sx = x.sum() 
2940         if sx > 1: 
2941             x = x / sx 
2942  
2943         if labels is None: 
2944             labels = [''] * len(x) 
2945         if explode is None: 
2946             explode = [0] * len(x) 
2947         if len(x) != len(labels): 
2948             raise ValueError("'label' must be of length 'x'") 
2949         if len(x) != len(explode): 
2950             raise ValueError("'explode' must be of length 'x'") 
2951         if colors is None: 
2952             get_next_color = self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color 
2953         else: 
2954             color_cycle = itertools.cycle(colors) 
2955  
2956             def get_next_color(): 
2957                 return next(color_cycle) 
2958  
2959         if radius is None: 
2960             radius = 1 
2961  
2962         # Starting theta1 is the start fraction of the circle 
2963         if startangle is None: 
2964             theta1 = 0 
2965         else: 
2966             theta1 = startangle / 360.0 
2967  
2968         # set default values in wedge_prop 
2969         if wedgeprops is None: 
2970             wedgeprops = {} 
2971         wedgeprops.setdefault('clip_on', False) 
2972  
2973         if textprops is None: 
2974             textprops = {} 
2975         textprops.setdefault('clip_on', False) 
2976  
2977         texts = [] 
2978         slices = [] 
2979         autotexts = [] 
2980  
2981         for frac, label, expl in zip(x, labels, explode): 
2982             x, y = center 
2983             theta2 = (theta1 + frac) if counterclock else (theta1 - frac) 
2984             thetam = 2 * np.pi * 0.5 * (theta1 + theta2) 
2985             x += expl * math.cos(thetam) 
2986             y += expl * math.sin(thetam) 
2987  
2988             w = mpatches.Wedge((x, y), radius, 360. * min(theta1, theta2), 
2989                                360. * max(theta1, theta2), 
2990                                facecolor=get_next_color(), 
2991                                **wedgeprops) 
2992             slices.append(w) 
2993             self.add_patch(w) 
2994             w.set_label(label) 
2995  
2996             if shadow: 
2997                 # make sure to add a shadow after the call to 
2998                 # add_patch so the figure and transform props will be 
2999                 # set 
3000                 shad = mpatches.Shadow(w, -0.02, -0.02) 
3001                 shad.set_zorder(0.9 * w.get_zorder()) 
3002                 shad.set_label('_nolegend_') 
3003                 self.add_patch(shad) 
3004  
3005             if labeldistance is not None: 
3006                 xt = x + labeldistance * radius * math.cos(thetam) 
3007                 yt = y + labeldistance * radius * math.sin(thetam) 
3008                 label_alignment_h = 'left' if xt > 0 else 'right' 
3009                 label_alignment_v = 'center' 
3010                 label_rotation = 'horizontal' 
3011                 if rotatelabels: 
3012                     label_alignment_v = 'bottom' if yt > 0 else 'top' 
3013                     label_rotation = (np.rad2deg(thetam) 
3014                                       + (0 if xt > 0 else 180)) 
3015                 props = dict(horizontalalignment=label_alignment_h, 
3016                              verticalalignment=label_alignment_v, 
3017                              rotation=label_rotation, 
3018                              size=rcParams['xtick.labelsize']) 
3019                 props.update(textprops) 
3020  
3021                 t = self.text(xt, yt, label, **props) 
3022  
3023                 texts.append(t) 
3024  
3025             if autopct is not None: 
3026                 xt = x + pctdistance * radius * math.cos(thetam) 
3027                 yt = y + pctdistance * radius * math.sin(thetam) 
3028                 if isinstance(autopct, str): 
3029                     s = autopct % (100. * frac) 
3030                 elif callable(autopct): 
3031                     s = autopct(100. * frac) 
3032                 else: 
3033                     raise TypeError( 
3034                         'autopct must be callable or a format string') 
3035  
3036                 props = dict(horizontalalignment='center', 
3037                              verticalalignment='center') 
3038                 props.update(textprops) 
3039                 t = self.text(xt, yt, s, **props) 
3040  
3041                 autotexts.append(t) 
3042  
3043             theta1 = theta2 
3044  
3045         if not frame: 
3046             self.set_frame_on(False) 
3047  
3048             self.set_xlim((-1.25 + center[0], 
3049                            1.25 + center[0])) 
3050             self.set_ylim((-1.25 + center[1], 
3051                            1.25 + center[1])) 
3052             self.set_xticks([]) 
3053             self.set_yticks([]) 
3054  
3055         if autopct is None: 
3056             return slices, texts 
3057         else: 
3058             return slices, texts, autotexts

3060     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y", "xerr", "yerr"], 
3061                       label_namer="y") 
3062     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
3063     def errorbar(self, x, y, yerr=None, xerr=None, 
3064                  fmt='', ecolor=None, elinewidth=None, capsize=None, 
3065                  barsabove=False, lolims=False, uplims=False, 
3066                  xlolims=False, xuplims=False, errorevery=1, capthick=None, 
3067                  **kwargs): 
3068         """ 
3069         Plot y versus x as lines and/or markers with attached errorbars. 
3070  
3071         *x*, *y* define the data locations, *xerr*, *yerr* define the errorbar 
3072         sizes. By default, this draws the data markers/lines as well the 
3073         errorbars. Use fmt='none' to draw errorbars without any data markers. 
3074  
3075         Parameters 
3076         ---------- 
3077         x, y : scalar or array-like 
3078             The data positions. 
3079  
3080         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like, shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
3081             The errorbar sizes: 
3082  
3083             - scalar: Symmetric +/- values for all data points. 
3084             - shape(N,): Symmetric +/-values for each data point. 
3085             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
3086               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
3087               errors. 
3088             - *None*: No errorbar. 
3089  
3090             Note that all error arrays should have *positive* values. 
3091  
3092             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
3093             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
3094  
3095         fmt : str, default: '' 
3096             The format for the data points / data lines. See `.plot` for 
3097             details. 
3098  
3099             Use 'none' (case insensitive) to plot errorbars without any data 
3100             markers. 
3101  
3102         ecolor : color, default: None 
3103             The color of the errorbar lines.  If None, use the color of the 
3104             line connecting the markers. 
3105  
3106         elinewidth : scalar, default: None 
3107             The linewidth of the errorbar lines. If None, the linewidth of 
3108             the current style is used. 
3109  
3110         capsize : scalar, default: None 
3111             The length of the error bar caps in points. If None, it will take 
3112             the value from :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
3113  
3114         capthick : scalar, default: None 
3115             An alias to the keyword argument *markeredgewidth* (a.k.a. *mew*). 
3116             This setting is a more sensible name for the property that 
3117             controls the thickness of the error bar cap in points. For 
3118             backwards compatibility, if *mew* or *markeredgewidth* are given, 
3119             then they will over-ride *capthick*. This may change in future 
3120             releases. 
3121  
3122         barsabove : bool, default: False 
3123             If True, will plot the errorbars above the plot 
3124             symbols. Default is below. 
3125  
3126         lolims, uplims, xlolims, xuplims : bool, default: False 
3127             These arguments can be used to indicate that a value gives only 
3128             upper/lower limits. In that case a caret symbol is used to 
3129             indicate this. *lims*-arguments may be of the same type as *xerr* 
3130             and *yerr*.  To use limits with inverted axes, :meth:`set_xlim` 
3131             or :meth:`set_ylim` must be called before :meth:`errorbar`. 
3132  
3133         errorevery : int or (int, int), default: 1 
3134             draws error bars on a subset of the data. *errorevery* =N draws 
3135             error bars on the points (x[::N], y[::N]). 
3136             *errorevery* =(start, N) draws error bars on the points 
3137             (x[start::N], y[start::N]). e.g. errorevery=(6, 3) 
3138             adds error bars to the data at (x[6], x[9], x[12], x[15], ...). 
3139             Used to avoid overlapping error bars when two series share x-axis 
3140             values. 
3141  
3142         Returns 
3143         ------- 
3144         container : :class:`~.container.ErrorbarContainer` 
3145             The container contains: 
3146  
3147             - plotline: `.Line2D` instance of x, y plot markers and/or line. 
3148             - caplines: A tuple of `.Line2D` instances of the error bar caps. 
3149             - barlinecols: A tuple of 
3150               :class:`~matplotlib.collections.LineCollection` with the 
3151               horizontal and vertical error ranges. 
3152  
3153         Other Parameters 
3154         ---------------- 
3155         **kwargs 
3156             All other keyword arguments are passed on to the plot 
3157             command for the markers. For example, this code makes big red 
3158             squares with thick green edges:: 
3159  
3160                 x, y, yerr = rand(3, 10) 
3161                 errorbar(x, y, yerr, marker='s', mfc='red', 
3162                          mec='green', ms=20, mew=4) 
3163  
3164             where *mfc*, *mec*, *ms* and *mew* are aliases for the longer 
3165             property names, *markerfacecolor*, *markeredgecolor*, *markersize* 
3166             and *markeredgewidth*. 
3167  
3168             Valid kwargs for the marker properties are `.Lines2D` properties: 
3169  
3170             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
3171         """ 
3172         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D) 
3173         # anything that comes in as 'None', drop so the default thing 
3174         # happens down stream 
3175         kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if v is not None} 
3176         kwargs.setdefault('zorder', 2) 
3177  
3178         try: 
3179             offset, errorevery = errorevery 
3180         except TypeError: 
3181             offset = 0 
3182  
3183         if errorevery < 1 or int(errorevery) != errorevery: 
3184             raise ValueError( 
3185                 'errorevery must be positive integer or tuple of integers') 
3186         if int(offset) != offset: 
3187             raise ValueError("errorevery's starting index must be an integer") 
3188  
3189         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
3190  
3191         plot_line = (fmt.lower() != 'none') 
3192         label = kwargs.pop("label", None) 
3193  
3194         if fmt == '': 
3195             fmt_style_kwargs = {} 
3196         else: 
3197             fmt_style_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in 
3198                                 zip(('linestyle', 'marker', 'color'), 
3199                                     _process_plot_format(fmt)) 
3200                                 if v is not None} 
3201         if fmt == 'none': 
3202             # Remove alpha=0 color that _process_plot_format returns 
3203             fmt_style_kwargs.pop('color') 
3204  
3205         if ('color' in kwargs or 'color' in fmt_style_kwargs or 
3206                 ecolor is not None): 
3207             base_style = {} 
3208             if 'color' in kwargs: 
3209                 base_style['color'] = kwargs.pop('color') 
3210         else: 
3211             base_style = next(self._get_lines.prop_cycler) 
3212  
3213         base_style['label'] = '_nolegend_' 
3214         base_style.update(fmt_style_kwargs) 
3215         if 'color' not in base_style: 
3216             base_style['color'] = 'C0' 
3217         if ecolor is None: 
3218             ecolor = base_style['color'] 
3219         # make sure all the args are iterable; use lists not arrays to 
3220         # preserve units 
3221         if not np.iterable(x): 
3222             x = [x] 
3223  
3224         if not np.iterable(y): 
3225             y = [y] 
3226  
3227         if xerr is not None: 
3228             if not np.iterable(xerr): 
3229                 xerr = [xerr] * len(x) 
3230  
3231         if yerr is not None: 
3232             if not np.iterable(yerr): 
3233                 yerr = [yerr] * len(y) 
3234  
3235         # make the style dict for the 'normal' plot line 
3236         plot_line_style = { 
3237             **base_style, 
3238             **kwargs, 
3239             'zorder': (kwargs['zorder'] - .1 if barsabove else 
3240                        kwargs['zorder'] + .1), 
3241         } 
3242  
3243         # make the style dict for the line collections (the bars) 
3244         eb_lines_style = dict(base_style) 
3245         eb_lines_style.pop('marker', None) 
3246         eb_lines_style.pop('linestyle', None) 
3247         eb_lines_style['color'] = ecolor 
3248  
3249         if elinewidth: 
3250             eb_lines_style['linewidth'] = elinewidth 
3251         elif 'linewidth' in kwargs: 
3252             eb_lines_style['linewidth'] = kwargs['linewidth'] 
3253  
3254         for key in ('transform', 'alpha', 'zorder', 'rasterized'): 
3255             if key in kwargs: 
3256                 eb_lines_style[key] = kwargs[key] 
3257  
3258         # set up cap style dictionary 
3259         eb_cap_style = dict(base_style) 
3260         # eject any marker information from format string 
3261         eb_cap_style.pop('marker', None) 
3262         eb_lines_style.pop('markerfacecolor', None) 
3263         eb_lines_style.pop('markeredgewidth', None) 
3264         eb_lines_style.pop('markeredgecolor', None) 
3265         eb_cap_style.pop('ls', None) 
3266         eb_cap_style['linestyle'] = 'none' 
3267         if capsize is None: 
3268             capsize = rcParams["errorbar.capsize"] 
3269         if capsize > 0: 
3270             eb_cap_style['markersize'] = 2. * capsize 
3271         if capthick is not None: 
3272             eb_cap_style['markeredgewidth'] = capthick 
3273  
3274         # For backwards-compat, allow explicit setting of 
3275         # 'markeredgewidth' to over-ride capthick. 
3276         for key in ('markeredgewidth', 'transform', 'alpha', 
3277                     'zorder', 'rasterized'): 
3278             if key in kwargs: 
3279                 eb_cap_style[key] = kwargs[key] 
3280         eb_cap_style['color'] = ecolor 
3281  
3282         data_line = None 
3283         if plot_line: 
3284             data_line = mlines.Line2D(x, y, **plot_line_style) 
3285             self.add_line(data_line) 
3286  
3287         barcols = [] 
3288         caplines = [] 
3289  
3290         # arrays fine here, they are booleans and hence not units 
3291         lolims = np.broadcast_to(lolims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3292         uplims = np.broadcast_to(uplims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3293         xlolims = np.broadcast_to(xlolims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3294         xuplims = np.broadcast_to(xuplims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3295  
3296         everymask = np.zeros(len(x), bool) 
3297         everymask[offset::errorevery] = True 
3298  
3299         def xywhere(xs, ys, mask): 
3300             """ 
3301             return xs[mask], ys[mask] where mask is True but xs and 
3302             ys are not arrays 
3303             """ 
3304             assert len(xs) == len(ys) 
3305             assert len(xs) == len(mask) 
3306             xs = [thisx for thisx, b in zip(xs, mask) if b] 
3307             ys = [thisy for thisy, b in zip(ys, mask) if b] 
3308             return xs, ys 
3309  
3310         def extract_err(err, data): 
3311             """ 
3312             Private function to parse *err* and subtract/add it to *data*. 
3313  
3314             Both *err* and *data* are already iterables at this point. 
3315             """ 
3316             try:  # Asymmetric error: pair of 1D iterables. 
3317                 a, b = err 
3318                 iter(a) 
3319                 iter(b) 
3320             except (TypeError, ValueError): 
3321                 a = b = err  # Symmetric error: 1D iterable. 
3322             # This could just be `np.ndim(a) > 1 and np.ndim(b) > 1`, except 
3323             # for the (undocumented, but tested) support for (n, 1) arrays. 
3324             a_sh = np.shape(a) 
3325             b_sh = np.shape(b) 
3326             if (len(a_sh) > 2 or (len(a_sh) == 2 and a_sh[1] != 1) 
3327                     or len(b_sh) > 2 or (len(b_sh) == 2 and b_sh[1] != 1)): 
3328                 raise ValueError( 
3329                     "err must be a scalar or a 1D or (2, n) array-like") 
3330             if len(a_sh) == 2 or len(b_sh) == 2: 
3331                 cbook.warn_deprecated( 
3332                     "3.1", message="Support for passing a (n, 1)-shaped error " 
3333                     "array to errorbar() is deprecated since Matplotlib " 
3334                     "%(since)s and will be removed %(removal)s; pass a 1D " 
3335                     "array instead.") 
3336             # Using list comprehensions rather than arrays to preserve units. 
3337             for e in [a, b]: 
3338                 if len(data) != len(e): 
3339                     raise ValueError( 
3340                         f"The lengths of the data ({len(data)}) and the " 
3341                         f"error {len(e)} do not match") 
3342             low = [v - e for v, e in zip(data, a)] 
3343             high = [v + e for v, e in zip(data, b)] 
3344             return low, high 
3345  
3346         if xerr is not None: 
3347             left, right = extract_err(xerr, x) 
3348             # select points without upper/lower limits in x and 
3349             # draw normal errorbars for these points 
3350             noxlims = ~(xlolims | xuplims) 
3351             if noxlims.any() or len(noxlims) == 0: 
3352                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, noxlims & everymask) 
3353                 lo, ro = xywhere(left, right, noxlims & everymask) 
3354                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3355                 if capsize > 0: 
3356                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(lo, yo, marker='|', 
3357                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3358                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(ro, yo, marker='|', 
3359                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3360  
3361             if xlolims.any(): 
3362                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, xlolims & everymask) 
3363                 lo, ro = xywhere(x, right, xlolims & everymask) 
3364                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3365                 rightup, yup = xywhere(right, y, xlolims & everymask) 
3366                 if self.xaxis_inverted(): 
3367                     marker = mlines.CARETLEFTBASE 
3368                 else: 
3369                     marker = mlines.CARETRIGHTBASE 
3370                 caplines.append( 
3371                     mlines.Line2D(rightup, yup, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3372                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3373                 if capsize > 0: 
3374                     xlo, ylo = xywhere(x, y, xlolims & everymask) 
3375                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xlo, ylo, marker='|', 
3376                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3377  
3378             if xuplims.any(): 
3379                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, xuplims & everymask) 
3380                 lo, ro = xywhere(left, x, xuplims & everymask) 
3381                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3382                 leftlo, ylo = xywhere(left, y, xuplims & everymask) 
3383                 if self.xaxis_inverted(): 
3384                     marker = mlines.CARETRIGHTBASE 
3385                 else: 
3386                     marker = mlines.CARETLEFTBASE 
3387                 caplines.append( 
3388                     mlines.Line2D(leftlo, ylo, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3389                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3390                 if capsize > 0: 
3391                     xup, yup = xywhere(x, y, xuplims & everymask) 
3392                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xup, yup, marker='|', 
3393                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3394  
3395         if yerr is not None: 
3396             lower, upper = extract_err(yerr, y) 
3397             # select points without upper/lower limits in y and 
3398             # draw normal errorbars for these points 
3399             noylims = ~(lolims | uplims) 
3400             if noylims.any() or len(noylims) == 0: 
3401                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, noylims & everymask) 
3402                 lo, uo = xywhere(lower, upper, noylims & everymask) 
3403                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3404                 if capsize > 0: 
3405                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xo, lo, marker='_', 
3406                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3407                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xo, uo, marker='_', 
3408                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3409  
3410             if lolims.any(): 
3411                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, lolims & everymask) 
3412                 lo, uo = xywhere(y, upper, lolims & everymask) 
3413                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3414                 xup, upperup = xywhere(x, upper, lolims & everymask) 
3415                 if self.yaxis_inverted(): 
3416                     marker = mlines.CARETDOWNBASE 
3417                 else: 
3418                     marker = mlines.CARETUPBASE 
3419                 caplines.append( 
3420                     mlines.Line2D(xup, upperup, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3421                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3422                 if capsize > 0: 
3423                     xlo, ylo = xywhere(x, y, lolims & everymask) 
3424                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xlo, ylo, marker='_', 
3425                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3426  
3427             if uplims.any(): 
3428                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, uplims & everymask) 
3429                 lo, uo = xywhere(lower, y, uplims & everymask) 
3430                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3431                 xlo, lowerlo = xywhere(x, lower, uplims & everymask) 
3432                 if self.yaxis_inverted(): 
3433                     marker = mlines.CARETUPBASE 
3434                 else: 
3435                     marker = mlines.CARETDOWNBASE 
3436                 caplines.append( 
3437                     mlines.Line2D(xlo, lowerlo, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3438                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3439                 if capsize > 0: 
3440                     xup, yup = xywhere(x, y, uplims & everymask) 
3441                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xup, yup, marker='_', 
3442                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3443         for l in caplines: 
3444             self.add_line(l) 
3445  
3446         self._request_autoscale_view() 
3447         errorbar_container = ErrorbarContainer((data_line, tuple(caplines), 
3448                                                 tuple(barcols)), 
3449                                                has_xerr=(xerr is not None), 
3450                                                has_yerr=(yerr is not None), 
3451                                                label=label) 
3452         self.containers.append(errorbar_container) 
3453  
3454         return errorbar_container  # (l0, caplines, barcols)
