3456     @cbook._rename_parameter("3.1", "manage_xticks", "manage_ticks") 
3457     @_preprocess_data() 
3458     def boxplot(self, x, notch=None, sym=None, vert=None, whis=None, 
3459                 positions=None, widths=None, patch_artist=None, 
3460                 bootstrap=None, usermedians=None, conf_intervals=None, 
3461                 meanline=None, showmeans=None, showcaps=None, 
3462                 showbox=None, showfliers=None, boxprops=None, 
3463                 labels=None, flierprops=None, medianprops=None, 
3464                 meanprops=None, capprops=None, whiskerprops=None, 
3465                 manage_ticks=True, autorange=False, zorder=None): 
3466         """ 
3467         Make a box and whisker plot. 
3468  
3469         Make a box and whisker plot for each column of ``x`` or each 
3470         vector in sequence ``x``.  The box extends from the lower to 
3471         upper quartile values of the data, with a line at the median. 
3472         The whiskers extend from the box to show the range of the 
3473         data.  Flier points are those past the end of the whiskers. 
3474  
3475         Parameters 
3476         ---------- 
3477         x : Array or a sequence of vectors. 
3478             The input data. 
3479  
3480         notch : bool, default: False 
3481             If `True`, will produce a notched box plot. Otherwise, a 
3482             rectangular boxplot is produced. The notches represent the 
3483             confidence interval (CI) around the median. See the entry 
3484             for the ``bootstrap`` parameter for information regarding 
3485             how the locations of the notches are computed. 
3486  
3487             .. note:: 
3488  
3489                 In cases where the values of the CI are less than the 
3490                 lower quartile or greater than the upper quartile, the 
3491                 notches will extend beyond the box, giving it a 
3492                 distinctive "flipped" appearance. This is expected 
3493                 behavior and consistent with other statistical 
3494                 visualization packages. 
3495  
3496         sym : str, optional 
3497             The default symbol for flier points. Enter an empty string 
3498             ('') if you don't want to show fliers. If `None`, then the 
3499             fliers default to 'b+'  If you want more control use the 
3500             flierprops kwarg. 
3501  
3502         vert : bool, default: True 
3503             If `True`, draws vertical boxes. 
3504             If `False`, draw horizontal boxes. 
3505  
3506         whis : float or (float, float), default: 1.5 
3507             The position of the whiskers. 
3508  
3509             If a float, the lower whisker is at the lowest datum above 
3510             ``Q1 - whis*(Q3-Q1)``, and the upper whisker at the highest datum 
3511             below ``Q3 + whis*(Q3-Q1)``, where Q1 and Q3 are the first and 
3512             third quartiles.  The default value of ``whis = 1.5`` corresponds 
3513             to Tukey's original definition of boxplots. 
3514  
3515             If a pair of floats, they indicate the percentiles at which to 
3516             draw the whiskers (e.g., (5, 95)).  In particular, setting this to 
3517             (0, 100) results in whiskers covering the whole range of the data. 
3518             "range" is a deprecated synonym for (0, 100). 
3519  
3520             In the edge case where ``Q1 == Q3``, *whis* is automatically set 
3521             to (0, 100) (cover the whole range of the data) if *autorange* is 
3522             True. 
3523  
3524             Beyond the whiskers, data are considered outliers and are plotted 
3525             as individual points. 
3526  
3527         bootstrap : int, optional 
3528             Specifies whether to bootstrap the confidence intervals 
3529             around the median for notched boxplots. If ``bootstrap`` is 
3530             None, no bootstrapping is performed, and notches are 
3531             calculated using a Gaussian-based asymptotic approximation 
3532             (see McGill, R., Tukey, J.W., and Larsen, W.A., 1978, and 
3533             Kendall and Stuart, 1967). Otherwise, bootstrap specifies 
3534             the number of times to bootstrap the median to determine its 
3535             95% confidence intervals. Values between 1000 and 10000 are 
3536             recommended. 
3537  
3538         usermedians : array-like, optional 
3539             An array or sequence whose first dimension (or length) is 
3540             compatible with ``x``. This overrides the medians computed 
3541             by matplotlib for each element of ``usermedians`` that is not 
3542             `None`. When an element of ``usermedians`` is None, the median 
3543             will be computed by matplotlib as normal. 
3544  
3545         conf_intervals : array-like, optional 
3546             Array or sequence whose first dimension (or length) is 
3547             compatible with ``x`` and whose second dimension is 2. When 
3548             the an element of ``conf_intervals`` is not None, the 
3549             notch locations computed by matplotlib are overridden 
3550             (provided ``notch`` is `True`). When an element of 
3551             ``conf_intervals`` is `None`, the notches are computed by the 
3552             method specified by the other kwargs (e.g., ``bootstrap``). 
3553  
3554         positions : array-like, optional 
3555             Sets the positions of the boxes. The ticks and limits are 
3556             automatically set to match the positions. Defaults to 
3557             `range(1, N+1)` where N is the number of boxes to be drawn. 
3558  
3559         widths : scalar or array-like 
3560             Sets the width of each box either with a scalar or a 
3561             sequence. The default is 0.5, or ``0.15*(distance between 
3562             extreme positions)``, if that is smaller. 
3563  
3564         patch_artist : bool, default: False 
3565             If `False` produces boxes with the Line2D artist. Otherwise, 
3566             boxes and drawn with Patch artists. 
3567  
3568         labels : sequence, optional 
3569             Labels for each dataset. Length must be compatible with 
3570             dimensions of ``x``. 
3571  
3572         manage_ticks : bool, default: True 
3573             If True, the tick locations and labels will be adjusted to match 
3574             the boxplot positions. 
3575  
3576         autorange : bool, default: False 
3577             When `True` and the data are distributed such that the 25th and 
3578             75th percentiles are equal, ``whis`` is set to (0, 100) such 
3579             that the whisker ends are at the minimum and maximum of the data. 
3580  
3581         meanline : bool, default: False 
3582             If `True` (and ``showmeans`` is `True`), will try to render 
3583             the mean as a line spanning the full width of the box 
3584             according to ``meanprops`` (see below). Not recommended if 
3585             ``shownotches`` is also True. Otherwise, means will be shown 
3586             as points. 
3587  
3588         zorder : scalar, default: None 
3589             Sets the zorder of the boxplot. 
3590  
3591         Other Parameters 
3592         ---------------- 
3593         showcaps : bool, default: True 
3594             Show the caps on the ends of whiskers. 
3595         showbox : bool, default: True 
3596             Show the central box. 
3597         showfliers : bool, default: True 
3598             Show the outliers beyond the caps. 
3599         showmeans : bool, default: False 
3600             Show the arithmetic means. 
3601         capprops : dict, default: None 
3602             The style of the caps. 
3603         boxprops : dict, default: None 
3604             The style of the box. 
3605         whiskerprops : dict, default: None 
3606             The style of the whiskers. 
3607         flierprops : dict, default: None 
3608             The style of the fliers. 
3609         medianprops : dict, default: None 
3610             The style of the median. 
3611         meanprops : dict, default: None 
3612             The style of the mean. 
3613  
3614         Returns 
3615         ------- 
3616         result : dict 
3617           A dictionary mapping each component of the boxplot to a list 
3618           of the `.Line2D` instances created. That dictionary has the 
3619           following keys (assuming vertical boxplots): 
3620  
3621           - ``boxes``: the main body of the boxplot showing the 
3622             quartiles and the median's confidence intervals if 
3623             enabled. 
3624  
3625           - ``medians``: horizontal lines at the median of each box. 
3626  
3627           - ``whiskers``: the vertical lines extending to the most 
3628             extreme, non-outlier data points. 
3629  
3630           - ``caps``: the horizontal lines at the ends of the 
3631             whiskers. 
3632  
3633           - ``fliers``: points representing data that extend beyond 
3634             the whiskers (fliers). 
3635  
3636           - ``means``: points or lines representing the means. 
3637  
3638         """ 
3639  
3640         # Missing arguments default to rcParams. 
3641         if whis is None: 
3642             whis = rcParams['boxplot.whiskers'] 
3643         if bootstrap is None: 
3644             bootstrap = rcParams['boxplot.bootstrap'] 
3645  
3646         bxpstats = cbook.boxplot_stats(x, whis=whis, bootstrap=bootstrap, 
3647                                        labels=labels, autorange=autorange) 
3648         if notch is None: 
3649             notch = rcParams['boxplot.notch'] 
3650         if vert is None: 
3651             vert = rcParams['boxplot.vertical'] 
3652         if patch_artist is None: 
3653             patch_artist = rcParams['boxplot.patchartist'] 
3654         if meanline is None: 
3655             meanline = rcParams['boxplot.meanline'] 
3656         if showmeans is None: 
3657             showmeans = rcParams['boxplot.showmeans'] 
3658         if showcaps is None: 
3659             showcaps = rcParams['boxplot.showcaps'] 
3660         if showbox is None: 
3661             showbox = rcParams['boxplot.showbox'] 
3662         if showfliers is None: 
3663             showfliers = rcParams['boxplot.showfliers'] 
3664  
3665         if boxprops is None: 
3666             boxprops = {} 
3667         if whiskerprops is None: 
3668             whiskerprops = {} 
3669         if capprops is None: 
3670             capprops = {} 
3671         if medianprops is None: 
3672             medianprops = {} 
3673         if meanprops is None: 
3674             meanprops = {} 
3675         if flierprops is None: 
3676             flierprops = {} 
3677  
3678         if patch_artist: 
3679             boxprops['linestyle'] = 'solid'  # Not consistent with bxp. 
3680             if 'color' in boxprops: 
3681                 boxprops['edgecolor'] = boxprops.pop('color') 
3682  
3683         # if non-default sym value, put it into the flier dictionary 
3684         # the logic for providing the default symbol ('b+') now lives 
3685         # in bxp in the initial value of final_flierprops 
3686         # handle all of the *sym* related logic here so we only have to pass 
3687         # on the flierprops dict. 
3688         if sym is not None: 
3689             # no-flier case, which should really be done with 
3690             # 'showfliers=False' but none-the-less deal with it to keep back 
3691             # compatibility 
3692             if sym == '': 
3693                 # blow away existing dict and make one for invisible markers 
3694                 flierprops = dict(linestyle='none', marker='', color='none') 
3695                 # turn the fliers off just to be safe 
3696                 showfliers = False 
3697             # now process the symbol string 
3698             else: 
3699                 # process the symbol string 
3700                 # discarded linestyle 
3701                 _, marker, color = _process_plot_format(sym) 
3702                 # if we have a marker, use it 
3703                 if marker is not None: 
3704                     flierprops['marker'] = marker 
3705                 # if we have a color, use it 
3706                 if color is not None: 
3707                     # assume that if color is passed in the user want 
3708                     # filled symbol, if the users want more control use 
3709                     # flierprops 
3710                     flierprops['color'] = color 
3711                     flierprops['markerfacecolor'] = color 
3712                     flierprops['markeredgecolor'] = color 
3713  
3714         # replace medians if necessary: 
3715         if usermedians is not None: 
3716             if (len(np.ravel(usermedians)) != len(bxpstats) or 
3717                     np.shape(usermedians)[0] != len(bxpstats)): 
3718                 raise ValueError('usermedians length not compatible with x') 
3719             else: 
3720                 # reassign medians as necessary 
3721                 for stats, med in zip(bxpstats, usermedians): 
3722                     if med is not None: 
3723                         stats['med'] = med 
3724  
3725         if conf_intervals is not None: 
3726             if np.shape(conf_intervals)[0] != len(bxpstats): 
3727                 err_mess = 'conf_intervals length not compatible with x' 
3728                 raise ValueError(err_mess) 
3729             else: 
3730                 for stats, ci in zip(bxpstats, conf_intervals): 
3731                     if ci is not None: 
3732                         if len(ci) != 2: 
3733                             raise ValueError('each confidence interval must ' 
3734                                              'have two values') 
3735                         else: 
3736                             if ci[0] is not None: 
3737                                 stats['cilo'] = ci[0] 
3738                             if ci[1] is not None: 
3739                                 stats['cihi'] = ci[1] 
3740  
3741         artists = self.bxp(bxpstats, positions=positions, widths=widths, 
3742                            vert=vert, patch_artist=patch_artist, 
3743                            shownotches=notch, showmeans=showmeans, 
3744                            showcaps=showcaps, showbox=showbox, 
3745                            boxprops=boxprops, flierprops=flierprops, 
3746                            medianprops=medianprops, meanprops=meanprops, 
3747                            meanline=meanline, showfliers=showfliers, 
3748                            capprops=capprops, whiskerprops=whiskerprops, 
3749                            manage_ticks=manage_ticks, zorder=zorder) 
3750         return artists 
3751  
3752     @cbook._rename_parameter("3.1", "manage_xticks", "manage_ticks") 
3753     def bxp(self, bxpstats, positions=None, widths=None, vert=True, 
3754             patch_artist=False, shownotches=False, showmeans=False, 
3755             showcaps=True, showbox=True, showfliers=True, 
3756             boxprops=None, whiskerprops=None, flierprops=None, 
3757             medianprops=None, capprops=None, meanprops=None, 
3758             meanline=False, manage_ticks=True, zorder=None): 
3759         """ 
3760         Drawing function for box and whisker plots. 
3761  
3762         Make a box and whisker plot for each column of *x* or each 
3763         vector in sequence *x*.  The box extends from the lower to 
3764         upper quartile values of the data, with a line at the median. 
3765         The whiskers extend from the box to show the range of the 
3766         data.  Flier points are those past the end of the whiskers. 
3767  
3768         Parameters 
3769         ---------- 
3770         bxpstats : list of dicts 
3771           A list of dictionaries containing stats for each boxplot. 
3772           Required keys are: 
3773  
3774           - ``med``: The median (scalar float). 
3775  
3776           - ``q1``: The first quartile (25th percentile) (scalar 
3777             float). 
3778  
3779           - ``q3``: The third quartile (75th percentile) (scalar 
3780             float). 
3781  
3782           - ``whislo``: Lower bound of the lower whisker (scalar 
3783             float). 
3784  
3785           - ``whishi``: Upper bound of the upper whisker (scalar 
3786             float). 
3787  
3788           Optional keys are: 
3789  
3790           - ``mean``: The mean (scalar float). Needed if 
3791             ``showmeans=True``. 
3792  
3793           - ``fliers``: Data beyond the whiskers (sequence of floats). 
3794             Needed if ``showfliers=True``. 
3795  
3796           - ``cilo`` & ``cihi``: Lower and upper confidence intervals 
3797             about the median. Needed if ``shownotches=True``. 
3798  
3799           - ``label``: Name of the dataset (string). If available, 
3800             this will be used a tick label for the boxplot 
3801  
3802         positions : array-like, default: [1, 2, ..., n] 
3803           Sets the positions of the boxes. The ticks and limits 
3804           are automatically set to match the positions. 
3805  
3806         widths : array-like, default: None 
3807           Either a scalar or a vector and sets the width of each 
3808           box. The default is ``0.15*(distance between extreme 
3809           positions)``, clipped to no less than 0.15 and no more than 
3810           0.5. 
3811  
3812         vert : bool, default: True 
3813           If `True` (default), makes the boxes vertical.  If `False`, 
3814           makes horizontal boxes. 
3815  
3816         patch_artist : bool, default: False 
3817           If `False` produces boxes with the `.Line2D` artist. 
3818           If `True` produces boxes with the `~matplotlib.patches.Patch` artist. 
3819  
3820         shownotches : bool, default: False 
3821           If `False` (default), produces a rectangular box plot. 
3822           If `True`, will produce a notched box plot 
3823  
3824         showmeans : bool, default: False 
3825           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the means 
3826  
3827         showcaps  : bool, default: True 
3828           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the caps 
3829  
3830         showbox  : bool, default: True 
3831           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the box 
3832  
3833         showfliers : bool, default: True 
3834           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the fliers 
3835  
3836         boxprops : dict or None (default) 
3837           If provided, will set the plotting style of the boxes 
3838  
3839         whiskerprops : dict or None (default) 
3840           If provided, will set the plotting style of the whiskers 
3841  
3842         capprops : dict or None (default) 
3843           If provided, will set the plotting style of the caps 
3844  
3845         flierprops : dict or None (default) 
3846           If provided will set the plotting style of the fliers 
3847  
3848         medianprops : dict or None (default) 
3849           If provided, will set the plotting style of the medians 
3850  
3851         meanprops : dict or None (default) 
3852           If provided, will set the plotting style of the means 
3853  
3854         meanline : bool, default: False 
3855           If `True` (and *showmeans* is `True`), will try to render the mean 
3856           as a line spanning the full width of the box according to 
3857           *meanprops*. Not recommended if *shownotches* is also True. 
3858           Otherwise, means will be shown as points. 
3859  
3860         manage_ticks : bool, default: True 
3861           If True, the tick locations and labels will be adjusted to match the 
3862           boxplot positions. 
3863  
3864         zorder : scalar, default: None 
3865           The zorder of the resulting boxplot. 
3866  
3867         Returns 
3868         ------- 
3869         result : dict 
3870           A dictionary mapping each component of the boxplot to a list 
3871           of the `.Line2D` instances created. That dictionary has the 
3872           following keys (assuming vertical boxplots): 
3873  
3874           - ``boxes``: the main body of the boxplot showing the 
3875             quartiles and the median's confidence intervals if 
3876             enabled. 
3877  
3878           - ``medians``: horizontal lines at the median of each box. 
3879  
3880           - ``whiskers``: the vertical lines extending to the most 
3881             extreme, non-outlier data points. 
3882  
3883           - ``caps``: the horizontal lines at the ends of the 
3884             whiskers. 
3885  
3886           - ``fliers``: points representing data that extend beyond 
3887             the whiskers (fliers). 
3888  
3889           - ``means``: points or lines representing the means. 
3890  
3891         Examples 
3892         -------- 
3893         .. plot:: gallery/statistics/bxp.py 
3894  
3895         """ 
3896         # lists of artists to be output 
3897         whiskers = [] 
3898         caps = [] 
3899         boxes = [] 
3900         medians = [] 
3901         means = [] 
3902         fliers = [] 
3903  
3904         # empty list of xticklabels 
3905         datalabels = [] 
3906  
3907         # Use default zorder if none specified 
3908         if zorder is None: 
3909             zorder = mlines.Line2D.zorder 
3910  
3911         zdelta = 0.1 
3912  
3913         def line_props_with_rcdefaults(subkey, explicit, zdelta=0): 
3914             d = {k.split('.')[-1]: v for k, v in rcParams.items() 
3915                  if k.startswith(f'boxplot.{subkey}')} 
3916             d['zorder'] = zorder + zdelta 
3917             if explicit is not None: 
3918                 d.update( 
3919                     cbook.normalize_kwargs(explicit, mlines.Line2D._alias_map)) 
3920             return d 
3921  
3922         # box properties 
3923         if patch_artist: 
3924             final_boxprops = dict( 
3925                 linestyle=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.linestyle'], 
3926                 linewidth=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.linewidth'], 
3927                 edgecolor=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.color'], 
3928                 facecolor=('white' if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] else 
3929                            rcParams['patch.facecolor']), 
3930                 zorder=zorder, 
3931             ) 
3932             if boxprops is not None: 
3933                 final_boxprops.update( 
3934                     cbook.normalize_kwargs( 
3935                         boxprops, mpatches.PathPatch._alias_map)) 
3936         else: 
3937             final_boxprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults('boxprops', boxprops) 
3938         final_whiskerprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3939             'whiskerprops', whiskerprops) 
3940         final_capprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3941             'capprops', capprops) 
3942         final_flierprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3943             'flierprops', flierprops) 
3944         final_medianprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3945             'medianprops', medianprops, zdelta) 
3946         final_meanprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3947             'meanprops', meanprops, zdelta) 
3948         removed_prop = 'marker' if meanline else 'linestyle' 
3949         # Only remove the property if it's not set explicitly as a parameter. 
3950         if meanprops is None or removed_prop not in meanprops: 
3951             final_meanprops[removed_prop] = '' 
3952  
3953         def to_vc(xs, ys): 
3954             # convert arguments to verts and codes, append (0, 0) (ignored). 
3955             verts = np.append(np.column_stack([xs, ys]), [(0, 0)], 0) 
3956             codes = ([mpath.Path.MOVETO] 
3957                      + [mpath.Path.LINETO] * (len(verts) - 2) 
3958                      + [mpath.Path.CLOSEPOLY]) 
3959             return verts, codes 
3960  
3961         def patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3962             verts, codes = to_vc(xs, ys) 
3963             path = mpath.Path(verts, codes) 
3964             patch = mpatches.PathPatch(path, **kwargs) 
3965             self.add_artist(patch) 
3966             return [patch] 
3967  
3968         # vertical or horizontal plot? 
3969         if vert: 
3970             def doplot(*args, **kwargs): 
3971                 return self.plot(*args, **kwargs) 
3972  
3973             def dopatch(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3974                 return patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs) 
3975  
3976         else: 
3977             def doplot(*args, **kwargs): 
3978                 shuffled = [] 
3979                 for i in range(0, len(args), 2): 
3980                     shuffled.extend([args[i + 1], args[i]]) 
3981                 return self.plot(*shuffled, **kwargs) 
3982  
3983             def dopatch(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3984                 xs, ys = ys, xs  # flip X, Y 
3985                 return patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs) 
3986  
3987         # input validation 
3988         N = len(bxpstats) 
3989         datashape_message = ("List of boxplot statistics and `{0}` " 
3990                              "values must have same the length") 
3991         # check position 
3992         if positions is None: 
3993             positions = list(range(1, N + 1)) 
3994         elif len(positions) != N: 
3995             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("positions")) 
3996  
3997         positions = np.array(positions) 
3998         if len(positions) > 0 and not isinstance(positions[0], Number): 
3999             raise TypeError("positions should be an iterable of numbers") 
4000  
4001         # width 
4002         if widths is None: 
4003             widths = [np.clip(0.15 * np.ptp(positions), 0.15, 0.5)] * N 
4004         elif np.isscalar(widths): 
4005             widths = [widths] * N 
4006         elif len(widths) != N: 
4007             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("widths")) 
4008  
4009         for pos, width, stats in zip(positions, widths, bxpstats): 
4010             # try to find a new label 
4011             datalabels.append(stats.get('label', pos)) 
4012  
4013             # whisker coords 
4014             whisker_x = np.ones(2) * pos 
4015             whiskerlo_y = np.array([stats['q1'], stats['whislo']]) 
4016             whiskerhi_y = np.array([stats['q3'], stats['whishi']]) 
4017  
4018             # cap coords 
4019             cap_left = pos - width * 0.25 
4020             cap_right = pos + width * 0.25 
4021             cap_x = np.array([cap_left, cap_right]) 
4022             cap_lo = np.ones(2) * stats['whislo'] 
4023             cap_hi = np.ones(2) * stats['whishi'] 
4024  
4025             # box and median coords 
4026             box_left = pos - width * 0.5 
4027             box_right = pos + width * 0.5 
4028             med_y = [stats['med'], stats['med']] 
4029  
4030             # notched boxes 
4031             if shownotches: 
4032                 box_x = [box_left, box_right, box_right, cap_right, box_right, 
4033                          box_right, box_left, box_left, cap_left, box_left, 
4034                          box_left] 
4035                 box_y = [stats['q1'], stats['q1'], stats['cilo'], 
4036                          stats['med'], stats['cihi'], stats['q3'], 
4037                          stats['q3'], stats['cihi'], stats['med'], 
4038                          stats['cilo'], stats['q1']] 
4039                 med_x = cap_x 
4040  
4041             # plain boxes 
4042             else: 
4043                 box_x = [box_left, box_right, box_right, box_left, box_left] 
4044                 box_y = [stats['q1'], stats['q1'], stats['q3'], stats['q3'], 
4045                          stats['q1']] 
4046                 med_x = [box_left, box_right] 
4047  
4048             # maybe draw the box: 
4049             if showbox: 
4050                 if patch_artist: 
4051                     boxes.extend(dopatch(box_x, box_y, **final_boxprops)) 
4052                 else: 
4053                     boxes.extend(doplot(box_x, box_y, **final_boxprops)) 
4054  
4055             # draw the whiskers 
4056             whiskers.extend(doplot( 
4057                 whisker_x, whiskerlo_y, **final_whiskerprops 
4058             )) 
4059             whiskers.extend(doplot( 
4060                 whisker_x, whiskerhi_y, **final_whiskerprops 
4061             )) 
4062  
4063             # maybe draw the caps: 
4064             if showcaps: 
4065                 caps.extend(doplot(cap_x, cap_lo, **final_capprops)) 
4066                 caps.extend(doplot(cap_x, cap_hi, **final_capprops)) 
4067  
4068             # draw the medians 
4069             medians.extend(doplot(med_x, med_y, **final_medianprops)) 
4070  
4071             # maybe draw the means 
4072             if showmeans: 
4073                 if meanline: 
4074                     means.extend(doplot( 
4075                         [box_left, box_right], [stats['mean'], stats['mean']], 
4076                         **final_meanprops 
4077                     )) 
4078                 else: 
4079                     means.extend(doplot( 
4080                         [pos], [stats['mean']], **final_meanprops 
4081                     )) 
4082  
4083             # maybe draw the fliers 
4084             if showfliers: 
4085                 # fliers coords 
4086                 flier_x = np.full(len(stats['fliers']), pos, dtype=np.float64) 
4087                 flier_y = stats['fliers'] 
4088  
4089                 fliers.extend(doplot( 
4090                     flier_x, flier_y, **final_flierprops 
4091                 )) 
4092  
4093         if manage_ticks: 
4094             axis_name = "x" if vert else "y" 
4095             interval = getattr(self.dataLim, f"interval{axis_name}") 
4096             axis = getattr(self, f"{axis_name}axis") 
4097             positions = axis.convert_units(positions) 
4098             # The 0.5 additional padding ensures reasonable-looking boxes 
4099             # even when drawing a single box.  We set the sticky edge to 
4100             # prevent margins expansion, in order to match old behavior (back 
4101             # when separate calls to boxplot() would completely reset the axis 
4102             # limits regardless of what was drawn before).  The sticky edges 
4103             # are attached to the median lines, as they are always present. 
4104             interval[:] = (min(interval[0], min(positions) - .5), 
4105                            max(interval[1], max(positions) + .5)) 
4106             for median, position in zip(medians, positions): 
4107                 getattr(median.sticky_edges, axis_name).extend( 
4108                     [position - .5, position + .5]) 
4109             # Modified from Axis.set_ticks and Axis.set_ticklabels. 
4110             locator = axis.get_major_locator() 
4111             if not isinstance(axis.get_major_locator(), 
4112                               mticker.FixedLocator): 
4113                 locator = mticker.FixedLocator([]) 
4114                 axis.set_major_locator(locator) 
4115             locator.locs = np.array([*locator.locs, *positions]) 
4116             formatter = axis.get_major_formatter() 
4117             if not isinstance(axis.get_major_formatter(), 
4118                               mticker.FixedFormatter): 
4119                 formatter = mticker.FixedFormatter([]) 
4120                 axis.set_major_formatter(formatter) 
4121             formatter.seq = [*formatter.seq, *datalabels] 
4122  
4123             self._request_autoscale_view( 
4124                 scalex=self._autoscaleXon, scaley=self._autoscaleYon) 
4125  
4126         return dict(whiskers=whiskers, caps=caps, boxes=boxes, 
4127                     medians=medians, fliers=fliers, means=means) 
4128  
4129     @staticmethod 
4130     def _parse_scatter_color_args(c, edgecolors, kwargs, xsize, 
4131                                   get_next_color_func): 
4132         """ 
4133         Helper function to process color related arguments of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4134  
4135         Argument precedence for facecolors: 
4136  
4137         - c (if not None) 
4138         - kwargs['facecolors'] 
4139         - kwargs['facecolor'] 
4140         - kwargs['color'] (==kwcolor) 
4141         - 'b' if in classic mode else the result of ``get_next_color_func()`` 
4142  
4143         Argument precedence for edgecolors: 
4144  
4145         - edgecolors (is an explicit kw argument in scatter()) 
4146         - kwargs['edgecolor'] 
4147         - kwargs['color'] (==kwcolor) 
4148         - 'face' if not in classic mode else None 
4149  
4150         Parameters 
4151         ---------- 
4152         c : color or sequence or sequence of color or None 
4153             See argument description of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4154         edgecolors : color or sequence of color or {'face', 'none'} or None 
4155             See argument description of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4156         kwargs : dict 
4157             Additional kwargs. If these keys exist, we pop and process them: 
4158             'facecolors', 'facecolor', 'edgecolor', 'color' 
4159             Note: The dict is modified by this function. 
4160         xsize : int 
4161             The size of the x and y arrays passed to `.Axes.scatter`. 
4162         get_next_color_func : callable 
4163             A callable that returns a color. This color is used as facecolor 
4164             if no other color is provided. 
4165  
4166             Note, that this is a function rather than a fixed color value to 
4167             support conditional evaluation of the next color.  As of the 
4168             current implementation obtaining the next color from the 
4169             property cycle advances the cycle. This must only happen if we 
4170             actually use the color, which will only be decided within this 
4171             method. 
4172  
4173         Returns 
4174         ------- 
4175         c 
4176             The input *c* if it was not *None*, else a color derived from the 
4177             other inputs or defaults. 
4178         colors : array(N, 4) or None 
4179             The facecolors as RGBA values, or *None* if a colormap is used. 
4180         edgecolors 
4181             The edgecolor. 
4182  
4183         """ 
4184         facecolors = kwargs.pop('facecolors', None) 
4185         facecolors = kwargs.pop('facecolor', facecolors) 
4186         edgecolors = kwargs.pop('edgecolor', edgecolors) 
4187  
4188         kwcolor = kwargs.pop('color', None) 
4189  
4190         if kwcolor is not None and c is not None: 
4191             raise ValueError("Supply a 'c' argument or a 'color'" 
4192                              " kwarg but not both; they differ but" 
4193                              " their functionalities overlap.") 
4194  
4195         if kwcolor is not None: 
4196             try: 
4197                 mcolors.to_rgba_array(kwcolor) 
4198             except ValueError: 
4199                 raise ValueError( 
4200                     "'color' kwarg must be an color or sequence of color " 
4201                     "specs.  For a sequence of values to be color-mapped, use " 
4202                     "the 'c' argument instead.") 
4203             if edgecolors is None: 
4204                 edgecolors = kwcolor 
4205             if facecolors is None: 
4206                 facecolors = kwcolor 
4207  
4208         if edgecolors is None and not rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
4209             edgecolors = rcParams['scatter.edgecolors'] 
4210  
4211         c_was_none = c is None 
4212         if c is None: 
4213             c = (facecolors if facecolors is not None 
4214                  else "b" if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] 
4215                  else get_next_color_func()) 
4216         c_is_string_or_strings = ( 
4217             isinstance(c, str) 
4218             or (isinstance(c, collections.abc.Iterable) and len(c) > 0 
4219                 and isinstance(cbook.safe_first_element(c), str))) 
4220  
4221         def invalid_shape_exception(csize, xsize): 
4222             return ValueError( 
4223                 f"'c' argument has {csize} elements, which is inconsistent " 
4224                 f"with 'x' and 'y' with size {xsize}.") 
4225  
4226         c_is_mapped = False  # Unless proven otherwise below. 
4227         valid_shape = True  # Unless proven otherwise below. 
4228         if not c_was_none and kwcolor is None and not c_is_string_or_strings: 
4229             try:  # First, does 'c' look suitable for value-mapping? 
4230                 c = np.asanyarray(c, dtype=float) 
4231             except ValueError: 
4232                 pass  # Failed to convert to float array; must be color specs. 
4233             else: 
4234                 # If c can be either mapped values or a RGB(A) color, prefer 
4235                 # the former if shapes match, the latter otherwise. 
4236                 if c.size == xsize: 
4237                     c = c.ravel() 
4238                     c_is_mapped = True 
4239                 else:  # Wrong size; it must not be intended for mapping. 
4240                     if c.shape in ((3,), (4,)): 
4241                         _log.warning( 
4242                             "'c' argument looks like a single numeric RGB or " 
4243                             "RGBA sequence, which should be avoided as value-" 
4244                             "mapping will have precedence in case its length " 
4245                             "matches with 'x' & 'y'.  Please use a 2-D array " 
4246                             "with a single row if you really want to specify " 
4247                             "the same RGB or RGBA value for all points.") 
4248                     valid_shape = False 
4249         if not c_is_mapped: 
4250             try:  # Is 'c' acceptable as PathCollection facecolors? 
4251                 colors = mcolors.to_rgba_array(c) 
4252             except ValueError: 
4253                 if not valid_shape: 
4254                     raise invalid_shape_exception(c.size, xsize) 
4255                 # Both the mapping *and* the RGBA conversion failed: pretty 
4256                 # severe failure => one may appreciate a verbose feedback. 
4257                 raise ValueError( 
4258                     f"'c' argument must be a color, a sequence of colors, or " 
4259                     f"a sequence of numbers, not {c}") 
4260             else: 
4261                 if len(colors) not in (0, 1, xsize): 
4262                     # NB: remember that a single color is also acceptable. 
4263                     # Besides *colors* will be an empty array if c == 'none'. 
4264                     raise invalid_shape_exception(len(colors), xsize) 
4265         else: 
4266             colors = None  # use cmap, norm after collection is created 
4267         return c, colors, edgecolors 
4268  
4269     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y", "s", "linewidths", 
4270                                      "edgecolors", "c", "facecolor", 
4271                                      "facecolors", "color"], 
4272                       label_namer="y") 
4273     @cbook._delete_parameter("3.2", "verts") 
4274     def scatter(self, x, y, s=None, c=None, marker=None, cmap=None, norm=None, 
4275                 vmin=None, vmax=None, alpha=None, linewidths=None, 
4276                 verts=None, edgecolors=None, *, plotnonfinite=False, 
4277                 **kwargs): 
4278         """ 
4279         A scatter plot of *y* vs. *x* with varying marker size and/or color. 
4280  
4281         Parameters 
4282         ---------- 
4283         x, y : scalar or array-like, shape (n, ) 
4284             The data positions. 
4285  
4286         s : scalar or array-like, shape (n, ), optional 
4287             The marker size in points**2. 
4288             Default is ``rcParams['lines.markersize'] ** 2``. 
4289  
4290         c : color, sequence, or sequence of colors, optional 
4291             The marker color. Possible values: 
4292  
4293             - A single color format string. 
4294             - A sequence of colors of length n. 
4295             - A scalar or sequence of n numbers to be mapped to colors using 
4296               *cmap* and *norm*. 
4297             - A 2-D array in which the rows are RGB or RGBA. 
4298  
4299             Note that *c* should not be a single numeric RGB or RGBA sequence 
4300             because that is indistinguishable from an array of values to be 
4301             colormapped. If you want to specify the same RGB or RGBA value for 
4302             all points, use a 2-D array with a single row.  Otherwise, value- 
4303             matching will have precedence in case of a size matching with *x* 
4304             and *y*. 
4305  
4306             Defaults to ``None``. In that case the marker color is determined 
4307             by the value of ``color``, ``facecolor`` or ``facecolors``. In case 
4308             those are not specified or ``None``, the marker color is determined 
4309             by the next color of the ``Axes``' current "shape and fill" color 
4310             cycle. This cycle defaults to :rc:`axes.prop_cycle`. 
4311  
4312         marker : `~matplotlib.markers.MarkerStyle`, optional 
4313             The marker style. *marker* can be either an instance of the class 
4314             or the text shorthand for a particular marker. 
4315             Defaults to ``None``, in which case it takes the value of 
4316             :rc:`scatter.marker` = 'o'. 
4317             See `~matplotlib.markers` for more information about marker styles. 
4318  
4319         cmap : `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
4320             A `.Colormap` instance or registered colormap name. *cmap* is only 
4321             used if *c* is an array of floats. If ``None``, defaults to 
4322             :rc:`image.cmap`. 
4323  
4324         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, default: None 
4325             A `.Normalize` instance is used to scale luminance data to 0, 1. 
4326             *norm* is only used if *c* is an array of floats. If *None*, use 
4327             the default `.colors.Normalize`. 
4328  
4329         vmin, vmax : scalar, default: None 
4330             *vmin* and *vmax* are used in conjunction with *norm* to normalize 
4331             luminance data. If None, the respective min and max of the color 
4332             array is used. *vmin* and *vmax* are ignored if you pass a *norm* 
4333             instance. 
4334  
4335         alpha : scalar, default: None 
4336             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
4337  
4338         linewidths : scalar or array-like, default: None 
4339             The linewidth of the marker edges. Note: The default *edgecolors* 
4340             is 'face'. You may want to change this as well. 
4341             If *None*, defaults to :rc:`lines.linewidth`. 
4342  
4343         edgecolors : {'face', 'none', *None*} or color or sequence of color, \ 
4344 optional. 
4345             The edge color of the marker. Possible values: 
4346  
4347             - 'face': The edge color will always be the same as the face color. 
4348             - 'none': No patch boundary will be drawn. 
4349             - A color or sequence of colors. 
4350  
4351             Defaults to ``None``, in which case it takes the value of 
4352             :rc:`scatter.edgecolors` = 'face'. 
4353  
4354             For non-filled markers, the *edgecolors* kwarg is ignored and 
4355             forced to 'face' internally. 
4356  
4357         plotnonfinite : bool, default: False 
4358             Set to plot points with nonfinite *c*, in conjunction with 
4359             `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap.set_bad`. 
4360  
4361         Returns 
4362         ------- 
4363         paths : `~matplotlib.collections.PathCollection` 
4364  
4365         Other Parameters 
4366         ---------------- 
4367         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.collections.Collection` properties 
4368  
4369         See Also 
4370         -------- 
4371         plot : To plot scatter plots when markers are identical in size and 
4372             color. 
4373  
4374         Notes 
4375         ----- 
4376         * The `.plot` function will be faster for scatterplots where markers 
4377           don't vary in size or color. 
4378  
4379         * Any or all of *x*, *y*, *s*, and *c* may be masked arrays, in which 
4380           case all masks will be combined and only unmasked points will be 
4381           plotted. 
4382  
4383         * Fundamentally, scatter works with 1-D arrays; *x*, *y*, *s*, and *c* 
4384           may be input as N-D arrays, but within scatter they will be 
4385           flattened. The exception is *c*, which will be flattened only if its 
4386           size matches the size of *x* and *y*. 
4387  
4388         """ 
4389         # Process **kwargs to handle aliases, conflicts with explicit kwargs: 
4390  
4391         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
4392         x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
4393         y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
4394  
4395         # np.ma.ravel yields an ndarray, not a masked array, 
4396         # unless its argument is a masked array. 
4397         x = np.ma.ravel(x) 
4398         y = np.ma.ravel(y) 
4399         if x.size != y.size: 
4400             raise ValueError("x and y must be the same size") 
4401  
4402         if s is None: 
4403             s = (20 if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] else 
4404                  rcParams['lines.markersize'] ** 2.0) 
4405         s = np.ma.ravel(s) 
4406         if len(s) not in (1, x.size): 
4407             raise ValueError("s must be a scalar, or the same size as x and y") 
4408  
4409         c, colors, edgecolors = \ 
4410             self._parse_scatter_color_args( 
4411                 c, edgecolors, kwargs, x.size, 
4412                 get_next_color_func=self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color) 
4413  
4414         if plotnonfinite and colors is None: 
4415             c = np.ma.masked_invalid(c) 
4416             x, y, s, edgecolors, linewidths = \ 
4417                 cbook._combine_masks(x, y, s, edgecolors, linewidths) 
4418         else: 
4419             x, y, s, c, colors, edgecolors, linewidths = \ 
4420                 cbook._combine_masks( 
4421                     x, y, s, c, colors, edgecolors, linewidths) 
4422  
4423         scales = s   # Renamed for readability below. 
4424  
4425         # load default marker from rcParams 
4426         if marker is None: 
4427             marker = rcParams['scatter.marker'] 
4428  
4429         if isinstance(marker, mmarkers.MarkerStyle): 
4430             marker_obj = marker 
4431         else: 
4432             marker_obj = mmarkers.MarkerStyle(marker) 
4433  
4434         path = marker_obj.get_path().transformed( 
4435             marker_obj.get_transform()) 
4436         if not marker_obj.is_filled(): 
4437             edgecolors = 'face' 
4438             linewidths = rcParams['lines.linewidth'] 
4439  
4440         offsets = np.ma.column_stack([x, y]) 
4441  
4442         collection = mcoll.PathCollection( 
4443                 (path,), scales, 
4444                 facecolors=colors, 
4445                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4446                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4447                 offsets=offsets, 
4448                 transOffset=kwargs.pop('transform', self.transData), 
4449                 alpha=alpha 
4450                 ) 
4451         collection.set_transform(mtransforms.IdentityTransform()) 
4452         collection.update(kwargs) 
4453  
4454         if colors is None: 
4455             collection.set_array(c) 
4456             collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
4457             collection.set_norm(norm) 
4458  
4459             if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
4460                 collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
4461             else: 
4462                 collection.autoscale_None() 
4463  
4464         # Classic mode only: 
4465         # ensure there are margins to allow for the 
4466         # finite size of the symbols.  In v2.x, margins 
4467         # are present by default, so we disable this 
4468         # scatter-specific override. 
4469         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
4470             if self._xmargin < 0.05 and x.size > 0: 
4471                 self.set_xmargin(0.05) 
4472             if self._ymargin < 0.05 and x.size > 0: 
4473                 self.set_ymargin(0.05) 
4474  
4475         self.add_collection(collection) 
4476         self._request_autoscale_view() 
4477  
4478         return collection

4480     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y") 
4481     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
4482     def hexbin(self, x, y, C=None, gridsize=100, bins=None, 
4483                xscale='linear', yscale='linear', extent=None, 
4484                cmap=None, norm=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, 
4485                alpha=None, linewidths=None, edgecolors='face', 
4486                reduce_C_function=np.mean, mincnt=None, marginals=False, 
4487                **kwargs): 
4488         """ 
4489         Make a 2D hexagonal binning plot of points *x*, *y*. 
4490  
4491         If *C* is *None*, the value of the hexagon is determined by the number 
4492         of points in the hexagon. Otherwise, *C* specifies values at the 
4493         coordinate (x[i], y[i]). For each hexagon, these values are reduced 
4494         using *reduce_C_function*. 
4495  
4496         Parameters 
4497         ---------- 
4498         x, y : array-like 
4499             The data positions. *x* and *y* must be of the same length. 
4500  
4501         C : array-like, optional 
4502             If given, these values are accumulated in the bins. Otherwise, 
4503             every point has a value of 1. Must be of the same length as *x* 
4504             and *y*. 
4505  
4506         gridsize : int or (int, int), default: 100 
4507             If a single int, the number of hexagons in the *x*-direction. 
4508             The number of hexagons in the *y*-direction is chosen such that 
4509             the hexagons are approximately regular. 
4510  
4511             Alternatively, if a tuple (*nx*, *ny*), the number of hexagons 
4512             in the *x*-direction and the *y*-direction. 
4513  
4514         bins : 'log' or int or sequence, default: None 
4515             Discretization of the hexagon values. 
4516  
4517             - If *None*, no binning is applied; the color of each hexagon 
4518               directly corresponds to its count value. 
4519             - If 'log', use a logarithmic scale for the color map. 
4520               Internally, :math:`log_{10}(i+1)` is used to determine the 
4521               hexagon color. This is equivalent to ``norm=LogNorm()``. 
4522             - If an integer, divide the counts in the specified number 
4523               of bins, and color the hexagons accordingly. 
4524             - If a sequence of values, the values of the lower bound of 
4525               the bins to be used. 
4526  
4527         xscale : {'linear', 'log'}, default: 'linear' 
4528             Use a linear or log10 scale on the horizontal axis. 
4529  
4530         yscale : {'linear', 'log'}, default: 'linear' 
4531             Use a linear or log10 scale on the vertical axis. 
4532  
4533         mincnt : int > 0, default: *None* 
4534             If not *None*, only display cells with more than *mincnt* 
4535             number of points in the cell. 
4536  
4537         marginals : bool, default: *False* 
4538             If marginals is *True*, plot the marginal density as 
4539             colormapped rectangles along the bottom of the x-axis and 
4540             left of the y-axis. 
4541  
4542         extent : float, default: *None* 
4543             The limits of the bins. The default assigns the limits 
4544             based on *gridsize*, *x*, *y*, *xscale* and *yscale*. 
4545  
4546             If *xscale* or *yscale* is set to 'log', the limits are 
4547             expected to be the exponent for a power of 10. E.g. for 
4548             x-limits of 1 and 50 in 'linear' scale and y-limits 
4549             of 10 and 1000 in 'log' scale, enter (1, 50, 1, 3). 
4550  
4551             Order of scalars is (left, right, bottom, top). 
4552  
4553         Other Parameters 
4554         ---------------- 
4555         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
4556             The Colormap instance or registered colormap name used to map 
4557             the bin values to colors. Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
4558  
4559         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
4560             The Normalize instance scales the bin values to the canonical 
4561             colormap range [0, 1] for mapping to colors. By default, the data 
4562             range is mapped to the colorbar range using linear scaling. 
4563  
4564         vmin, vmax : float, default: None 
4565             The colorbar range. If *None*, suitable min/max values are 
4566             automatically chosen by the `~.Normalize` instance (defaults to 
4567             the respective min/max values of the bins in case of the default 
4568             linear scaling). This is ignored if *norm* is given. 
4569  
4570         alpha : float between 0 and 1, optional 
4571             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
4572  
4573         linewidths : float, default: *None* 
4574             If *None*, defaults to 1.0. 
4575  
4576         edgecolors : {'face', 'none', *None*} or color, default: 'face' 
4577             The color of the hexagon edges. Possible values are: 
4578  
4579             - 'face': Draw the edges in the same color as the fill color. 
4580             - 'none': No edges are drawn. This can sometimes lead to unsightly 
4581               unpainted pixels between the hexagons. 
4582             - *None*: Draw outlines in the default color. 
4583             - An explicit color. 
4584  
4585         reduce_C_function : callable, default: `numpy.mean` 
4586             The function to aggregate *C* within the bins. It is ignored if 
4587             *C* is not given. This must have the signature:: 
4588  
4589                 def reduce_C_function(C: array) -> float 
4590  
4591             Commonly used functions are: 
4592  
4593             - `numpy.mean`: average of the points 
4594             - `numpy.sum`: integral of the point values 
4595             - `numpy.max`: value taken from the largest point 
4596  
4597         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.collections.PolyCollection` properties 
4598             All other keyword arguments are passed on to `.PolyCollection`: 
4599  
4600             %(PolyCollection)s 
4601  
4602         Returns 
4603         ------- 
4604         polycollection : `~matplotlib.collections.PolyCollection` 
4605             A `.PolyCollection` defining the hexagonal bins. 
4606  
4607             - `.PolyCollection.get_offset` contains a Mx2 array containing 
4608               the x, y positions of the M hexagon centers. 
4609             - `.PolyCollection.get_array` contains the values of the M 
4610               hexagons. 
4611  
4612             If *marginals* is *True*, horizontal 
4613             bar and vertical bar (both PolyCollections) will be attached 
4614             to the return collection as attributes *hbar* and *vbar*. 
4615  
4616         """ 
4617         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
4618  
4619         x, y, C = cbook.delete_masked_points(x, y, C) 
4620  
4621         # Set the size of the hexagon grid 
4622         if np.iterable(gridsize): 
4623             nx, ny = gridsize 
4624         else: 
4625             nx = gridsize 
4626             ny = int(nx / math.sqrt(3)) 
4627         # Count the number of data in each hexagon 
4628         x = np.array(x, float) 
4629         y = np.array(y, float) 
4630         if xscale == 'log': 
4631             if np.any(x <= 0.0): 
4632                 raise ValueError("x contains non-positive values, so can not" 
4633                                  " be log-scaled") 
4634             x = np.log10(x) 
4635         if yscale == 'log': 
4636             if np.any(y <= 0.0): 
4637                 raise ValueError("y contains non-positive values, so can not" 
4638                                  " be log-scaled") 
4639             y = np.log10(y) 
4640         if extent is not None: 
4641             xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax = extent 
4642         else: 
4643             xmin, xmax = (np.min(x), np.max(x)) if len(x) else (0, 1) 
4644             ymin, ymax = (np.min(y), np.max(y)) if len(y) else (0, 1) 
4645  
4646             # to avoid issues with singular data, expand the min/max pairs 
4647             xmin, xmax = mtransforms.nonsingular(xmin, xmax, expander=0.1) 
4648             ymin, ymax = mtransforms.nonsingular(ymin, ymax, expander=0.1) 
4649  
4650         # In the x-direction, the hexagons exactly cover the region from 
4651         # xmin to xmax. Need some padding to avoid roundoff errors. 
4652         padding = 1.e-9 * (xmax - xmin) 
4653         xmin -= padding 
4654         xmax += padding 
4655         sx = (xmax - xmin) / nx 
4656         sy = (ymax - ymin) / ny 
4657  
4658         if marginals: 
4659             xorig = x.copy() 
4660             yorig = y.copy() 
4661  
4662         x = (x - xmin) / sx 
4663         y = (y - ymin) / sy 
4664         ix1 = np.round(x).astype(int) 
4665         iy1 = np.round(y).astype(int) 
4666         ix2 = np.floor(x).astype(int) 
4667         iy2 = np.floor(y).astype(int) 
4668  
4669         nx1 = nx + 1 
4670         ny1 = ny + 1 
4671         nx2 = nx 
4672         ny2 = ny 
4673         n = nx1 * ny1 + nx2 * ny2 
4674  
4675         d1 = (x - ix1) ** 2 + 3.0 * (y - iy1) ** 2 
4676         d2 = (x - ix2 - 0.5) ** 2 + 3.0 * (y - iy2 - 0.5) ** 2 
4677         bdist = (d1 < d2) 
4678         if C is None: 
4679             lattice1 = np.zeros((nx1, ny1)) 
4680             lattice2 = np.zeros((nx2, ny2)) 
4681             c1 = (0 <= ix1) & (ix1 < nx1) & (0 <= iy1) & (iy1 < ny1) & bdist 
4682             c2 = (0 <= ix2) & (ix2 < nx2) & (0 <= iy2) & (iy2 < ny2) & ~bdist 
4683             np.add.at(lattice1, (ix1[c1], iy1[c1]), 1) 
4684             np.add.at(lattice2, (ix2[c2], iy2[c2]), 1) 
4685             if mincnt is not None: 
4686                 lattice1[lattice1 < mincnt] = np.nan 
4687                 lattice2[lattice2 < mincnt] = np.nan 
4688             accum = np.concatenate([lattice1.ravel(), lattice2.ravel()]) 
4689             good_idxs = ~np.isnan(accum) 
4690  
4691         else: 
4692             if mincnt is None: 
4693                 mincnt = 0 
4694  
4695             # create accumulation arrays 
4696             lattice1 = np.empty((nx1, ny1), dtype=object) 
4697             for i in range(nx1): 
4698                 for j in range(ny1): 
4699                     lattice1[i, j] = [] 
4700             lattice2 = np.empty((nx2, ny2), dtype=object) 
4701             for i in range(nx2): 
4702                 for j in range(ny2): 
4703                     lattice2[i, j] = [] 
4704  
4705             for i in range(len(x)): 
4706                 if bdist[i]: 
4707                     if 0 <= ix1[i] < nx1 and 0 <= iy1[i] < ny1: 
4708                         lattice1[ix1[i], iy1[i]].append(C[i]) 
4709                 else: 
4710                     if 0 <= ix2[i] < nx2 and 0 <= iy2[i] < ny2: 
4711                         lattice2[ix2[i], iy2[i]].append(C[i]) 
4712  
4713             for i in range(nx1): 
4714                 for j in range(ny1): 
4715                     vals = lattice1[i, j] 
4716                     if len(vals) > mincnt: 
4717                         lattice1[i, j] = reduce_C_function(vals) 
4718                     else: 
4719                         lattice1[i, j] = np.nan 
4720             for i in range(nx2): 
4721                 for j in range(ny2): 
4722                     vals = lattice2[i, j] 
4723                     if len(vals) > mincnt: 
4724                         lattice2[i, j] = reduce_C_function(vals) 
4725                     else: 
4726                         lattice2[i, j] = np.nan 
4727  
4728             accum = np.hstack((lattice1.astype(float).ravel(), 
4729                                lattice2.astype(float).ravel())) 
4730             good_idxs = ~np.isnan(accum) 
4731  
4732         offsets = np.zeros((n, 2), float) 
4733         offsets[:nx1 * ny1, 0] = np.repeat(np.arange(nx1), ny1) 
4734         offsets[:nx1 * ny1, 1] = np.tile(np.arange(ny1), nx1) 
4735         offsets[nx1 * ny1:, 0] = np.repeat(np.arange(nx2) + 0.5, ny2) 
4736         offsets[nx1 * ny1:, 1] = np.tile(np.arange(ny2), nx2) + 0.5 
4737         offsets[:, 0] *= sx 
4738         offsets[:, 1] *= sy 
4739         offsets[:, 0] += xmin 
4740         offsets[:, 1] += ymin 
4741         # remove accumulation bins with no data 
4742         offsets = offsets[good_idxs, :] 
4743         accum = accum[good_idxs] 
4744  
4745         polygon = [sx, sy / 3] * np.array( 
4746             [[.5, -.5], [.5, .5], [0., 1.], [-.5, .5], [-.5, -.5], [0., -1.]]) 
4747  
4748         if linewidths is None: 
4749             linewidths = [1.0] 
4750  
4751         if xscale == 'log' or yscale == 'log': 
4752             polygons = np.expand_dims(polygon, 0) + np.expand_dims(offsets, 1) 
4753             if xscale == 'log': 
4754                 polygons[:, :, 0] = 10.0 ** polygons[:, :, 0] 
4755                 xmin = 10.0 ** xmin 
4756                 xmax = 10.0 ** xmax 
4757                 self.set_xscale(xscale) 
4758             if yscale == 'log': 
4759                 polygons[:, :, 1] = 10.0 ** polygons[:, :, 1] 
4760                 ymin = 10.0 ** ymin 
4761                 ymax = 10.0 ** ymax 
4762                 self.set_yscale(yscale) 
4763             collection = mcoll.PolyCollection( 
4764                 polygons, 
4765                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4766                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4767                 ) 
4768         else: 
4769             collection = mcoll.PolyCollection( 
4770                 [polygon], 
4771                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4772                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4773                 offsets=offsets, 
4774                 transOffset=mtransforms.IdentityTransform(), 
4775                 offset_position="data" 
4776                 ) 
4777  
4778         # Set normalizer if bins is 'log' 
4779         if bins == 'log': 
4780             if norm is not None: 
4781                 cbook._warn_external("Only one of 'bins' and 'norm' " 
4782                                      "arguments can be supplied, ignoring " 
4783                                      "bins={}".format(bins)) 
4784             else: 
4785                 norm = mcolors.LogNorm() 
4786             bins = None 
4787  
4788         if isinstance(norm, mcolors.LogNorm): 
4789             if (accum == 0).any(): 
4790                 # make sure we have no zeros 
4791                 accum += 1 
4792  
4793         # autoscale the norm with curren accum values if it hasn't 
4794         # been set 
4795         if norm is not None: 
4796             if norm.vmin is None and norm.vmax is None: 
4797                 norm.autoscale(accum) 
4798  
4799         if bins is not None: 
4800             if not np.iterable(bins): 
4801                 minimum, maximum = min(accum), max(accum) 
4802                 bins -= 1  # one less edge than bins 
4803                 bins = minimum + (maximum - minimum) * np.arange(bins) / bins 
4804             bins = np.sort(bins) 
4805             accum = bins.searchsorted(accum) 
4806  
4807         collection.set_array(accum) 
4808         collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
4809         collection.set_norm(norm) 
4810         collection.set_alpha(alpha) 
4811         collection.update(kwargs) 
4812  
4813         if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
4814             collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
4815         else: 
4816             collection.autoscale_None() 
4817  
4818         corners = ((xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymax)) 
4819         self.update_datalim(corners) 
4820         self._request_autoscale_view(tight=True) 
4821  
4822         # add the collection last 
4823         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
4824         if not marginals: 
4825             return collection 
4826  
4827         if C is None: 
4828             C = np.ones(len(x)) 
4829  
4830         def coarse_bin(x, y, coarse): 
4831             ind = coarse.searchsorted(x).clip(0, len(coarse) - 1) 
4832             mus = np.zeros(len(coarse)) 
4833             for i in range(len(coarse)): 
4834                 yi = y[ind == i] 
4835                 if len(yi) > 0: 
4836                     mu = reduce_C_function(yi) 
4837                 else: 
4838                     mu = np.nan 
4839                 mus[i] = mu 
4840             return mus 
4841  
4842         coarse = np.linspace(xmin, xmax, gridsize) 
4843  
4844         xcoarse = coarse_bin(xorig, C, coarse) 
4845         valid = ~np.isnan(xcoarse) 
4846         verts, values = [], [] 
4847         for i, val in enumerate(xcoarse): 
4848             thismin = coarse[i] 
4849             if i < len(coarse) - 1: 
4850                 thismax = coarse[i + 1] 
4851             else: 
4852                 thismax = thismin + np.diff(coarse)[-1] 
4853  
4854             if not valid[i]: 
4855                 continue 
4856  
4857             verts.append([(thismin, 0), 
4858                           (thismin, 0.05), 
4859                           (thismax, 0.05), 
4860                           (thismax, 0)]) 
4861             values.append(val) 
4862  
4863         values = np.array(values) 
4864         trans = self.get_xaxis_transform(which='grid') 
4865  
4866         hbar = mcoll.PolyCollection(verts, transform=trans, edgecolors='face') 
4867  
4868         hbar.set_array(values) 
4869         hbar.set_cmap(cmap) 
4870         hbar.set_norm(norm) 
4871         hbar.set_alpha(alpha) 
4872         hbar.update(kwargs) 
4873         self.add_collection(hbar, autolim=False) 
4874  
4875         coarse = np.linspace(ymin, ymax, gridsize) 
4876         ycoarse = coarse_bin(yorig, C, coarse) 
4877         valid = ~np.isnan(ycoarse) 
4878         verts, values = [], [] 
4879         for i, val in enumerate(ycoarse): 
4880             thismin = coarse[i] 
4881             if i < len(coarse) - 1: 
4882                 thismax = coarse[i + 1] 
4883             else: 
4884                 thismax = thismin + np.diff(coarse)[-1] 
4885             if not valid[i]: 
4886                 continue 
4887             verts.append([(0, thismin), (0.0, thismax), 
4888                           (0.05, thismax), (0.05, thismin)]) 
4889             values.append(val) 
4890  
4891         values = np.array(values) 
4892  
4893         trans = self.get_yaxis_transform(which='grid') 
4894  
4895         vbar = mcoll.PolyCollection(verts, transform=trans, edgecolors='face') 
4896         vbar.set_array(values) 
4897         vbar.set_cmap(cmap) 
4898         vbar.set_norm(norm) 
4899         vbar.set_alpha(alpha) 
4900         vbar.update(kwargs) 
4901         self.add_collection(vbar, autolim=False) 
4902  
4903         collection.hbar = hbar 
4904         collection.vbar = vbar 
4905  
4906         def on_changed(collection): 
4907             hbar.set_cmap(collection.get_cmap()) 
4908             hbar.set_clim(collection.get_clim()) 
4909             vbar.set_cmap(collection.get_cmap()) 
4910             vbar.set_clim(collection.get_clim()) 
4911  
4912         collection.callbacksSM.connect('changed', on_changed) 
4913  
4914         return collection

5004     # Uses a custom implementation of data-kwarg handling in 
5005     # _process_plot_var_args. 
5006     def fill(self, *args, data=None, **kwargs): 
5007         """ 
5008         Plot filled polygons. 
5009  
5010         Parameters 
5011         ---------- 
5012         *args : sequence of x, y, [color] 
5013             Each polygon is defined by the lists of *x* and *y* positions of 
5014             its nodes, optionally followed by a *color* specifier. See 
5015             :mod:`matplotlib.colors` for supported color specifiers. The 
5016             standard color cycle is used for polygons without a color 
5017             specifier. 
5018  
5019             You can plot multiple polygons by providing multiple *x*, *y*, 
5020             *[color]* groups. 
5021  
5022             For example, each of the following is legal:: 
5023  
5024                 ax.fill(x, y)                    # a polygon with default color 
5025                 ax.fill(x, y, "b")               # a blue polygon 
5026                 ax.fill(x, y, x2, y2)            # two polygons 
5027                 ax.fill(x, y, "b", x2, y2, "r")  # a blue and a red polygon 
5028  
5029         data : indexable object, optional 
5030             An object with labelled data. If given, provide the label names to 
5031             plot in *x* and *y*, e.g.:: 
5032  
5033                 ax.fill("time", "signal", 
5034                         data={"time": [0, 1, 2], "signal": [0, 1, 0]}) 
5035  
5036         Returns 
5037         ------- 
5038         a list of :class:`~matplotlib.patches.Polygon` 
5039  
5040         Other Parameters 
5041         ---------------- 
5042         **kwargs : :class:`~matplotlib.patches.Polygon` properties 
5043  
5044         Notes 
5045         ----- 
5046         Use :meth:`fill_between` if you would like to fill the region between 
5047         two curves. 
5048         """ 
5049         # For compatibility(!), get aliases from Line2D rather than Patch. 
5050         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D) 
5051         # _get_patches_for_fill returns a generator, convert it to a list. 
5052         patches = [*self._get_patches_for_fill(*args, data=data, **kwargs)] 
5053         for poly in patches: 
5054             self.add_patch(poly) 
5055         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5056         return patches

5058     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y1", "y2", "where"]) 
5059     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
5060     def fill_between(self, x, y1, y2=0, where=None, interpolate=False, 
5061                      step=None, **kwargs): 
5062         """ 
5063         Fill the area between two horizontal curves. 
5064  
5065         The curves are defined by the points (*x*, *y1*) and (*x*, *y2*). This 
5066         creates one or multiple polygons describing the filled area. 
5067  
5068         You may exclude some horizontal sections from filling using *where*. 
5069  
5070         By default, the edges connect the given points directly. Use *step* if 
5071         the filling should be a step function, i.e. constant in between *x*. 
5072  
5073  
5074         Parameters 
5075         ---------- 
5076         x : array (length N) 
5077             The x coordinates of the nodes defining the curves. 
5078  
5079         y1 : array (length N) or scalar 
5080             The y coordinates of the nodes defining the first curve. 
5081  
5082         y2 : array (length N) or scalar, default: 0 
5083             The y coordinates of the nodes defining the second curve. 
5084  
5085         where : array of bool (length N), optional 
5086             Define *where* to exclude some horizontal regions from being 
5087             filled. The filled regions are defined by the coordinates 
5088             ``x[where]``.  More precisely, fill between ``x[i]`` and ``x[i+1]`` 
5089             if ``where[i] and where[i+1]``.  Note that this definition implies 
5090             that an isolated *True* value between two *False* values in 
5091             *where* will not result in filling.  Both sides of the *True* 
5092             position remain unfilled due to the adjacent *False* values. 
5093  
5094         interpolate : bool, default: False 
5095             This option is only relevant if *where* is used and the two curves 
5096             are crossing each other. 
5097  
5098             Semantically, *where* is often used for *y1* > *y2* or similar. 
5099             By default, the nodes of the polygon defining the filled region 
5100             will only be placed at the positions in the *x* array.  Such a 
5101             polygon cannot describe the above semantics close to the 
5102             intersection.  The x-sections containing the intersection are 
5103             simply clipped. 
5104  
5105             Setting *interpolate* to *True* will calculate the actual 
5106             intersection point and extend the filled region up to this point. 
5107  
5108         step : {'pre', 'post', 'mid'}, optional 
5109             Define *step* if the filling should be a step function, 
5110             i.e. constant in between *x*. The value determines where the 
5111             step will occur: 
5112  
5113             - 'pre': The y value is continued constantly to the left from 
5114               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``(x[i-1], x[i]]`` has the 
5115               value ``y[i]``. 
5116             - 'post': The y value is continued constantly to the right from 
5117               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``[x[i], x[i+1])`` has the 
5118               value ``y[i]``. 
5119             - 'mid': Steps occur half-way between the *x* positions. 
5120  
5121         Other Parameters 
5122         ---------------- 
5123         **kwargs 
5124             All other keyword arguments are passed on to `.PolyCollection`. 
5125             They control the `.Polygon` properties: 
5126  
5127             %(PolyCollection)s 
5128  
5129         Returns 
5130         ------- 
5131         `.PolyCollection` 
5132             A `.PolyCollection` containing the plotted polygons. 
5133  
5134         See Also 
5135         -------- 
5136         fill_betweenx : Fill between two sets of x-values. 
5137  
5138         Notes 
5139         ----- 
5140         .. [notes section required to get data note injection right] 
5141  
5142         """ 
5143         if not rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
5144             kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mcoll.Collection) 
5145             if not any(c in kwargs for c in ('color', 'facecolor')): 
5146                 kwargs['facecolor'] = \ 
5147                     self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color() 
5148  
5149         # Handle united data, such as dates 
5150         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y1, kwargs=kwargs) 
5151         self._process_unit_info(ydata=y2) 
5152  
5153         # Convert the arrays so we can work with them 
5154         x = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_xunits(x)) 
5155         y1 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_yunits(y1)) 
5156         y2 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_yunits(y2)) 
5157  
5158         for name, array in [('x', x), ('y1', y1), ('y2', y2)]: 
5159             if array.ndim > 1: 
5160                 raise ValueError('Input passed into argument "%r"' % name + 
5161                                  'is not 1-dimensional.') 
5162  
5163         if where is None: 
5164             where = True 
5165         else: 
5166             where = np.asarray(where, dtype=bool) 
5167             if where.size != x.size: 
5168                 cbook.warn_deprecated( 
5169                     "3.2", 
5170                     message="The parameter where must have the same size as x " 
5171                             "in fill_between(). This will become an error in " 
5172                             "future versions of Matplotlib.") 
5173         where = where & ~functools.reduce(np.logical_or, 
5174                                           map(np.ma.getmask, [x, y1, y2])) 
5175  
5176         x, y1, y2 = np.broadcast_arrays(np.atleast_1d(x), y1, y2) 
5177  
5178         polys = [] 
5179         for ind0, ind1 in cbook.contiguous_regions(where): 
5180             xslice = x[ind0:ind1] 
5181             y1slice = y1[ind0:ind1] 
5182             y2slice = y2[ind0:ind1] 
5183             if step is not None: 
5184                 step_func = cbook.STEP_LOOKUP_MAP["steps-" + step] 
5185                 xslice, y1slice, y2slice = step_func(xslice, y1slice, y2slice) 
5186  
5187             if not len(xslice): 
5188                 continue 
5189  
5190             N = len(xslice) 
5191             X = np.zeros((2 * N + 2, 2), float) 
5192  
5193             if interpolate: 
5194                 def get_interp_point(ind): 
5195                     im1 = max(ind - 1, 0) 
5196                     x_values = x[im1:ind + 1] 
5197                     diff_values = y1[im1:ind + 1] - y2[im1:ind + 1] 
5198                     y1_values = y1[im1:ind + 1] 
5199  
5200                     if len(diff_values) == 2: 
5201                         if np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[1]): 
5202                             return x[im1], y1[im1] 
5203                         elif np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[0]): 
5204                             return x[ind], y1[ind] 
5205  
5206                     diff_order = diff_values.argsort() 
5207                     diff_root_x = np.interp( 
5208                         0, diff_values[diff_order], x_values[diff_order]) 
5209                     x_order = x_values.argsort() 
5210                     diff_root_y = np.interp(diff_root_x, x_values[x_order], 
5211                                             y1_values[x_order]) 
5212                     return diff_root_x, diff_root_y 
5213  
5214                 start = get_interp_point(ind0) 
5215                 end = get_interp_point(ind1) 
5216             else: 
5217                 # the purpose of the next two lines is for when y2 is a 
5218                 # scalar like 0 and we want the fill to go all the way 
5219                 # down to 0 even if none of the y1 sample points do 
5220                 start = xslice[0], y2slice[0] 
5221                 end = xslice[-1], y2slice[-1] 
5222  
5223             X[0] = start 
5224             X[N + 1] = end 
5225  
5226             X[1:N + 1, 0] = xslice 
5227             X[1:N + 1, 1] = y1slice 
5228             X[N + 2:, 0] = xslice[::-1] 
5229             X[N + 2:, 1] = y2slice[::-1] 
5230  
5231             polys.append(X) 
5232  
5233         collection = mcoll.PolyCollection(polys, **kwargs) 
5234  
5235         # now update the datalim and autoscale 
5236         XY1 = np.array([x[where], y1[where]]).T 
5237         XY2 = np.array([x[where], y2[where]]).T 
5238         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(XY1, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5239                                          updatex=True, updatey=True) 
5240         self.ignore_existing_data_limits = False 
5241         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(XY2, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5242                                          updatex=False, updatey=True) 
5243         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
5244         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5245         return collection
