1223     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["positions", "lineoffsets", 
1224                                      "linelengths", "linewidths", 
1225                                      "colors", "linestyles"]) 
1226     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
1227     def eventplot(self, positions, orientation='horizontal', lineoffsets=1, 
1228                   linelengths=1, linewidths=None, colors=None, 
1229                   linestyles='solid', **kwargs): 
1230         """ 
1231         Plot identical parallel lines at the given positions. 
1232  
1233         *positions* should be a 1D or 2D array-like object, with each row 
1234         corresponding to a row or column of lines. 
1235  
1236         This type of plot is commonly used in neuroscience for representing 
1237         neural events, where it is usually called a spike raster, dot raster, 
1238         or raster plot. 
1239  
1240         However, it is useful in any situation where you wish to show the 
1241         timing or position of multiple sets of discrete events, such as the 
1242         arrival times of people to a business on each day of the month or the 
1243         date of hurricanes each year of the last century. 
1244  
1245         Parameters 
1246         ---------- 
1247         positions : 1D or 2D array-like object 
1248             Each value is an event. If *positions* is a 2D array-like, each 
1249             row corresponds to a row or a column of lines (depending on the 
1250             *orientation* parameter). 
1251  
1252         orientation : {'horizontal', 'vertical'}, optional 
1253             The direction of the event collections: 
1254  
1255             - 'horizontal': the lines are arranged horizontally in rows, 
1256               and are vertical. 
1257             - 'vertical': the lines are arranged vertically in columns, 
1258               and are horizontal. 
1259  
1260         lineoffsets : scalar or sequence of scalars, default: 1 
1261             The offset of the center of the lines from the origin, in the 
1262             direction orthogonal to *orientation*. 
1263  
1264         linelengths : scalar or sequence of scalars, default: 1 
1265             The total height of the lines (i.e. the lines stretches from 
1266             ``lineoffset - linelength/2`` to ``lineoffset + linelength/2``). 
1267  
1268         linewidths : scalar, scalar sequence or None, default: None 
1269             The line width(s) of the event lines, in points. If it is None, 
1270             defaults to its rcParams setting. 
1271  
1272         colors : color, sequence of colors or None, default: None 
1273             The color(s) of the event lines. If it is None, defaults to its 
1274             rcParams setting. 
1275  
1276         linestyles : str or tuple or a sequence of such values, optional 
1277             Default is 'solid'. Valid strings are ['solid', 'dashed', 
1278             'dashdot', 'dotted', '-', '--', '-.', ':']. Dash tuples 
1279             should be of the form:: 
1280  
1281                 (offset, onoffseq), 
1282  
1283             where *onoffseq* is an even length tuple of on and off ink 
1284             in points. 
1285  
1286         **kwargs : optional 
1287             Other keyword arguments are line collection properties.  See 
1288             :class:`~matplotlib.collections.LineCollection` for a list of 
1289             the valid properties. 
1290  
1291         Returns 
1292         ------- 
1293         list : A list of :class:`~.collections.EventCollection` objects. 
1294             Contains the :class:`~.collections.EventCollection` that 
1295             were added. 
1296  
1297         Notes 
1298         ----- 
1299         For *linelengths*, *linewidths*, *colors*, and *linestyles*, if only 
1300         a single value is given, that value is applied to all lines.  If an 
1301         array-like is given, it must have the same length as *positions*, and 
1302         each value will be applied to the corresponding row of the array. 
1303  
1304         Examples 
1305         -------- 
1306         .. plot:: gallery/lines_bars_and_markers/eventplot_demo.py 
1307         """ 
1308         self._process_unit_info(xdata=positions, 
1309                                 ydata=[lineoffsets, linelengths], 
1310                                 kwargs=kwargs) 
1311  
1312         # We do the conversion first since not all unitized data is uniform 
1313         positions = self.convert_xunits(positions) 
1314         lineoffsets = self.convert_yunits(lineoffsets) 
1315         linelengths = self.convert_yunits(linelengths) 
1316  
1317         if not np.iterable(positions): 
1318             positions = [positions] 
1319         elif any(np.iterable(position) for position in positions): 
1320             positions = [np.asanyarray(position) for position in positions] 
1321         else: 
1322             positions = [np.asanyarray(positions)] 
1323  
1324         if len(positions) == 0: 
1325             return [] 
1326  
1327         # prevent 'singular' keys from **kwargs dict from overriding the effect 
1328         # of 'plural' keyword arguments (e.g. 'color' overriding 'colors') 
1329         colors = cbook.local_over_kwdict(colors, kwargs, 'color') 
1330         linewidths = cbook.local_over_kwdict(linewidths, kwargs, 'linewidth') 
1331         linestyles = cbook.local_over_kwdict(linestyles, kwargs, 'linestyle') 
1332  
1333         if not np.iterable(lineoffsets): 
1334             lineoffsets = [lineoffsets] 
1335         if not np.iterable(linelengths): 
1336             linelengths = [linelengths] 
1337         if not np.iterable(linewidths): 
1338             linewidths = [linewidths] 
1339         if not np.iterable(colors): 
1340             colors = [colors] 
1341         if hasattr(linestyles, 'lower') or not np.iterable(linestyles): 
1342             linestyles = [linestyles] 
1343  
1344         lineoffsets = np.asarray(lineoffsets) 
1345         linelengths = np.asarray(linelengths) 
1346         linewidths = np.asarray(linewidths) 
1347  
1348         if len(lineoffsets) == 0: 
1349             lineoffsets = [None] 
1350         if len(linelengths) == 0: 
1351             linelengths = [None] 
1352         if len(linewidths) == 0: 
1353             lineoffsets = [None] 
1354         if len(linewidths) == 0: 
1355             lineoffsets = [None] 
1356         if len(colors) == 0: 
1357             colors = [None] 
1358         try: 
1359             # Early conversion of the colors into RGBA values to take care 
1360             # of cases like colors='0.5' or colors='C1'.  (Issue #8193) 
1361             colors = mcolors.to_rgba_array(colors) 
1362         except ValueError: 
1363             # Will fail if any element of *colors* is None. But as long 
1364             # as len(colors) == 1 or len(positions), the rest of the 
1365             # code should process *colors* properly. 
1366             pass 
1367  
1368         if len(lineoffsets) == 1 and len(positions) != 1: 
1369             lineoffsets = np.tile(lineoffsets, len(positions)) 
1370             lineoffsets[0] = 0 
1371             lineoffsets = np.cumsum(lineoffsets) 
1372         if len(linelengths) == 1: 
1373             linelengths = np.tile(linelengths, len(positions)) 
1374         if len(linewidths) == 1: 
1375             linewidths = np.tile(linewidths, len(positions)) 
1376         if len(colors) == 1: 
1377             colors = list(colors) 
1378             colors = colors * len(positions) 
1379         if len(linestyles) == 1: 
1380             linestyles = [linestyles] * len(positions) 
1381  
1382         if len(lineoffsets) != len(positions): 
1383             raise ValueError('lineoffsets and positions are unequal sized ' 
1384                              'sequences') 
1385         if len(linelengths) != len(positions): 
1386             raise ValueError('linelengths and positions are unequal sized ' 
1387                              'sequences') 
1388         if len(linewidths) != len(positions): 
1389             raise ValueError('linewidths and positions are unequal sized ' 
1390                              'sequences') 
1391         if len(colors) != len(positions): 
1392             raise ValueError('colors and positions are unequal sized ' 
1393                              'sequences') 
1394         if len(linestyles) != len(positions): 
1395             raise ValueError('linestyles and positions are unequal sized ' 
1396                              'sequences') 
1397  
1398         colls = [] 
1399         for position, lineoffset, linelength, linewidth, color, linestyle in \ 
1400             zip(positions, lineoffsets, linelengths, linewidths, 
1401                            colors, linestyles): 
1402             coll = mcoll.EventCollection(position, 
1403                                          orientation=orientation, 
1404                                          lineoffset=lineoffset, 
1405                                          linelength=linelength, 
1406                                          linewidth=linewidth, 
1407                                          color=color, 
1408                                          linestyle=linestyle) 
1409             self.add_collection(coll, autolim=False) 
1410             coll.update(kwargs) 
1411             colls.append(coll) 
1412  
1413         if len(positions) > 0: 
1414             # try to get min/max 
1415             min_max = [(np.min(_p), np.max(_p)) for _p in positions 
1416                        if len(_p) > 0] 
1417             # if we have any non-empty positions, try to autoscale 
1418             if len(min_max) > 0: 
1419                 mins, maxes = zip(*min_max) 
1420                 minpos = np.min(mins) 
1421                 maxpos = np.max(maxes) 
1422  
1423                 minline = (lineoffsets - linelengths).min() 
1424                 maxline = (lineoffsets + linelengths).max() 
1425  
1426                 if (orientation is not None and 
1427                         orientation.lower() == "vertical"): 
1428                     corners = (minline, minpos), (maxline, maxpos) 
1429                 else:  # "horizontal", None or "none" (see EventCollection) 
1430                     corners = (minpos, minline), (maxpos, maxline) 
1431                 self.update_datalim(corners) 
1432                 self._request_autoscale_view() 
1433  
1434         return colls 
1435  
1436     #### Basic plotting 
1437  
1438     # Uses a custom implementation of data-kwarg handling in 
1439     # _process_plot_var_args. 
1440     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
1441     def plot(self, *args, scalex=True, scaley=True, data=None, **kwargs): 
1442         """ 
1443         Plot y versus x as lines and/or markers. 
1444  
1445         Call signatures:: 
1446  
1447             plot([x], y, [fmt], *, data=None, **kwargs) 
1448             plot([x], y, [fmt], [x2], y2, [fmt2], ..., **kwargs) 
1449  
1450         The coordinates of the points or line nodes are given by *x*, *y*. 
1451  
1452         The optional parameter *fmt* is a convenient way for defining basic 
1453         formatting like color, marker and linestyle. It's a shortcut string 
1454         notation described in the *Notes* section below. 
1455  
1456         >>> plot(x, y)        # plot x and y using default line style and color 
1457         >>> plot(x, y, 'bo')  # plot x and y using blue circle markers 
1458         >>> plot(y)           # plot y using x as index array 0..N-1 
1459         >>> plot(y, 'r+')     # ditto, but with red plusses 
1460  
1461         You can use `.Line2D` properties as keyword arguments for more 
1462         control on the appearance. Line properties and *fmt* can be mixed. 
1463         The following two calls yield identical results: 
1464  
1465         >>> plot(x, y, 'go--', linewidth=2, markersize=12) 
1466         >>> plot(x, y, color='green', marker='o', linestyle='dashed', 
1467         ...      linewidth=2, markersize=12) 
1468  
1469         When conflicting with *fmt*, keyword arguments take precedence. 
1470  
1471  
1472         **Plotting labelled data** 
1473  
1474         There's a convenient way for plotting objects with labelled data (i.e. 
1475         data that can be accessed by index ``obj['y']``). Instead of giving 
1476         the data in *x* and *y*, you can provide the object in the *data* 
1477         parameter and just give the labels for *x* and *y*:: 
1478  
1479         >>> plot('xlabel', 'ylabel', data=obj) 
1480  
1481         All indexable objects are supported. This could e.g. be a `dict`, a 
1482         `pandas.DataFame` or a structured numpy array. 
1483  
1484  
1485         **Plotting multiple sets of data** 
1486  
1487         There are various ways to plot multiple sets of data. 
1488  
1489         - The most straight forward way is just to call `plot` multiple times. 
1490           Example: 
1491  
1492           >>> plot(x1, y1, 'bo') 
1493           >>> plot(x2, y2, 'go') 
1494  
1495         - Alternatively, if your data is already a 2d array, you can pass it 
1496           directly to *x*, *y*. A separate data set will be drawn for every 
1497           column. 
1498  
1499           Example: an array ``a`` where the first column represents the *x* 
1500           values and the other columns are the *y* columns:: 
1501  
1502           >>> plot(a[0], a[1:]) 
1503  
1504         - The third way is to specify multiple sets of *[x]*, *y*, *[fmt]* 
1505           groups:: 
1506  
1507           >>> plot(x1, y1, 'g^', x2, y2, 'g-') 
1508  
1509           In this case, any additional keyword argument applies to all 
1510           datasets. Also this syntax cannot be combined with the *data* 
1511           parameter. 
1512  
1513         By default, each line is assigned a different style specified by a 
1514         'style cycle'. The *fmt* and line property parameters are only 
1515         necessary if you want explicit deviations from these defaults. 
1516         Alternatively, you can also change the style cycle using 
1517         :rc:`axes.prop_cycle`. 
1518  
1519  
1520         Parameters 
1521         ---------- 
1522         x, y : array-like or scalar 
1523             The horizontal / vertical coordinates of the data points. 
1524             *x* values are optional and default to ``range(len(y))``. 
1525  
1526             Commonly, these parameters are 1D arrays. 
1527  
1528             They can also be scalars, or two-dimensional (in that case, the 
1529             columns represent separate data sets). 
1530  
1531             These arguments cannot be passed as keywords. 
1532  
1533         fmt : str, optional 
1534             A format string, e.g. 'ro' for red circles. See the *Notes* 
1535             section for a full description of the format strings. 
1536  
1537             Format strings are just an abbreviation for quickly setting 
1538             basic line properties. All of these and more can also be 
1539             controlled by keyword arguments. 
1540  
1541             This argument cannot be passed as keyword. 
1542  
1543         data : indexable object, optional 
1544             An object with labelled data. If given, provide the label names to 
1545             plot in *x* and *y*. 
1546  
1547             .. note:: 
1548                 Technically there's a slight ambiguity in calls where the 
1549                 second label is a valid *fmt*. ``plot('n', 'o', data=obj)`` 
1550                 could be ``plt(x, y)`` or ``plt(y, fmt)``. In such cases, 
1551                 the former interpretation is chosen, but a warning is issued. 
1552                 You may suppress the warning by adding an empty format string 
1553                 ``plot('n', 'o', '', data=obj)``. 
1554  
1555         Other Parameters 
1556         ---------------- 
1557         scalex, scaley : bool, default: True 
1558             These parameters determined if the view limits are adapted to 
1559             the data limits. The values are passed on to `autoscale_view`. 
1560  
1561         **kwargs : `.Line2D` properties, optional 
1562             *kwargs* are used to specify properties like a line label (for 
1563             auto legends), linewidth, antialiasing, marker face color. 
1564             Example:: 
1565  
1566             >>> plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3], 'go-', label='line 1', linewidth=2) 
1567             >>> plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 4, 9], 'rs', label='line 2') 
1568  
1569             If you make multiple lines with one plot command, the kwargs 
1570             apply to all those lines. 
1571  
1572             Here is a list of available `.Line2D` properties: 
1573  
1574             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
1575  
1576         Returns 
1577         ------- 
1578         lines 
1579             A list of `.Line2D` objects representing the plotted data. 
1580  
1581         See Also 
1582         -------- 
1583         scatter : XY scatter plot with markers of varying size and/or color ( 
1584             sometimes also called bubble chart). 
1585  
1586         Notes 
1587         ----- 
1588         **Format Strings** 
1589  
1590         A format string consists of a part for color, marker and line:: 
1591  
1592             fmt = '[marker][line][color]' 
1593  
1594         Each of them is optional. If not provided, the value from the style 
1595         cycle is used. Exception: If ``line`` is given, but no ``marker``, 
1596         the data will be a line without markers. 
1597  
1598         Other combinations such as ``[color][marker][line]`` are also 
1599         supported, but note that their parsing may be ambiguous. 
1600  
1601         **Markers** 
1602  
1603         =============    =============================== 
1604         character        description 
1605         =============    =============================== 
1606         ``'.'``          point marker 
1607         ``','``          pixel marker 
1608         ``'o'``          circle marker 
1609         ``'v'``          triangle_down marker 
1610         ``'^'``          triangle_up marker 
1611         ``'<'``          triangle_left marker 
1612         ``'>'``          triangle_right marker 
1613         ``'1'``          tri_down marker 
1614         ``'2'``          tri_up marker 
1615         ``'3'``          tri_left marker 
1616         ``'4'``          tri_right marker 
1617         ``'s'``          square marker 
1618         ``'p'``          pentagon marker 
1619         ``'*'``          star marker 
1620         ``'h'``          hexagon1 marker 
1621         ``'H'``          hexagon2 marker 
1622         ``'+'``          plus marker 
1623         ``'x'``          x marker 
1624         ``'D'``          diamond marker 
1625         ``'d'``          thin_diamond marker 
1626         ``'|'``          vline marker 
1627         ``'_'``          hline marker 
1628         =============    =============================== 
1629  
1630         **Line Styles** 
1631  
1632         =============    =============================== 
1633         character        description 
1634         =============    =============================== 
1635         ``'-'``          solid line style 
1636         ``'--'``         dashed line style 
1637         ``'-.'``         dash-dot line style 
1638         ``':'``          dotted line style 
1639         =============    =============================== 
1640  
1641         Example format strings:: 
1642  
1643             'b'    # blue markers with default shape 
1644             'or'   # red circles 
1645             '-g'   # green solid line 
1646             '--'   # dashed line with default color 
1647             '^k:'  # black triangle_up markers connected by a dotted line 
1648  
1649         **Colors** 
1650  
1651         The supported color abbreviations are the single letter codes 
1652  
1653         =============    =============================== 
1654         character        color 
1655         =============    =============================== 
1656         ``'b'``          blue 
1657         ``'g'``          green 
1658         ``'r'``          red 
1659         ``'c'``          cyan 
1660         ``'m'``          magenta 
1661         ``'y'``          yellow 
1662         ``'k'``          black 
1663         ``'w'``          white 
1664         =============    =============================== 
1665  
1666         and the ``'CN'`` colors that index into the default property cycle. 
1667  
1668         If the color is the only part of the format string, you can 
1669         additionally use any  `matplotlib.colors` spec, e.g. full names 
1670         (``'green'``) or hex strings (``'#008000'``). 
1671         """ 
1672         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D) 
1673         lines = [*self._get_lines(*args, data=data, **kwargs)] 
1674         for line in lines: 
1675             self.add_line(line) 
1676         self._request_autoscale_view(scalex=scalex, scaley=scaley) 
1677         return lines

1679     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y")

1681     def plot_date(self, x, y, fmt='o', tz=None, xdate=True, ydate=False, 
1682                   **kwargs): 
1683         """ 
1684         Plot data that contains dates. 
1685  
1686         Similar to `.plot`, this plots *y* vs. *x* as lines or markers. 
1687         However, the axis labels are formatted as dates depending on *xdate* 
1688         and *ydate*. 
1689  
1690         Parameters 
1691         ---------- 
1692         x, y : array-like 
1693             The coordinates of the data points. If *xdate* or *ydate* is 
1694             *True*, the respective values *x* or *y* are interpreted as 
1695             :ref:`Matplotlib dates <date-format>`. 
1696  
1697         fmt : str, optional 
1698             The plot format string. For details, see the corresponding 
1699             parameter in `.plot`. 
1700  
1701         tz : timezone string or `tzinfo` or None 
1702             The time zone to use in labeling dates. If *None*, defaults to 
1703             :rc:`timezone`. 
1704  
1705         xdate : bool, default: True 
1706             If *True*, the *x*-axis will be interpreted as Matplotlib dates. 
1707  
1708         ydate : bool, default: False 
1709             If *True*, the *y*-axis will be interpreted as Matplotlib dates. 
1710  
1711  
1712         Returns 
1713         ------- 
1714         lines 
1715             A list of `.Line2D` objects representing the plotted data. 
1716  
1717  
1718         Other Parameters 
1719         ---------------- 
1720         **kwargs 
1721             Keyword arguments control the `.Line2D` properties: 
1722  
1723             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
1724  
1725         See Also 
1726         -------- 
1727         matplotlib.dates : Helper functions on dates. 
1728         matplotlib.dates.date2num : Convert dates to num. 
1729         matplotlib.dates.num2date : Convert num to dates. 
1730         matplotlib.dates.drange : Create an equally spaced sequence of dates. 
1731  
1732         Notes 
1733         ----- 
1734         If you are using custom date tickers and formatters, it may be 
1735         necessary to set the formatters/locators after the call to 
1736         `.plot_date`. `.plot_date` will set the default tick locator to 
1737         `.AutoDateLocator` (if the tick locator is not already set to a 
1738         `.DateLocator` instance) and the default tick formatter to 
1739         `.AutoDateFormatter` (if the tick formatter is not already set to a 
1740         `.DateFormatter` instance). 
1741         """ 
1742         if xdate: 
1743             self.xaxis_date(tz) 
1744         if ydate: 
1745             self.yaxis_date(tz) 
1746  
1747         ret = self.plot(x, y, fmt, **kwargs) 
1748  
1749         self._request_autoscale_view() 
1750  
1751         return ret

1753     # @_preprocess_data() # let 'plot' do the unpacking.. 
1754     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
1755     def loglog(self, *args, **kwargs): 
1756         """ 
1757         Make a plot with log scaling on both the x and y axis. 
1758  
1759         Call signatures:: 
1760  
1761             loglog([x], y, [fmt], data=None, **kwargs) 
1762             loglog([x], y, [fmt], [x2], y2, [fmt2], ..., **kwargs) 
1763  
1764         This is just a thin wrapper around `.plot` which additionally changes 
1765         both the x-axis and the y-axis to log scaling. All of the concepts and 
1766         parameters of plot can be used here as well. 
1767  
1768         The additional parameters *basex/y*, *subsx/y* and *nonposx/y* control 
1769         the x/y-axis properties. They are just forwarded to `.Axes.set_xscale` 
1770         and `.Axes.set_yscale`. 
1771  
1772         Parameters 
1773         ---------- 
1774         basex, basey : scalar, optional, default 10 
1775             Base of the x/y logarithm. 
1776  
1777         subsx, subsy : sequence, optional 
1778             The location of the minor x/y ticks. If *None*, reasonable 
1779             locations are automatically chosen depending on the number of 
1780             decades in the plot. 
1781             See `.Axes.set_xscale` / `.Axes.set_yscale` for details. 
1782  
1783         nonposx, nonposy : {'mask', 'clip'}, optional, default 'mask' 
1784             Non-positive values in x or y can be masked as invalid, or clipped 
1785             to a very small positive number. 
1786  
1787         Returns 
1788         ------- 
1789         lines 
1790             A list of `.Line2D` objects representing the plotted data. 
1791  
1792         Other Parameters 
1793         ---------------- 
1794         **kwargs 
1795             All parameters supported by `.plot`. 
1796         """ 
1797         dx = {k: kwargs.pop(k) for k in ['basex', 'subsx', 'nonposx'] 
1798               if k in kwargs} 
1799         dy = {k: kwargs.pop(k) for k in ['basey', 'subsy', 'nonposy'] 
1800               if k in kwargs} 
1801  
1802         self.set_xscale('log', **dx) 
1803         self.set_yscale('log', **dy) 
1804  
1805         l = self.plot(*args, **kwargs) 
1806         return l

1906     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x"], label_namer="x") 
1907     def acorr(self, x, **kwargs): 
1908         """ 
1909         Plot the autocorrelation of *x*. 
1910  
1911         Parameters 
1912         ---------- 
1913         x : array-like 
1914  
1915         detrend : callable, default: `mlab.detrend_none` 
1916             *x* is detrended by the *detrend* callable. This must be a 
1917             function ``x = detrend(x)`` accepting and returning an 
1918             `numpy.array`. Default is no detrending. 
1919  
1920         normed : bool, default: True 
1921             If ``True``, input vectors are normalised to unit length. 
1922  
1923         usevlines : bool, default: True 
1924             Determines the plot style. 
1925  
1926             If ``True``, vertical lines are plotted from 0 to the acorr value 
1927             using `Axes.vlines`. Additionally, a horizontal line is plotted 
1928             at y=0 using `Axes.axhline`. 
1929  
1930             If ``False``, markers are plotted at the acorr values using 
1931             `Axes.plot`. 
1932  
1933         maxlags : int, default: 10 
1934             Number of lags to show. If ``None``, will return all 
1935             ``2 * len(x) - 1`` lags. 
1936  
1937         Returns 
1938         ------- 
1939         lags : array (length ``2*maxlags+1``) 
1940             The lag vector. 
1941         c : array  (length ``2*maxlags+1``) 
1942             The auto correlation vector. 
1943         line : `.LineCollection` or `.Line2D` 
1944             `.Artist` added to the axes of the correlation: 
1945  
1946             - `.LineCollection` if *usevlines* is True. 
1947             - `.Line2D` if *usevlines* is False. 
1948         b : `.Line2D` or None 
1949             Horizontal line at 0 if *usevlines* is True 
1950             None *usevlines* is False. 
1951  
1952         Other Parameters 
1953         ---------------- 
1954         linestyle : `.Line2D` property, optional 
1955             The linestyle for plotting the data points. 
1956             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``. 
1957  
1958         marker : str, default: 'o' 
1959             The marker for plotting the data points. 
1960             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``. 
1961  
1962         Notes 
1963         ----- 
1964         The cross correlation is performed with :func:`numpy.correlate` with 
1965         ``mode = "full"``. 
1966         """ 
1967         return self.xcorr(x, x, **kwargs) 
1968  
1969     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y") 
1970     def xcorr(self, x, y, normed=True, detrend=mlab.detrend_none, 
1971               usevlines=True, maxlags=10, **kwargs): 
1972         r""" 
1973         Plot the cross correlation between *x* and *y*. 
1974  
1975         The correlation with lag k is defined as 
1976         :math:`\sum_n x[n+k] \cdot y^*[n]`, where :math:`y^*` is the complex 
1977         conjugate of :math:`y`. 
1978  
1979         Parameters 
1980         ---------- 
1981         x : array-like of length n 
1982  
1983         y : array-like of length n 
1984  
1985         detrend : callable, default: `mlab.detrend_none` 
1986             *x* and *y* are detrended by the *detrend* callable. This must be a 
1987             function ``x = detrend(x)`` accepting and returning an 
1988             `numpy.array`. Default is no detrending. 
1989  
1990         normed : bool, default: True 
1991             If ``True``, input vectors are normalised to unit length. 
1992  
1993         usevlines : bool, default: True 
1994             Determines the plot style. 
1995  
1996             If ``True``, vertical lines are plotted from 0 to the xcorr value 
1997             using `Axes.vlines`. Additionally, a horizontal line is plotted 
1998             at y=0 using `Axes.axhline`. 
1999  
2000             If ``False``, markers are plotted at the xcorr values using 
2001             `Axes.plot`. 
2002  
2003         maxlags : int, default: 10 
2004             Number of lags to show. If None, will return all ``2 * len(x) - 1`` 
2005             lags. 
2006  
2007         Returns 
2008         ------- 
2009         lags : array (length ``2*maxlags+1``) 
2010             The lag vector. 
2011         c : array  (length ``2*maxlags+1``) 
2012             The auto correlation vector. 
2013         line : `.LineCollection` or `.Line2D` 
2014             `.Artist` added to the axes of the correlation: 
2015  
2016             - `.LineCollection` if *usevlines* is True. 
2017             - `.Line2D` if *usevlines* is False. 
2018         b : `.Line2D` or None 
2019             Horizontal line at 0 if *usevlines* is True 
2020             None *usevlines* is False. 
2021  
2022         Other Parameters 
2023         ---------------- 
2024         linestyle : `.Line2D` property, optional 
2025             The linestyle for plotting the data points. 
2026             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``. 
2027  
2028         marker : str, default: 'o' 
2029             The marker for plotting the data points. 
2030             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``. 
2031  
2032         Notes 
2033         ----- 
2034         The cross correlation is performed with :func:`numpy.correlate` with 
2035         ``mode = "full"``. 
2036         """ 
2037         Nx = len(x) 
2038         if Nx != len(y): 
2039             raise ValueError('x and y must be equal length') 
2040  
2041         x = detrend(np.asarray(x)) 
2042         y = detrend(np.asarray(y)) 
2043  
2044         correls = np.correlate(x, y, mode="full") 
2045  
2046         if normed: 
2047             correls /= np.sqrt(np.dot(x, x) * np.dot(y, y)) 
2048  
2049         if maxlags is None: 
2050             maxlags = Nx - 1 
2051  
2052         if maxlags >= Nx or maxlags < 1: 
2053             raise ValueError('maxlags must be None or strictly ' 
2054                              'positive < %d' % Nx) 
2055  
2056         lags = np.arange(-maxlags, maxlags + 1) 
2057         correls = correls[Nx - 1 - maxlags:Nx + maxlags] 
2058  
2059         if usevlines: 
2060             a = self.vlines(lags, [0], correls, **kwargs) 
2061             # Make label empty so only vertical lines get a legend entry 
2062             kwargs.pop('label', '') 
2063             b = self.axhline(**kwargs) 
2064         else: 
2065             kwargs.setdefault('marker', 'o') 
2066             kwargs.setdefault('linestyle', 'None') 
2067             a, = self.plot(lags, correls, **kwargs) 
2068             b = None 
2069         return lags, correls, a, b 
2070  
2071     #### Specialized plotting 
2072  
2073     # @_preprocess_data() # let 'plot' do the unpacking.. 
2074     def step(self, x, y, *args, where='pre', data=None, **kwargs): 
2075         """ 
2076         Make a step plot. 
2077  
2078         Call signatures:: 
2079  
2080             step(x, y, [fmt], *, data=None, where='pre', **kwargs) 
2081             step(x, y, [fmt], x2, y2, [fmt2], ..., *, where='pre', **kwargs) 
2082  
2083         This is just a thin wrapper around `.plot` which changes some 
2084         formatting options. Most of the concepts and parameters of plot can be 
2085         used here as well. 
2086  
2087         Parameters 
2088         ---------- 
2089         x : array-like 
2090             1-D sequence of x positions. It is assumed, but not checked, that 
2091             it is uniformly increasing. 
2092  
2093         y : array-like 
2094             1-D sequence of y levels. 
2095  
2096         fmt : str, optional 
2097             A format string, e.g. 'g' for a green line. See `.plot` for a more 
2098             detailed description. 
2099  
2100             Note: While full format strings are accepted, it is recommended to 
2101             only specify the color. Line styles are currently ignored (use 
2102             the keyword argument *linestyle* instead). Markers are accepted 
2103             and plotted on the given positions, however, this is a rarely 
2104             needed feature for step plots. 
2105  
2106         data : indexable object, optional 
2107             An object with labelled data. If given, provide the label names to 
2108             plot in *x* and *y*. 
2109  
2110         where : {'pre', 'post', 'mid'}, default: 'pre' 
2111             Define where the steps should be placed: 
2112  
2113             - 'pre': The y value is continued constantly to the left from 
2114               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``(x[i-1], x[i]]`` has the 
2115               value ``y[i]``. 
2116             - 'post': The y value is continued constantly to the right from 
2117               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``[x[i], x[i+1])`` has the 
2118               value ``y[i]``. 
2119             - 'mid': Steps occur half-way between the *x* positions. 
2120  
2121         Returns 
2122         ------- 
2123         lines 
2124             A list of `.Line2D` objects representing the plotted data. 
2125  
2126         Other Parameters 
2127         ---------------- 
2128         **kwargs 
2129             Additional parameters are the same as those for `.plot`. 
2130  
2131         Notes 
2132         ----- 
2133         .. [notes section required to get data note injection right] 
2134         """ 
2135         cbook._check_in_list(('pre', 'post', 'mid'), where=where) 
2136         kwargs['drawstyle'] = 'steps-' + where 
2137         return self.plot(x, y, *args, data=data, **kwargs)

2139     @staticmethod 
2140     def _convert_dx(dx, x0, xconv, convert): 
2141         """ 
2142         Small helper to do logic of width conversion flexibly. 
2143  
2144         *dx* and *x0* have units, but *xconv* has already been converted 
2145         to unitless (and is an ndarray).  This allows the *dx* to have units 
2146         that are different from *x0*, but are still accepted by the 
2147         ``__add__`` operator of *x0*. 
2148         """ 
2149  
2150         # x should be an array... 
2151         assert type(xconv) is np.ndarray 
2152  
2153         if xconv.size == 0: 
2154             # xconv has already been converted, but maybe empty... 
2155             return convert(dx) 
2156  
2157         try: 
2158             # attempt to add the width to x0; this works for 
2159             # datetime+timedelta, for instance 
2160  
2161             # only use the first element of x and x0.  This saves 
2162             # having to be sure addition works across the whole 
2163             # vector.  This is particularly an issue if 
2164             # x0 and dx are lists so x0 + dx just concatenates the lists. 
2165             # We can't just cast x0 and dx to numpy arrays because that 
2166             # removes the units from unit packages like `pint` that 
2167             # wrap numpy arrays. 
2168             try: 
2169                 x0 = cbook.safe_first_element(x0) 
2170             except (TypeError, IndexError, KeyError): 
2171                 x0 = x0 
2172  
2173             try: 
2174                 x = cbook.safe_first_element(xconv) 
2175             except (TypeError, IndexError, KeyError): 
2176                 x = xconv 
2177  
2178             delist = False 
2179             if not np.iterable(dx): 
2180                 dx = [dx] 
2181                 delist = True 
2182             dx = [convert(x0 + ddx) - x for ddx in dx] 
2183             if delist: 
2184                 dx = dx[0] 
2185         except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): 
2186             # if the above fails (for any reason) just fallback to what 
2187             # we do by default and convert dx by itself. 
2188             dx = convert(dx) 
2189         return dx

2191     @_preprocess_data() 
2192     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
2193     def bar(self, x, height, width=0.8, bottom=None, *, align="center", 
2194             **kwargs): 
2195         r""" 
2196         Make a bar plot. 
2197  
2198         The bars are positioned at *x* with the given *align*\ment. Their 
2199         dimensions are given by *width* and *height*. The vertical baseline 
2200         is *bottom* (default 0). 
2201  
2202         Each of *x*, *height*, *width*, and *bottom* may either be a scalar 
2203         applying to all bars, or it may be a sequence of length N providing a 
2204         separate value for each bar. 
2205  
2206         Parameters 
2207         ---------- 
2208         x : sequence of scalars 
2209             The x coordinates of the bars. See also *align* for the 
2210             alignment of the bars to the coordinates. 
2211  
2212         height : scalar or sequence of scalars 
2213             The height(s) of the bars. 
2214  
2215         width : scalar or array-like, default: 0.8 
2216             The width(s) of the bars. 
2217  
2218         bottom : scalar or array-like, default: 0 
2219             The y coordinate(s) of the bars bases. 
2220  
2221         align : {'center', 'edge'}, default: 'center' 
2222             Alignment of the bars to the *x* coordinates: 
2223  
2224             - 'center': Center the base on the *x* positions. 
2225             - 'edge': Align the left edges of the bars with the *x* positions. 
2226  
2227             To align the bars on the right edge pass a negative *width* and 
2228             ``align='edge'``. 
2229  
2230         Returns 
2231         ------- 
2232         container : `.BarContainer` 
2233             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars. 
2234  
2235         Other Parameters 
2236         ---------------- 
2237         color : scalar or array-like, optional 
2238             The colors of the bar faces. 
2239  
2240         edgecolor : scalar or array-like, optional 
2241             The colors of the bar edges. 
2242  
2243         linewidth : scalar or array-like, optional 
2244             Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges. 
2245  
2246         tick_label : str or array-like, optional 
2247             The tick labels of the bars. 
2248             Default: None (Use default numeric labels.) 
2249  
2250         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
2251             If not *None*, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the bar tips. 
2252             The values are +/- sizes relative to the data: 
2253  
2254             - scalar: symmetric +/- values for all bars 
2255             - shape(N,): symmetric +/- values for each bar 
2256             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
2257               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
2258               errors. 
2259             - *None*: No errorbar. (Default) 
2260  
2261             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
2262             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
2263  
2264         ecolor : scalar or array-like, default: 'black' 
2265             The line color of the errorbars. 
2266  
2267         capsize : scalar, optional 
2268            The length of the error bar caps in points. 
2269            Default: None, which will take the value from 
2270            :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
2271  
2272         error_kw : dict, optional 
2273             Dictionary of kwargs to be passed to the `~.Axes.errorbar` 
2274             method. Values of *ecolor* or *capsize* defined here take 
2275             precedence over the independent kwargs. 
2276  
2277         log : bool, default: False 
2278             If *True*, set the y-axis to be log scale. 
2279  
2280         orientation : {'vertical',  'horizontal'}, optional 
2281             *This is for internal use only.* Please use `barh` for 
2282             horizontal bar plots. Default: 'vertical'. 
2283  
2284         See also 
2285         -------- 
2286         barh: Plot a horizontal bar plot. 
2287  
2288         Notes 
2289         ----- 
2290         The optional arguments *color*, *edgecolor*, *linewidth*, 
2291         *xerr*, and *yerr* can be either scalars or sequences of 
2292         length equal to the number of bars.  This enables you to use 
2293         bar as the basis for stacked bar charts, or candlestick plots. 
2294         Detail: *xerr* and *yerr* are passed directly to 
2295         :meth:`errorbar`, so they can also have shape 2xN for 
2296         independent specification of lower and upper errors. 
2297  
2298         Other optional kwargs: 
2299  
2300         %(Rectangle)s 
2301         """ 
2302         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mpatches.Patch) 
2303         color = kwargs.pop('color', None) 
2304         if color is None: 
2305             color = self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color() 
2306         edgecolor = kwargs.pop('edgecolor', None) 
2307         linewidth = kwargs.pop('linewidth', None) 
2308  
2309         # Because xerr and yerr will be passed to errorbar, most dimension 
2310         # checking and processing will be left to the errorbar method. 
2311         xerr = kwargs.pop('xerr', None) 
2312         yerr = kwargs.pop('yerr', None) 
2313         error_kw = kwargs.pop('error_kw', {}) 
2314         ezorder = error_kw.pop('zorder', None) 
2315         if ezorder is None: 
2316             ezorder = kwargs.get('zorder', None) 
2317             if ezorder is not None: 
2318                 # If using the bar zorder, increment slightly to make sure 
2319                 # errorbars are drawn on top of bars 
2320                 ezorder += 0.01 
2321         error_kw.setdefault('zorder', ezorder) 
2322         ecolor = kwargs.pop('ecolor', 'k') 
2323         capsize = kwargs.pop('capsize', rcParams["errorbar.capsize"]) 
2324         error_kw.setdefault('ecolor', ecolor) 
2325         error_kw.setdefault('capsize', capsize) 
2326  
2327         orientation = kwargs.pop('orientation', 'vertical') 
2328         cbook._check_in_list(['vertical', 'horizontal'], 
2329                              orientation=orientation) 
2330         log = kwargs.pop('log', False) 
2331         label = kwargs.pop('label', '') 
2332         tick_labels = kwargs.pop('tick_label', None) 
2333  
2334         y = bottom  # Matches barh call signature. 
2335         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2336             if y is None: 
2337                 y = 0 
2338         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2339             if x is None: 
2340                 x = 0 
2341  
2342         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2343             self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=height, kwargs=kwargs) 
2344             if log: 
2345                 self.set_yscale('log', nonposy='clip') 
2346         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2347             self._process_unit_info(xdata=width, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
2348             if log: 
2349                 self.set_xscale('log', nonposx='clip') 
2350  
2351         # lets do some conversions now since some types cannot be 
2352         # subtracted uniformly 
2353         if self.xaxis is not None: 
2354             x0 = x 
2355             x = np.asarray(self.convert_xunits(x)) 
2356             width = self._convert_dx(width, x0, x, self.convert_xunits) 
2357             if xerr is not None: 
2358                 xerr = self._convert_dx(xerr, x0, x, self.convert_xunits) 
2359         if self.yaxis is not None: 
2360             y0 = y 
2361             y = np.asarray(self.convert_yunits(y)) 
2362             height = self._convert_dx(height, y0, y, self.convert_yunits) 
2363             if yerr is not None: 
2364                 yerr = self._convert_dx(yerr, y0, y, self.convert_yunits) 
2365  
2366         x, height, width, y, linewidth = np.broadcast_arrays( 
2367             # Make args iterable too. 
2368             np.atleast_1d(x), height, width, y, linewidth) 
2369  
2370         # Now that units have been converted, set the tick locations. 
2371         if orientation == 'vertical': 
2372             tick_label_axis = self.xaxis 
2373             tick_label_position = x 
2374         elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2375             tick_label_axis = self.yaxis 
2376             tick_label_position = y 
2377  
2378         linewidth = itertools.cycle(np.atleast_1d(linewidth)) 
2379         color = itertools.chain(itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(color)), 
2380                                 # Fallback if color == "none". 
2381                                 itertools.repeat('none')) 
2382         if edgecolor is None: 
2383             edgecolor = itertools.repeat(None) 
2384         else: 
2385             edgecolor = itertools.chain( 
2386                 itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(edgecolor)), 
2387                 # Fallback if edgecolor == "none". 
2388                 itertools.repeat('none')) 
2389  
2390         # We will now resolve the alignment and really have 
2391         # left, bottom, width, height vectors 
2392         cbook._check_in_list(['center', 'edge'], align=align) 
2393         if align == 'center': 
2394             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2395                 try: 
2396                     left = x - width / 2 
2397                 except TypeError as e: 
2398                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters x ({x.dtype}) ' 
2399                                     f'and width ({width.dtype}) ' 
2400                                     f'are incompatible') from e 
2401                 bottom = y 
2402             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2403                 try: 
2404                     bottom = y - height / 2 
2405                 except TypeError as e: 
2406                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters y ({y.dtype}) ' 
2407                                     f'and height ({height.dtype}) ' 
2408                                     f'are incompatible') from e 
2409                 left = x 
2410         elif align == 'edge': 
2411             left = x 
2412             bottom = y 
2413  
2414         patches = [] 
2415         args = zip(left, bottom, width, height, color, edgecolor, linewidth) 
2416         for l, b, w, h, c, e, lw in args: 
2417             r = mpatches.Rectangle( 
2418                 xy=(l, b), width=w, height=h, 
2419                 facecolor=c, 
2420                 edgecolor=e, 
2421                 linewidth=lw, 
2422                 label='_nolegend_', 
2423                 ) 
2424             r.update(kwargs) 
2425             r.get_path()._interpolation_steps = 100 
2426             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2427                 r.sticky_edges.y.append(b) 
2428             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2429                 r.sticky_edges.x.append(l) 
2430             self.add_patch(r) 
2431             patches.append(r) 
2432  
2433         if xerr is not None or yerr is not None: 
2434             if orientation == 'vertical': 
2435                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info 
2436                 ex = [l + 0.5 * w for l, w in zip(left, width)] 
2437                 ey = [b + h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)] 
2438  
2439             elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
2440                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info 
2441                 ex = [l + w for l, w in zip(left, width)] 
2442                 ey = [b + 0.5 * h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)] 
2443  
2444             error_kw.setdefault("label", '_nolegend_') 
2445  
2446             errorbar = self.errorbar(ex, ey, 
2447                                      yerr=yerr, xerr=xerr, 
2448                                      fmt='none', **error_kw) 
2449         else: 
2450             errorbar = None 
2451  
2452         self._request_autoscale_view() 
2453  
2454         bar_container = BarContainer(patches, errorbar, label=label) 
2455         self.add_container(bar_container) 
2456  
2457         if tick_labels is not None: 
2458             tick_labels = np.broadcast_to(tick_labels, len(patches)) 
2459             tick_label_axis.set_ticks(tick_label_position) 
2460             tick_label_axis.set_ticklabels(tick_labels) 
2461  
2462         return bar_container 
2463  
2464     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
2465     def barh(self, y, width, height=0.8, left=None, *, align="center", 
2466              **kwargs): 
2467         r""" 
2468         Make a horizontal bar plot. 
2469  
2470         The bars are positioned at *y* with the given *align*\ment. Their 
2471         dimensions are given by *width* and *height*. The horizontal baseline 
2472         is *left* (default 0). 
2473  
2474         Each of *y*, *width*, *height*, and *left* may either be a scalar 
2475         applying to all bars, or it may be a sequence of length N providing a 
2476         separate value for each bar. 
2477  
2478         Parameters 
2479         ---------- 
2480         y : scalar or array-like 
2481             The y coordinates of the bars. See also *align* for the 
2482             alignment of the bars to the coordinates. 
2483  
2484         width : scalar or array-like 
2485             The width(s) of the bars. 
2486  
2487         height : sequence of scalars, default: 0.8 
2488             The heights of the bars. 
2489  
2490         left : sequence of scalars, default: 0 
2491             The x coordinates of the left sides of the bars. 
2492  
2493         align : {'center', 'edge'}, default: 'center' 
2494             Alignment of the base to the *y* coordinates*: 
2495  
2496             - 'center': Center the bars on the *y* positions. 
2497             - 'edge': Align the bottom edges of the bars with the *y* 
2498               positions. 
2499  
2500             To align the bars on the top edge pass a negative *height* and 
2501             ``align='edge'``. 
2502  
2503         Returns 
2504         ------- 
2505         container : `.BarContainer` 
2506             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars. 
2507  
2508         Other Parameters 
2509         ---------------- 
2510         color : scalar or array-like, optional 
2511             The colors of the bar faces. 
2512  
2513         edgecolor : scalar or array-like, optional 
2514             The colors of the bar edges. 
2515  
2516         linewidth : scalar or array-like, optional 
2517             Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges. 
2518  
2519         tick_label : str or array-like, optional 
2520             The tick labels of the bars. 
2521             Default: None (Use default numeric labels.) 
2522  
2523         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
2524             If not ``None``, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the 
2525             bar tips. The values are +/- sizes relative to the data: 
2526  
2527             - scalar: symmetric +/- values for all bars 
2528             - shape(N,): symmetric +/- values for each bar 
2529             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
2530               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
2531               errors. 
2532             - *None*: No errorbar. (default) 
2533  
2534             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
2535             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
2536  
2537         ecolor : scalar or array-like, default: 'black' 
2538             The line color of the errorbars. 
2539  
2540         capsize : scalar, optional 
2541            The length of the error bar caps in points. 
2542            Default: None, which will take the value from 
2543            :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
2544  
2545         error_kw : dict, optional 
2546             Dictionary of kwargs to be passed to the `~.Axes.errorbar` 
2547             method. Values of *ecolor* or *capsize* defined here take 
2548             precedence over the independent kwargs. 
2549  
2550         log : bool, default: False 
2551             If ``True``, set the x-axis to be log scale. 
2552  
2553         See also 
2554         -------- 
2555         bar: Plot a vertical bar plot. 
2556  
2557         Notes 
2558         ----- 
2559         The optional arguments *color*, *edgecolor*, *linewidth*, 
2560         *xerr*, and *yerr* can be either scalars or sequences of 
2561         length equal to the number of bars.  This enables you to use 
2562         bar as the basis for stacked bar charts, or candlestick plots. 
2563         Detail: *xerr* and *yerr* are passed directly to 
2564         :meth:`errorbar`, so they can also have shape 2xN for 
2565         independent specification of lower and upper errors. 
2566  
2567         Other optional kwargs: 
2568  
2569         %(Rectangle)s 
2570         """ 
2571         kwargs.setdefault('orientation', 'horizontal') 
2572         patches = self.bar(x=left, height=height, width=width, bottom=y, 
2573                            align=align, **kwargs) 
2574         return patches

2576     @_preprocess_data() 
2577     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
2578     def broken_barh(self, xranges, yrange, **kwargs): 
2579         """ 
2580         Plot a horizontal sequence of rectangles. 
2581  
2582         A rectangle is drawn for each element of *xranges*. All rectangles 
2583         have the same vertical position and size defined by *yrange*. 
2584  
2585         This is a convenience function for instantiating a 
2586         `.BrokenBarHCollection`, adding it to the axes and autoscaling the 
2587         view. 
2588  
2589         Parameters 
2590         ---------- 
2591         xranges : sequence of tuples (*xmin*, *xwidth*) 
2592             The x-positions and extends of the rectangles. For each tuple 
2593             (*xmin*, *xwidth*) a rectangle is drawn from *xmin* to *xmin* + 
2594             *xwidth*. 
2595         yrange : (*ymin*, *yheight*) 
2596             The y-position and extend for all the rectangles. 
2597  
2598         Other Parameters 
2599         ---------------- 
2600         **kwargs : :class:`.BrokenBarHCollection` properties 
2601  
2602             Each *kwarg* can be either a single argument applying to all 
2603             rectangles, e.g.:: 
2604  
2605                 facecolors='black' 
2606  
2607             or a sequence of arguments over which is cycled, e.g.:: 
2608  
2609                 facecolors=('black', 'blue') 
2610  
2611             would create interleaving black and blue rectangles. 
2612  
2613             Supported keywords: 
2614  
2615             %(BrokenBarHCollection)s 
2616  
2617         Returns 
2618         ------- 
2619         collection : A :class:`~.collections.BrokenBarHCollection` 
2620         """ 
2621         # process the unit information 
2622         if len(xranges): 
2623             xdata = cbook.safe_first_element(xranges) 
2624         else: 
2625             xdata = None 
2626         if len(yrange): 
2627             ydata = cbook.safe_first_element(yrange) 
2628         else: 
2629             ydata = None 
2630         self._process_unit_info(xdata=xdata, 
2631                                 ydata=ydata, 
2632                                 kwargs=kwargs) 
2633         xranges_conv = [] 
2634         for xr in xranges: 
2635             if len(xr) != 2: 
2636                 raise ValueError('each range in xrange must be a sequence ' 
2637                                  'with two elements (i.e. an Nx2 array)') 
2638             # convert the absolute values, not the x and dx... 
2639             x_conv = np.asarray(self.convert_xunits(xr[0])) 
2640             x1 = self._convert_dx(xr[1], xr[0], x_conv, self.convert_xunits) 
2641             xranges_conv.append((x_conv, x1)) 
2642  
2643         yrange_conv = self.convert_yunits(yrange) 
2644  
2645         col = mcoll.BrokenBarHCollection(xranges_conv, yrange_conv, **kwargs) 
2646         self.add_collection(col, autolim=True) 
2647         self._request_autoscale_view() 
2648  
2649         return col

2651     @_preprocess_data() 
2652     def stem(self, *args, linefmt=None, markerfmt=None, basefmt=None, bottom=0, 
2653              label=None, use_line_collection=False): 
2654         """ 
2655         Create a stem plot. 
2656  
2657         A stem plot plots vertical lines at each *x* location from the baseline 
2658         to *y*, and places a marker there. 
2659  
2660         Call signature:: 
2661  
2662           stem([x,] y, linefmt=None, markerfmt=None, basefmt=None) 
2663  
2664         The x-positions are optional. The formats may be provided either as 
2665         positional or as keyword-arguments. 
2666  
2667         Parameters 
2668         ---------- 
2669         x : array-like, optional 
2670             The x-positions of the stems. Default: (0, 1, ..., len(y) - 1). 
2671  
2672         y : array-like 
2673             The y-values of the stem heads. 
2674  
2675         linefmt : str, optional 
2676             A string defining the properties of the vertical lines. Usually, 
2677             this will be a color or a color and a linestyle: 
2678  
2679             =========  ============= 
2680             Character  Line Style 
2681             =========  ============= 
2682             ``'-'``    solid line 
2683             ``'--'``   dashed line 
2684             ``'-.'``   dash-dot line 
2685             ``':'``    dotted line 
2686             =========  ============= 
2687  
2688             Default: 'C0-', i.e. solid line with the first color of the color 
2689             cycle. 
2690  
2691             Note: While it is technically possible to specify valid formats 
2692             other than color or color and linestyle (e.g. 'rx' or '-.'), this 
2693             is beyond the intention of the method and will most likely not 
2694             result in a reasonable reasonable plot. 
2695  
2696         markerfmt : str, optional 
2697             A string defining the properties of the markers at the stem heads. 
2698             Default: 'C0o', i.e. filled circles with the first color of the 
2699             color cycle. 
2700  
2701         basefmt : str, default: 'C3-' ('C2-' in classic mode) 
2702             A format string defining the properties of the baseline. 
2703  
2704         bottom : float, default: 0 
2705             The y-position of the baseline. 
2706  
2707         label : str, default: None 
2708             The label to use for the stems in legends. 
2709  
2710         use_line_collection : bool, default: False 
2711             If ``True``, store and plot the stem lines as a 
2712             `~.collections.LineCollection` instead of individual lines. This 
2713             significantly increases performance, and will become the default 
2714             option in Matplotlib 3.3. If ``False``, defaults to the old 
2715             behavior of using a list of `.Line2D` objects. 
2716  
2717         Returns 
2718         ------- 
2719         container : :class:`~matplotlib.container.StemContainer` 
2720             The container may be treated like a tuple 
2721             (*markerline*, *stemlines*, *baseline*) 
2722  
2723         Notes 
2724         ----- 
2725         .. seealso:: 
2726             The MATLAB function 
2727             `stem <http://www.mathworks.com/help/techdoc/ref/stem.html>`_ 
2728             which inspired this method. 
2729         """ 
2730         if not 1 <= len(args) <= 5: 
2731             raise TypeError('stem expected between 1 and 5 positional ' 
2732                             'arguments, got {}'.format(args)) 
2733  
2734         if len(args) == 1: 
2735             y, = args 
2736             x = np.arange(len(y)) 
2737             args = () 
2738         else: 
2739             x, y, *args = args 
2740  
2741         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y) 
2742         x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
2743         y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
2744  
2745         # defaults for formats 
2746         if linefmt is None: 
2747             try: 
2748                 # fallback to positional argument 
2749                 linefmt = args[0] 
2750             except IndexError: 
2751                 linecolor = 'C0' 
2752                 linemarker = 'None' 
2753                 linestyle = '-' 
2754             else: 
2755                 linestyle, linemarker, linecolor = \ 
2756                     _process_plot_format(linefmt) 
2757         else: 
2758             linestyle, linemarker, linecolor = _process_plot_format(linefmt) 
2759  
2760         if markerfmt is None: 
2761             try: 
2762                 # fallback to positional argument 
2763                 markerfmt = args[1] 
2764             except IndexError: 
2765                 markercolor = 'C0' 
2766                 markermarker = 'o' 
2767                 markerstyle = 'None' 
2768             else: 
2769                 markerstyle, markermarker, markercolor = \ 
2770                     _process_plot_format(markerfmt) 
2771         else: 
2772             markerstyle, markermarker, markercolor = \ 
2773                 _process_plot_format(markerfmt) 
2774  
2775         if basefmt is None: 
2776             try: 
2777                 # fallback to positional argument 
2778                 basefmt = args[2] 
2779             except IndexError: 
2780                 if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
2781                     basecolor = 'C2' 
2782                 else: 
2783                     basecolor = 'C3' 
2784                 basemarker = 'None' 
2785                 basestyle = '-' 
2786             else: 
2787                 basestyle, basemarker, basecolor = \ 
2788                     _process_plot_format(basefmt) 
2789         else: 
2790             basestyle, basemarker, basecolor = _process_plot_format(basefmt) 
2791  
2792         # New behaviour in 3.1 is to use a LineCollection for the stemlines 
2793         if use_line_collection: 
2794             stemlines = [((xi, bottom), (xi, yi)) for xi, yi in zip(x, y)] 
2795             if linestyle is None: 
2796                 linestyle = rcParams['lines.linestyle'] 
2797             stemlines = mcoll.LineCollection(stemlines, linestyles=linestyle, 
2798                                              colors=linecolor, 
2799                                              label='_nolegend_') 
2800             self.add_collection(stemlines) 
2801         # Old behaviour is to plot each of the lines individually 
2802         else: 
2803             cbook._warn_external( 
2804                 'In Matplotlib 3.3 individual lines on a stem plot will be ' 
2805                 'added as a LineCollection instead of individual lines. ' 
2806                 'This significantly improves the performance of a stem plot. ' 
2807                 'To remove this warning and switch to the new behaviour, ' 
2808                 'set the "use_line_collection" keyword argument to True.') 
2809             stemlines = [] 
2810             for xi, yi in zip(x, y): 
2811                 l, = self.plot([xi, xi], [bottom, yi], 
2812                                color=linecolor, linestyle=linestyle, 
2813                                marker=linemarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2814                 stemlines.append(l) 
2815  
2816         markerline, = self.plot(x, y, color=markercolor, linestyle=markerstyle, 
2817                                 marker=markermarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2818  
2819         baseline, = self.plot([np.min(x), np.max(x)], [bottom, bottom], 
2820                               color=basecolor, linestyle=basestyle, 
2821                               marker=basemarker, label="_nolegend_") 
2822  
2823         stem_container = StemContainer((markerline, stemlines, baseline), 
2824                                        label=label) 
2825         self.add_container(stem_container) 
2826         return stem_container

2828     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "explode", "labels", "colors"]) 
2829     def pie(self, x, explode=None, labels=None, colors=None, 
2830             autopct=None, pctdistance=0.6, shadow=False, labeldistance=1.1, 
2831             startangle=None, radius=None, counterclock=True, 
2832             wedgeprops=None, textprops=None, center=(0, 0), 
2833             frame=False, rotatelabels=False): 
2834         """ 
2835         Plot a pie chart. 
2836  
2837         Make a pie chart of array *x*.  The fractional area of each wedge is 
2838         given by ``x/sum(x)``.  If ``sum(x) < 1``, then the values of *x* give 
2839         the fractional area directly and the array will not be normalized. The 
2840         resulting pie will have an empty wedge of size ``1 - sum(x)``. 
2841  
2842         The wedges are plotted counterclockwise, by default starting from the 
2843         x-axis. 
2844  
2845         Parameters 
2846         ---------- 
2847         x : array-like 
2848             The wedge sizes. 
2849  
2850         explode : array-like, default: None 
2851             If not *None*, is a ``len(x)`` array which specifies the fraction 
2852             of the radius with which to offset each wedge. 
2853  
2854         labels : list, default: None 
2855             A sequence of strings providing the labels for each wedge 
2856  
2857         colors : array-like, default: None 
2858             A sequence of colors through which the pie chart will cycle.  If 
2859             *None*, will use the colors in the currently active cycle. 
2860  
2861         autopct : None or str or callable, default: None 
2862             If not *None*, is a string or function used to label the wedges 
2863             with their numeric value.  The label will be placed inside the 
2864             wedge.  If it is a format string, the label will be ``fmt%pct``. 
2865             If it is a function, it will be called. 
2866  
2867         pctdistance : float, default: 0.6 
2868             The ratio between the center of each pie slice and the start of 
2869             the text generated by *autopct*.  Ignored if *autopct* is *None*. 
2870  
2871         shadow : bool, default: False 
2872             Draw a shadow beneath the pie. 
2873  
2874         labeldistance : float or None, default: 1.1 
2875             The radial distance at which the pie labels are drawn. 
2876             If set to ``None``, label are not drawn, but are stored for use in 
2877             ``legend()`` 
2878  
2879         startangle : float, default: None 
2880             If not *None*, rotates the start of the pie chart by *angle* 
2881             degrees counterclockwise from the x-axis. 
2882  
2883         radius : float, default: None 
2884             The radius of the pie, if *radius* is *None* it will be set to 1. 
2885  
2886         counterclock : bool, default: True 
2887             Specify fractions direction, clockwise or counterclockwise. 
2888  
2889         wedgeprops : dict, default: None 
2890             Dict of arguments passed to the wedge objects making the pie. 
2891             For example, you can pass in ``wedgeprops = {'linewidth': 3}`` 
2892             to set the width of the wedge border lines equal to 3. 
2893             For more details, look at the doc/arguments of the wedge object. 
2894             By default ``clip_on=False``. 
2895  
2896         textprops : dict, default: None 
2897             Dict of arguments to pass to the text objects. 
2898  
2899         center : (float, float), default: (0, 0) 
2900             The coordinates of the center of the chart. 
2901  
2902         frame : bool, default: False 
2903             Plot axes frame with the chart if true. 
2904  
2905         rotatelabels : bool, default: False 
2906             Rotate each label to the angle of the corresponding slice if true. 
2907  
2908         Returns 
2909         ------- 
2910         patches : list 
2911             A sequence of :class:`matplotlib.patches.Wedge` instances 
2912  
2913         texts : list 
2914             A list of the label :class:`matplotlib.text.Text` instances. 
2915  
2916         autotexts : list 
2917             A list of :class:`~matplotlib.text.Text` instances for the numeric 
2918             labels. This will only be returned if the parameter *autopct* is 
2919             not *None*. 
2920  
2921         Notes 
2922         ----- 
2923         The pie chart will probably look best if the figure and axes are 
2924         square, or the Axes aspect is equal. 
2925         This method sets the aspect ratio of the axis to "equal". 
2926         The axes aspect ratio can be controlled with `Axes.set_aspect`. 
2927         """ 
2928         self.set_aspect('equal') 
2929         # The use of float32 is "historical", but can't be changed without 
2930         # regenerating the test baselines. 
2931         x = np.asarray(x, np.float32) 
2932         if x.ndim != 1 and x.squeeze().ndim <= 1: 
2933             cbook.warn_deprecated( 
2934                 "3.1", message="Non-1D inputs to pie() are currently " 
2935                 "squeeze()d, but this behavior is deprecated since %(since)s " 
2936                 "and will be removed %(removal)s; pass a 1D array instead.") 
2937             x = np.atleast_1d(x.squeeze()) 
2938  
2939         sx = x.sum() 
2940         if sx > 1: 
2941             x = x / sx 
2942  
2943         if labels is None: 
2944             labels = [''] * len(x) 
2945         if explode is None: 
2946             explode = [0] * len(x) 
2947         if len(x) != len(labels): 
2948             raise ValueError("'label' must be of length 'x'") 
2949         if len(x) != len(explode): 
2950             raise ValueError("'explode' must be of length 'x'") 
2951         if colors is None: 
2952             get_next_color = self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color 
2953         else: 
2954             color_cycle = itertools.cycle(colors) 
2955  
2956             def get_next_color(): 
2957                 return next(color_cycle) 
2958  
2959         if radius is None: 
2960             radius = 1 
2961  
2962         # Starting theta1 is the start fraction of the circle 
2963         if startangle is None: 
2964             theta1 = 0 
2965         else: 
2966             theta1 = startangle / 360.0 
2967  
2968         # set default values in wedge_prop 
2969         if wedgeprops is None: 
2970             wedgeprops = {} 
2971         wedgeprops.setdefault('clip_on', False) 
2972  
2973         if textprops is None: 
2974             textprops = {} 
2975         textprops.setdefault('clip_on', False) 
2976  
2977         texts = [] 
2978         slices = [] 
2979         autotexts = [] 
2980  
2981         for frac, label, expl in zip(x, labels, explode): 
2982             x, y = center 
2983             theta2 = (theta1 + frac) if counterclock else (theta1 - frac) 
2984             thetam = 2 * np.pi * 0.5 * (theta1 + theta2) 
2985             x += expl * math.cos(thetam) 
2986             y += expl * math.sin(thetam) 
2987  
2988             w = mpatches.Wedge((x, y), radius, 360. * min(theta1, theta2), 
2989                                360. * max(theta1, theta2), 
2990                                facecolor=get_next_color(), 
2991                                **wedgeprops) 
2992             slices.append(w) 
2993             self.add_patch(w) 
2994             w.set_label(label) 
2995  
2996             if shadow: 
2997                 # make sure to add a shadow after the call to 
2998                 # add_patch so the figure and transform props will be 
2999                 # set 
3000                 shad = mpatches.Shadow(w, -0.02, -0.02) 
3001                 shad.set_zorder(0.9 * w.get_zorder()) 
3002                 shad.set_label('_nolegend_') 
3003                 self.add_patch(shad) 
3004  
3005             if labeldistance is not None: 
3006                 xt = x + labeldistance * radius * math.cos(thetam) 
3007                 yt = y + labeldistance * radius * math.sin(thetam) 
3008                 label_alignment_h = 'left' if xt > 0 else 'right' 
3009                 label_alignment_v = 'center' 
3010                 label_rotation = 'horizontal' 
3011                 if rotatelabels: 
3012                     label_alignment_v = 'bottom' if yt > 0 else 'top' 
3013                     label_rotation = (np.rad2deg(thetam) 
3014                                       + (0 if xt > 0 else 180)) 
3015                 props = dict(horizontalalignment=label_alignment_h, 
3016                              verticalalignment=label_alignment_v, 
3017                              rotation=label_rotation, 
3018                              size=rcParams['xtick.labelsize']) 
3019                 props.update(textprops) 
3020  
3021                 t = self.text(xt, yt, label, **props) 
3022  
3023                 texts.append(t) 
3024  
3025             if autopct is not None: 
3026                 xt = x + pctdistance * radius * math.cos(thetam) 
3027                 yt = y + pctdistance * radius * math.sin(thetam) 
3028                 if isinstance(autopct, str): 
3029                     s = autopct % (100. * frac) 
3030                 elif callable(autopct): 
3031                     s = autopct(100. * frac) 
3032                 else: 
3033                     raise TypeError( 
3034                         'autopct must be callable or a format string') 
3035  
3036                 props = dict(horizontalalignment='center', 
3037                              verticalalignment='center') 
3038                 props.update(textprops) 
3039                 t = self.text(xt, yt, s, **props) 
3040  
3041                 autotexts.append(t) 
3042  
3043             theta1 = theta2 
3044  
3045         if not frame: 
3046             self.set_frame_on(False) 
3047  
3048             self.set_xlim((-1.25 + center[0], 
3049                            1.25 + center[0])) 
3050             self.set_ylim((-1.25 + center[1], 
3051                            1.25 + center[1])) 
3052             self.set_xticks([]) 
3053             self.set_yticks([]) 
3054  
3055         if autopct is None: 
3056             return slices, texts 
3057         else: 
3058             return slices, texts, autotexts
