3060     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y", "xerr", "yerr"], 
3061                       label_namer="y") 
3062     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
3063     def errorbar(self, x, y, yerr=None, xerr=None, 
3064                  fmt='', ecolor=None, elinewidth=None, capsize=None, 
3065                  barsabove=False, lolims=False, uplims=False, 
3066                  xlolims=False, xuplims=False, errorevery=1, capthick=None, 
3067                  **kwargs): 
3068         """ 
3069         Plot y versus x as lines and/or markers with attached errorbars. 
3070  
3071         *x*, *y* define the data locations, *xerr*, *yerr* define the errorbar 
3072         sizes. By default, this draws the data markers/lines as well the 
3073         errorbars. Use fmt='none' to draw errorbars without any data markers. 
3074  
3075         Parameters 
3076         ---------- 
3077         x, y : scalar or array-like 
3078             The data positions. 
3079  
3080         xerr, yerr : scalar or array-like, shape(N,) or shape(2, N), optional 
3081             The errorbar sizes: 
3082  
3083             - scalar: Symmetric +/- values for all data points. 
3084             - shape(N,): Symmetric +/-values for each data point. 
3085             - shape(2, N): Separate - and + values for each bar. First row 
3086               contains the lower errors, the second row contains the upper 
3087               errors. 
3088             - *None*: No errorbar. 
3089  
3090             Note that all error arrays should have *positive* values. 
3091  
3092             See :doc:`/gallery/statistics/errorbar_features` 
3093             for an example on the usage of ``xerr`` and ``yerr``. 
3094  
3095         fmt : str, default: '' 
3096             The format for the data points / data lines. See `.plot` for 
3097             details. 
3098  
3099             Use 'none' (case insensitive) to plot errorbars without any data 
3100             markers. 
3101  
3102         ecolor : color, default: None 
3103             The color of the errorbar lines.  If None, use the color of the 
3104             line connecting the markers. 
3105  
3106         elinewidth : scalar, default: None 
3107             The linewidth of the errorbar lines. If None, the linewidth of 
3108             the current style is used. 
3109  
3110         capsize : scalar, default: None 
3111             The length of the error bar caps in points. If None, it will take 
3112             the value from :rc:`errorbar.capsize`. 
3113  
3114         capthick : scalar, default: None 
3115             An alias to the keyword argument *markeredgewidth* (a.k.a. *mew*). 
3116             This setting is a more sensible name for the property that 
3117             controls the thickness of the error bar cap in points. For 
3118             backwards compatibility, if *mew* or *markeredgewidth* are given, 
3119             then they will over-ride *capthick*. This may change in future 
3120             releases. 
3121  
3122         barsabove : bool, default: False 
3123             If True, will plot the errorbars above the plot 
3124             symbols. Default is below. 
3125  
3126         lolims, uplims, xlolims, xuplims : bool, default: False 
3127             These arguments can be used to indicate that a value gives only 
3128             upper/lower limits. In that case a caret symbol is used to 
3129             indicate this. *lims*-arguments may be of the same type as *xerr* 
3130             and *yerr*.  To use limits with inverted axes, :meth:`set_xlim` 
3131             or :meth:`set_ylim` must be called before :meth:`errorbar`. 
3132  
3133         errorevery : int or (int, int), default: 1 
3134             draws error bars on a subset of the data. *errorevery* =N draws 
3135             error bars on the points (x[::N], y[::N]). 
3136             *errorevery* =(start, N) draws error bars on the points 
3137             (x[start::N], y[start::N]). e.g. errorevery=(6, 3) 
3138             adds error bars to the data at (x[6], x[9], x[12], x[15], ...). 
3139             Used to avoid overlapping error bars when two series share x-axis 
3140             values. 
3141  
3142         Returns 
3143         ------- 
3144         container : :class:`~.container.ErrorbarContainer` 
3145             The container contains: 
3146  
3147             - plotline: `.Line2D` instance of x, y plot markers and/or line. 
3148             - caplines: A tuple of `.Line2D` instances of the error bar caps. 
3149             - barlinecols: A tuple of 
3150               :class:`~matplotlib.collections.LineCollection` with the 
3151               horizontal and vertical error ranges. 
3152  
3153         Other Parameters 
3154         ---------------- 
3155         **kwargs 
3156             All other keyword arguments are passed on to the plot 
3157             command for the markers. For example, this code makes big red 
3158             squares with thick green edges:: 
3159  
3160                 x, y, yerr = rand(3, 10) 
3161                 errorbar(x, y, yerr, marker='s', mfc='red', 
3162                          mec='green', ms=20, mew=4) 
3163  
3164             where *mfc*, *mec*, *ms* and *mew* are aliases for the longer 
3165             property names, *markerfacecolor*, *markeredgecolor*, *markersize* 
3166             and *markeredgewidth*. 
3167  
3168             Valid kwargs for the marker properties are `.Lines2D` properties: 
3169  
3170             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
3171         """ 
3172         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D) 
3173         # anything that comes in as 'None', drop so the default thing 
3174         # happens down stream 
3175         kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if v is not None} 
3176         kwargs.setdefault('zorder', 2) 
3177  
3178         try: 
3179             offset, errorevery = errorevery 
3180         except TypeError: 
3181             offset = 0 
3182  
3183         if errorevery < 1 or int(errorevery) != errorevery: 
3184             raise ValueError( 
3185                 'errorevery must be positive integer or tuple of integers') 
3186         if int(offset) != offset: 
3187             raise ValueError("errorevery's starting index must be an integer") 
3188  
3189         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
3190  
3191         plot_line = (fmt.lower() != 'none') 
3192         label = kwargs.pop("label", None) 
3193  
3194         if fmt == '': 
3195             fmt_style_kwargs = {} 
3196         else: 
3197             fmt_style_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in 
3198                                 zip(('linestyle', 'marker', 'color'), 
3199                                     _process_plot_format(fmt)) 
3200                                 if v is not None} 
3201         if fmt == 'none': 
3202             # Remove alpha=0 color that _process_plot_format returns 
3203             fmt_style_kwargs.pop('color') 
3204  
3205         if ('color' in kwargs or 'color' in fmt_style_kwargs or 
3206                 ecolor is not None): 
3207             base_style = {} 
3208             if 'color' in kwargs: 
3209                 base_style['color'] = kwargs.pop('color') 
3210         else: 
3211             base_style = next(self._get_lines.prop_cycler) 
3212  
3213         base_style['label'] = '_nolegend_' 
3214         base_style.update(fmt_style_kwargs) 
3215         if 'color' not in base_style: 
3216             base_style['color'] = 'C0' 
3217         if ecolor is None: 
3218             ecolor = base_style['color'] 
3219         # make sure all the args are iterable; use lists not arrays to 
3220         # preserve units 
3221         if not np.iterable(x): 
3222             x = [x] 
3223  
3224         if not np.iterable(y): 
3225             y = [y] 
3226  
3227         if xerr is not None: 
3228             if not np.iterable(xerr): 
3229                 xerr = [xerr] * len(x) 
3230  
3231         if yerr is not None: 
3232             if not np.iterable(yerr): 
3233                 yerr = [yerr] * len(y) 
3234  
3235         # make the style dict for the 'normal' plot line 
3236         plot_line_style = { 
3237             **base_style, 
3238             **kwargs, 
3239             'zorder': (kwargs['zorder'] - .1 if barsabove else 
3240                        kwargs['zorder'] + .1), 
3241         } 
3242  
3243         # make the style dict for the line collections (the bars) 
3244         eb_lines_style = dict(base_style) 
3245         eb_lines_style.pop('marker', None) 
3246         eb_lines_style.pop('linestyle', None) 
3247         eb_lines_style['color'] = ecolor 
3248  
3249         if elinewidth: 
3250             eb_lines_style['linewidth'] = elinewidth 
3251         elif 'linewidth' in kwargs: 
3252             eb_lines_style['linewidth'] = kwargs['linewidth'] 
3253  
3254         for key in ('transform', 'alpha', 'zorder', 'rasterized'): 
3255             if key in kwargs: 
3256                 eb_lines_style[key] = kwargs[key] 
3257  
3258         # set up cap style dictionary 
3259         eb_cap_style = dict(base_style) 
3260         # eject any marker information from format string 
3261         eb_cap_style.pop('marker', None) 
3262         eb_lines_style.pop('markerfacecolor', None) 
3263         eb_lines_style.pop('markeredgewidth', None) 
3264         eb_lines_style.pop('markeredgecolor', None) 
3265         eb_cap_style.pop('ls', None) 
3266         eb_cap_style['linestyle'] = 'none' 
3267         if capsize is None: 
3268             capsize = rcParams["errorbar.capsize"] 
3269         if capsize > 0: 
3270             eb_cap_style['markersize'] = 2. * capsize 
3271         if capthick is not None: 
3272             eb_cap_style['markeredgewidth'] = capthick 
3273  
3274         # For backwards-compat, allow explicit setting of 
3275         # 'markeredgewidth' to over-ride capthick. 
3276         for key in ('markeredgewidth', 'transform', 'alpha', 
3277                     'zorder', 'rasterized'): 
3278             if key in kwargs: 
3279                 eb_cap_style[key] = kwargs[key] 
3280         eb_cap_style['color'] = ecolor 
3281  
3282         data_line = None 
3283         if plot_line: 
3284             data_line = mlines.Line2D(x, y, **plot_line_style) 
3285             self.add_line(data_line) 
3286  
3287         barcols = [] 
3288         caplines = [] 
3289  
3290         # arrays fine here, they are booleans and hence not units 
3291         lolims = np.broadcast_to(lolims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3292         uplims = np.broadcast_to(uplims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3293         xlolims = np.broadcast_to(xlolims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3294         xuplims = np.broadcast_to(xuplims, len(x)).astype(bool) 
3295  
3296         everymask = np.zeros(len(x), bool) 
3297         everymask[offset::errorevery] = True 
3298  
3299         def xywhere(xs, ys, mask): 
3300             """ 
3301             return xs[mask], ys[mask] where mask is True but xs and 
3302             ys are not arrays 
3303             """ 
3304             assert len(xs) == len(ys) 
3305             assert len(xs) == len(mask) 
3306             xs = [thisx for thisx, b in zip(xs, mask) if b] 
3307             ys = [thisy for thisy, b in zip(ys, mask) if b] 
3308             return xs, ys 
3309  
3310         def extract_err(err, data): 
3311             """ 
3312             Private function to parse *err* and subtract/add it to *data*. 
3313  
3314             Both *err* and *data* are already iterables at this point. 
3315             """ 
3316             try:  # Asymmetric error: pair of 1D iterables. 
3317                 a, b = err 
3318                 iter(a) 
3319                 iter(b) 
3320             except (TypeError, ValueError): 
3321                 a = b = err  # Symmetric error: 1D iterable. 
3322             # This could just be `np.ndim(a) > 1 and np.ndim(b) > 1`, except 
3323             # for the (undocumented, but tested) support for (n, 1) arrays. 
3324             a_sh = np.shape(a) 
3325             b_sh = np.shape(b) 
3326             if (len(a_sh) > 2 or (len(a_sh) == 2 and a_sh[1] != 1) 
3327                     or len(b_sh) > 2 or (len(b_sh) == 2 and b_sh[1] != 1)): 
3328                 raise ValueError( 
3329                     "err must be a scalar or a 1D or (2, n) array-like") 
3330             if len(a_sh) == 2 or len(b_sh) == 2: 
3331                 cbook.warn_deprecated( 
3332                     "3.1", message="Support for passing a (n, 1)-shaped error " 
3333                     "array to errorbar() is deprecated since Matplotlib " 
3334                     "%(since)s and will be removed %(removal)s; pass a 1D " 
3335                     "array instead.") 
3336             # Using list comprehensions rather than arrays to preserve units. 
3337             for e in [a, b]: 
3338                 if len(data) != len(e): 
3339                     raise ValueError( 
3340                         f"The lengths of the data ({len(data)}) and the " 
3341                         f"error {len(e)} do not match") 
3342             low = [v - e for v, e in zip(data, a)] 
3343             high = [v + e for v, e in zip(data, b)] 
3344             return low, high 
3345  
3346         if xerr is not None: 
3347             left, right = extract_err(xerr, x) 
3348             # select points without upper/lower limits in x and 
3349             # draw normal errorbars for these points 
3350             noxlims = ~(xlolims | xuplims) 
3351             if noxlims.any() or len(noxlims) == 0: 
3352                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, noxlims & everymask) 
3353                 lo, ro = xywhere(left, right, noxlims & everymask) 
3354                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3355                 if capsize > 0: 
3356                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(lo, yo, marker='|', 
3357                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3358                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(ro, yo, marker='|', 
3359                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3360  
3361             if xlolims.any(): 
3362                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, xlolims & everymask) 
3363                 lo, ro = xywhere(x, right, xlolims & everymask) 
3364                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3365                 rightup, yup = xywhere(right, y, xlolims & everymask) 
3366                 if self.xaxis_inverted(): 
3367                     marker = mlines.CARETLEFTBASE 
3368                 else: 
3369                     marker = mlines.CARETRIGHTBASE 
3370                 caplines.append( 
3371                     mlines.Line2D(rightup, yup, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3372                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3373                 if capsize > 0: 
3374                     xlo, ylo = xywhere(x, y, xlolims & everymask) 
3375                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xlo, ylo, marker='|', 
3376                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3377  
3378             if xuplims.any(): 
3379                 yo, _ = xywhere(y, right, xuplims & everymask) 
3380                 lo, ro = xywhere(left, x, xuplims & everymask) 
3381                 barcols.append(self.hlines(yo, lo, ro, **eb_lines_style)) 
3382                 leftlo, ylo = xywhere(left, y, xuplims & everymask) 
3383                 if self.xaxis_inverted(): 
3384                     marker = mlines.CARETRIGHTBASE 
3385                 else: 
3386                     marker = mlines.CARETLEFTBASE 
3387                 caplines.append( 
3388                     mlines.Line2D(leftlo, ylo, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3389                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3390                 if capsize > 0: 
3391                     xup, yup = xywhere(x, y, xuplims & everymask) 
3392                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xup, yup, marker='|', 
3393                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3394  
3395         if yerr is not None: 
3396             lower, upper = extract_err(yerr, y) 
3397             # select points without upper/lower limits in y and 
3398             # draw normal errorbars for these points 
3399             noylims = ~(lolims | uplims) 
3400             if noylims.any() or len(noylims) == 0: 
3401                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, noylims & everymask) 
3402                 lo, uo = xywhere(lower, upper, noylims & everymask) 
3403                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3404                 if capsize > 0: 
3405                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xo, lo, marker='_', 
3406                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3407                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xo, uo, marker='_', 
3408                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3409  
3410             if lolims.any(): 
3411                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, lolims & everymask) 
3412                 lo, uo = xywhere(y, upper, lolims & everymask) 
3413                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3414                 xup, upperup = xywhere(x, upper, lolims & everymask) 
3415                 if self.yaxis_inverted(): 
3416                     marker = mlines.CARETDOWNBASE 
3417                 else: 
3418                     marker = mlines.CARETUPBASE 
3419                 caplines.append( 
3420                     mlines.Line2D(xup, upperup, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3421                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3422                 if capsize > 0: 
3423                     xlo, ylo = xywhere(x, y, lolims & everymask) 
3424                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xlo, ylo, marker='_', 
3425                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3426  
3427             if uplims.any(): 
3428                 xo, _ = xywhere(x, lower, uplims & everymask) 
3429                 lo, uo = xywhere(lower, y, uplims & everymask) 
3430                 barcols.append(self.vlines(xo, lo, uo, **eb_lines_style)) 
3431                 xlo, lowerlo = xywhere(x, lower, uplims & everymask) 
3432                 if self.yaxis_inverted(): 
3433                     marker = mlines.CARETUPBASE 
3434                 else: 
3435                     marker = mlines.CARETDOWNBASE 
3436                 caplines.append( 
3437                     mlines.Line2D(xlo, lowerlo, ls='None', marker=marker, 
3438                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3439                 if capsize > 0: 
3440                     xup, yup = xywhere(x, y, uplims & everymask) 
3441                     caplines.append(mlines.Line2D(xup, yup, marker='_', 
3442                                                   **eb_cap_style)) 
3443         for l in caplines: 
3444             self.add_line(l) 
3445  
3446         self._request_autoscale_view() 
3447         errorbar_container = ErrorbarContainer((data_line, tuple(caplines), 
3448                                                 tuple(barcols)), 
3449                                                has_xerr=(xerr is not None), 
3450                                                has_yerr=(yerr is not None), 
3451                                                label=label) 
3452         self.containers.append(errorbar_container) 
3453  
3454         return errorbar_container  # (l0, caplines, barcols)

3456     @cbook._rename_parameter("3.1", "manage_xticks", "manage_ticks") 
3457     @_preprocess_data() 
3458     def boxplot(self, x, notch=None, sym=None, vert=None, whis=None, 
3459                 positions=None, widths=None, patch_artist=None, 
3460                 bootstrap=None, usermedians=None, conf_intervals=None, 
3461                 meanline=None, showmeans=None, showcaps=None, 
3462                 showbox=None, showfliers=None, boxprops=None, 
3463                 labels=None, flierprops=None, medianprops=None, 
3464                 meanprops=None, capprops=None, whiskerprops=None, 
3465                 manage_ticks=True, autorange=False, zorder=None): 
3466         """ 
3467         Make a box and whisker plot. 
3468  
3469         Make a box and whisker plot for each column of ``x`` or each 
3470         vector in sequence ``x``.  The box extends from the lower to 
3471         upper quartile values of the data, with a line at the median. 
3472         The whiskers extend from the box to show the range of the 
3473         data.  Flier points are those past the end of the whiskers. 
3474  
3475         Parameters 
3476         ---------- 
3477         x : Array or a sequence of vectors. 
3478             The input data. 
3479  
3480         notch : bool, default: False 
3481             If `True`, will produce a notched box plot. Otherwise, a 
3482             rectangular boxplot is produced. The notches represent the 
3483             confidence interval (CI) around the median. See the entry 
3484             for the ``bootstrap`` parameter for information regarding 
3485             how the locations of the notches are computed. 
3486  
3487             .. note:: 
3488  
3489                 In cases where the values of the CI are less than the 
3490                 lower quartile or greater than the upper quartile, the 
3491                 notches will extend beyond the box, giving it a 
3492                 distinctive "flipped" appearance. This is expected 
3493                 behavior and consistent with other statistical 
3494                 visualization packages. 
3495  
3496         sym : str, optional 
3497             The default symbol for flier points. Enter an empty string 
3498             ('') if you don't want to show fliers. If `None`, then the 
3499             fliers default to 'b+'  If you want more control use the 
3500             flierprops kwarg. 
3501  
3502         vert : bool, default: True 
3503             If `True`, draws vertical boxes. 
3504             If `False`, draw horizontal boxes. 
3505  
3506         whis : float or (float, float), default: 1.5 
3507             The position of the whiskers. 
3508  
3509             If a float, the lower whisker is at the lowest datum above 
3510             ``Q1 - whis*(Q3-Q1)``, and the upper whisker at the highest datum 
3511             below ``Q3 + whis*(Q3-Q1)``, where Q1 and Q3 are the first and 
3512             third quartiles.  The default value of ``whis = 1.5`` corresponds 
3513             to Tukey's original definition of boxplots. 
3514  
3515             If a pair of floats, they indicate the percentiles at which to 
3516             draw the whiskers (e.g., (5, 95)).  In particular, setting this to 
3517             (0, 100) results in whiskers covering the whole range of the data. 
3518             "range" is a deprecated synonym for (0, 100). 
3519  
3520             In the edge case where ``Q1 == Q3``, *whis* is automatically set 
3521             to (0, 100) (cover the whole range of the data) if *autorange* is 
3522             True. 
3523  
3524             Beyond the whiskers, data are considered outliers and are plotted 
3525             as individual points. 
3526  
3527         bootstrap : int, optional 
3528             Specifies whether to bootstrap the confidence intervals 
3529             around the median for notched boxplots. If ``bootstrap`` is 
3530             None, no bootstrapping is performed, and notches are 
3531             calculated using a Gaussian-based asymptotic approximation 
3532             (see McGill, R., Tukey, J.W., and Larsen, W.A., 1978, and 
3533             Kendall and Stuart, 1967). Otherwise, bootstrap specifies 
3534             the number of times to bootstrap the median to determine its 
3535             95% confidence intervals. Values between 1000 and 10000 are 
3536             recommended. 
3537  
3538         usermedians : array-like, optional 
3539             An array or sequence whose first dimension (or length) is 
3540             compatible with ``x``. This overrides the medians computed 
3541             by matplotlib for each element of ``usermedians`` that is not 
3542             `None`. When an element of ``usermedians`` is None, the median 
3543             will be computed by matplotlib as normal. 
3544  
3545         conf_intervals : array-like, optional 
3546             Array or sequence whose first dimension (or length) is 
3547             compatible with ``x`` and whose second dimension is 2. When 
3548             the an element of ``conf_intervals`` is not None, the 
3549             notch locations computed by matplotlib are overridden 
3550             (provided ``notch`` is `True`). When an element of 
3551             ``conf_intervals`` is `None`, the notches are computed by the 
3552             method specified by the other kwargs (e.g., ``bootstrap``). 
3553  
3554         positions : array-like, optional 
3555             Sets the positions of the boxes. The ticks and limits are 
3556             automatically set to match the positions. Defaults to 
3557             `range(1, N+1)` where N is the number of boxes to be drawn. 
3558  
3559         widths : scalar or array-like 
3560             Sets the width of each box either with a scalar or a 
3561             sequence. The default is 0.5, or ``0.15*(distance between 
3562             extreme positions)``, if that is smaller. 
3563  
3564         patch_artist : bool, default: False 
3565             If `False` produces boxes with the Line2D artist. Otherwise, 
3566             boxes and drawn with Patch artists. 
3567  
3568         labels : sequence, optional 
3569             Labels for each dataset. Length must be compatible with 
3570             dimensions of ``x``. 
3571  
3572         manage_ticks : bool, default: True 
3573             If True, the tick locations and labels will be adjusted to match 
3574             the boxplot positions. 
3575  
3576         autorange : bool, default: False 
3577             When `True` and the data are distributed such that the 25th and 
3578             75th percentiles are equal, ``whis`` is set to (0, 100) such 
3579             that the whisker ends are at the minimum and maximum of the data. 
3580  
3581         meanline : bool, default: False 
3582             If `True` (and ``showmeans`` is `True`), will try to render 
3583             the mean as a line spanning the full width of the box 
3584             according to ``meanprops`` (see below). Not recommended if 
3585             ``shownotches`` is also True. Otherwise, means will be shown 
3586             as points. 
3587  
3588         zorder : scalar, default: None 
3589             Sets the zorder of the boxplot. 
3590  
3591         Other Parameters 
3592         ---------------- 
3593         showcaps : bool, default: True 
3594             Show the caps on the ends of whiskers. 
3595         showbox : bool, default: True 
3596             Show the central box. 
3597         showfliers : bool, default: True 
3598             Show the outliers beyond the caps. 
3599         showmeans : bool, default: False 
3600             Show the arithmetic means. 
3601         capprops : dict, default: None 
3602             The style of the caps. 
3603         boxprops : dict, default: None 
3604             The style of the box. 
3605         whiskerprops : dict, default: None 
3606             The style of the whiskers. 
3607         flierprops : dict, default: None 
3608             The style of the fliers. 
3609         medianprops : dict, default: None 
3610             The style of the median. 
3611         meanprops : dict, default: None 
3612             The style of the mean. 
3613  
3614         Returns 
3615         ------- 
3616         result : dict 
3617           A dictionary mapping each component of the boxplot to a list 
3618           of the `.Line2D` instances created. That dictionary has the 
3619           following keys (assuming vertical boxplots): 
3620  
3621           - ``boxes``: the main body of the boxplot showing the 
3622             quartiles and the median's confidence intervals if 
3623             enabled. 
3624  
3625           - ``medians``: horizontal lines at the median of each box. 
3626  
3627           - ``whiskers``: the vertical lines extending to the most 
3628             extreme, non-outlier data points. 
3629  
3630           - ``caps``: the horizontal lines at the ends of the 
3631             whiskers. 
3632  
3633           - ``fliers``: points representing data that extend beyond 
3634             the whiskers (fliers). 
3635  
3636           - ``means``: points or lines representing the means. 
3637  
3638         """ 
3639  
3640         # Missing arguments default to rcParams. 
3641         if whis is None: 
3642             whis = rcParams['boxplot.whiskers'] 
3643         if bootstrap is None: 
3644             bootstrap = rcParams['boxplot.bootstrap'] 
3645  
3646         bxpstats = cbook.boxplot_stats(x, whis=whis, bootstrap=bootstrap, 
3647                                        labels=labels, autorange=autorange) 
3648         if notch is None: 
3649             notch = rcParams['boxplot.notch'] 
3650         if vert is None: 
3651             vert = rcParams['boxplot.vertical'] 
3652         if patch_artist is None: 
3653             patch_artist = rcParams['boxplot.patchartist'] 
3654         if meanline is None: 
3655             meanline = rcParams['boxplot.meanline'] 
3656         if showmeans is None: 
3657             showmeans = rcParams['boxplot.showmeans'] 
3658         if showcaps is None: 
3659             showcaps = rcParams['boxplot.showcaps'] 
3660         if showbox is None: 
3661             showbox = rcParams['boxplot.showbox'] 
3662         if showfliers is None: 
3663             showfliers = rcParams['boxplot.showfliers'] 
3664  
3665         if boxprops is None: 
3666             boxprops = {} 
3667         if whiskerprops is None: 
3668             whiskerprops = {} 
3669         if capprops is None: 
3670             capprops = {} 
3671         if medianprops is None: 
3672             medianprops = {} 
3673         if meanprops is None: 
3674             meanprops = {} 
3675         if flierprops is None: 
3676             flierprops = {} 
3677  
3678         if patch_artist: 
3679             boxprops['linestyle'] = 'solid'  # Not consistent with bxp. 
3680             if 'color' in boxprops: 
3681                 boxprops['edgecolor'] = boxprops.pop('color') 
3682  
3683         # if non-default sym value, put it into the flier dictionary 
3684         # the logic for providing the default symbol ('b+') now lives 
3685         # in bxp in the initial value of final_flierprops 
3686         # handle all of the *sym* related logic here so we only have to pass 
3687         # on the flierprops dict. 
3688         if sym is not None: 
3689             # no-flier case, which should really be done with 
3690             # 'showfliers=False' but none-the-less deal with it to keep back 
3691             # compatibility 
3692             if sym == '': 
3693                 # blow away existing dict and make one for invisible markers 
3694                 flierprops = dict(linestyle='none', marker='', color='none') 
3695                 # turn the fliers off just to be safe 
3696                 showfliers = False 
3697             # now process the symbol string 
3698             else: 
3699                 # process the symbol string 
3700                 # discarded linestyle 
3701                 _, marker, color = _process_plot_format(sym) 
3702                 # if we have a marker, use it 
3703                 if marker is not None: 
3704                     flierprops['marker'] = marker 
3705                 # if we have a color, use it 
3706                 if color is not None: 
3707                     # assume that if color is passed in the user want 
3708                     # filled symbol, if the users want more control use 
3709                     # flierprops 
3710                     flierprops['color'] = color 
3711                     flierprops['markerfacecolor'] = color 
3712                     flierprops['markeredgecolor'] = color 
3713  
3714         # replace medians if necessary: 
3715         if usermedians is not None: 
3716             if (len(np.ravel(usermedians)) != len(bxpstats) or 
3717                     np.shape(usermedians)[0] != len(bxpstats)): 
3718                 raise ValueError('usermedians length not compatible with x') 
3719             else: 
3720                 # reassign medians as necessary 
3721                 for stats, med in zip(bxpstats, usermedians): 
3722                     if med is not None: 
3723                         stats['med'] = med 
3724  
3725         if conf_intervals is not None: 
3726             if np.shape(conf_intervals)[0] != len(bxpstats): 
3727                 err_mess = 'conf_intervals length not compatible with x' 
3728                 raise ValueError(err_mess) 
3729             else: 
3730                 for stats, ci in zip(bxpstats, conf_intervals): 
3731                     if ci is not None: 
3732                         if len(ci) != 2: 
3733                             raise ValueError('each confidence interval must ' 
3734                                              'have two values') 
3735                         else: 
3736                             if ci[0] is not None: 
3737                                 stats['cilo'] = ci[0] 
3738                             if ci[1] is not None: 
3739                                 stats['cihi'] = ci[1] 
3740  
3741         artists = self.bxp(bxpstats, positions=positions, widths=widths, 
3742                            vert=vert, patch_artist=patch_artist, 
3743                            shownotches=notch, showmeans=showmeans, 
3744                            showcaps=showcaps, showbox=showbox, 
3745                            boxprops=boxprops, flierprops=flierprops, 
3746                            medianprops=medianprops, meanprops=meanprops, 
3747                            meanline=meanline, showfliers=showfliers, 
3748                            capprops=capprops, whiskerprops=whiskerprops, 
3749                            manage_ticks=manage_ticks, zorder=zorder) 
3750         return artists

3752     @cbook._rename_parameter("3.1", "manage_xticks", "manage_ticks") 
3753     def bxp(self, bxpstats, positions=None, widths=None, vert=True, 
3754             patch_artist=False, shownotches=False, showmeans=False, 
3755             showcaps=True, showbox=True, showfliers=True, 
3756             boxprops=None, whiskerprops=None, flierprops=None, 
3757             medianprops=None, capprops=None, meanprops=None, 
3758             meanline=False, manage_ticks=True, zorder=None): 
3759         """ 
3760         Drawing function for box and whisker plots. 
3761  
3762         Make a box and whisker plot for each column of *x* or each 
3763         vector in sequence *x*.  The box extends from the lower to 
3764         upper quartile values of the data, with a line at the median. 
3765         The whiskers extend from the box to show the range of the 
3766         data.  Flier points are those past the end of the whiskers. 
3767  
3768         Parameters 
3769         ---------- 
3770         bxpstats : list of dicts 
3771           A list of dictionaries containing stats for each boxplot. 
3772           Required keys are: 
3773  
3774           - ``med``: The median (scalar float). 
3775  
3776           - ``q1``: The first quartile (25th percentile) (scalar 
3777             float). 
3778  
3779           - ``q3``: The third quartile (75th percentile) (scalar 
3780             float). 
3781  
3782           - ``whislo``: Lower bound of the lower whisker (scalar 
3783             float). 
3784  
3785           - ``whishi``: Upper bound of the upper whisker (scalar 
3786             float). 
3787  
3788           Optional keys are: 
3789  
3790           - ``mean``: The mean (scalar float). Needed if 
3791             ``showmeans=True``. 
3792  
3793           - ``fliers``: Data beyond the whiskers (sequence of floats). 
3794             Needed if ``showfliers=True``. 
3795  
3796           - ``cilo`` & ``cihi``: Lower and upper confidence intervals 
3797             about the median. Needed if ``shownotches=True``. 
3798  
3799           - ``label``: Name of the dataset (string). If available, 
3800             this will be used a tick label for the boxplot 
3801  
3802         positions : array-like, default: [1, 2, ..., n] 
3803           Sets the positions of the boxes. The ticks and limits 
3804           are automatically set to match the positions. 
3805  
3806         widths : array-like, default: None 
3807           Either a scalar or a vector and sets the width of each 
3808           box. The default is ``0.15*(distance between extreme 
3809           positions)``, clipped to no less than 0.15 and no more than 
3810           0.5. 
3811  
3812         vert : bool, default: True 
3813           If `True` (default), makes the boxes vertical.  If `False`, 
3814           makes horizontal boxes. 
3815  
3816         patch_artist : bool, default: False 
3817           If `False` produces boxes with the `.Line2D` artist. 
3818           If `True` produces boxes with the `~matplotlib.patches.Patch` artist. 
3819  
3820         shownotches : bool, default: False 
3821           If `False` (default), produces a rectangular box plot. 
3822           If `True`, will produce a notched box plot 
3823  
3824         showmeans : bool, default: False 
3825           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the means 
3826  
3827         showcaps  : bool, default: True 
3828           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the caps 
3829  
3830         showbox  : bool, default: True 
3831           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the box 
3832  
3833         showfliers : bool, default: True 
3834           If `True`, will toggle on the rendering of the fliers 
3835  
3836         boxprops : dict or None (default) 
3837           If provided, will set the plotting style of the boxes 
3838  
3839         whiskerprops : dict or None (default) 
3840           If provided, will set the plotting style of the whiskers 
3841  
3842         capprops : dict or None (default) 
3843           If provided, will set the plotting style of the caps 
3844  
3845         flierprops : dict or None (default) 
3846           If provided will set the plotting style of the fliers 
3847  
3848         medianprops : dict or None (default) 
3849           If provided, will set the plotting style of the medians 
3850  
3851         meanprops : dict or None (default) 
3852           If provided, will set the plotting style of the means 
3853  
3854         meanline : bool, default: False 
3855           If `True` (and *showmeans* is `True`), will try to render the mean 
3856           as a line spanning the full width of the box according to 
3857           *meanprops*. Not recommended if *shownotches* is also True. 
3858           Otherwise, means will be shown as points. 
3859  
3860         manage_ticks : bool, default: True 
3861           If True, the tick locations and labels will be adjusted to match the 
3862           boxplot positions. 
3863  
3864         zorder : scalar, default: None 
3865           The zorder of the resulting boxplot. 
3866  
3867         Returns 
3868         ------- 
3869         result : dict 
3870           A dictionary mapping each component of the boxplot to a list 
3871           of the `.Line2D` instances created. That dictionary has the 
3872           following keys (assuming vertical boxplots): 
3873  
3874           - ``boxes``: the main body of the boxplot showing the 
3875             quartiles and the median's confidence intervals if 
3876             enabled. 
3877  
3878           - ``medians``: horizontal lines at the median of each box. 
3879  
3880           - ``whiskers``: the vertical lines extending to the most 
3881             extreme, non-outlier data points. 
3882  
3883           - ``caps``: the horizontal lines at the ends of the 
3884             whiskers. 
3885  
3886           - ``fliers``: points representing data that extend beyond 
3887             the whiskers (fliers). 
3888  
3889           - ``means``: points or lines representing the means. 
3890  
3891         Examples 
3892         -------- 
3893         .. plot:: gallery/statistics/bxp.py 
3894  
3895         """ 
3896         # lists of artists to be output 
3897         whiskers = [] 
3898         caps = [] 
3899         boxes = [] 
3900         medians = [] 
3901         means = [] 
3902         fliers = [] 
3903  
3904         # empty list of xticklabels 
3905         datalabels = [] 
3906  
3907         # Use default zorder if none specified 
3908         if zorder is None: 
3909             zorder = mlines.Line2D.zorder 
3910  
3911         zdelta = 0.1 
3912  
3913         def line_props_with_rcdefaults(subkey, explicit, zdelta=0, 
3914                                        use_marker=True): 
3915             d = {k.split('.')[-1]: v for k, v in rcParams.items() 
3916                  if k.startswith(f'boxplot.{subkey}')} 
3917             d['zorder'] = zorder + zdelta 
3918             if not use_marker: 
3919                 d['marker'] = '' 
3920             if explicit is not None: 
3921                 d.update( 
3922                     cbook.normalize_kwargs(explicit, mlines.Line2D._alias_map)) 
3923             return d 
3924  
3925         # box properties 
3926         if patch_artist: 
3927             final_boxprops = dict( 
3928                 linestyle=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.linestyle'], 
3929                 linewidth=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.linewidth'], 
3930                 edgecolor=rcParams['boxplot.boxprops.color'], 
3931                 facecolor=('white' if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] else 
3932                            rcParams['patch.facecolor']), 
3933                 zorder=zorder, 
3934             ) 
3935             if boxprops is not None: 
3936                 final_boxprops.update( 
3937                     cbook.normalize_kwargs( 
3938                         boxprops, mpatches.PathPatch._alias_map)) 
3939         else: 
3940             final_boxprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults('boxprops', boxprops, 
3941                                                         use_marker=False) 
3942         final_whiskerprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3943             'whiskerprops', whiskerprops, use_marker=False) 
3944         final_capprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3945             'capprops', capprops, use_marker=False) 
3946         final_flierprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3947             'flierprops', flierprops) 
3948         final_medianprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3949             'medianprops', medianprops, zdelta, use_marker=False) 
3950         final_meanprops = line_props_with_rcdefaults( 
3951             'meanprops', meanprops, zdelta) 
3952         removed_prop = 'marker' if meanline else 'linestyle' 
3953         # Only remove the property if it's not set explicitly as a parameter. 
3954         if meanprops is None or removed_prop not in meanprops: 
3955             final_meanprops[removed_prop] = '' 
3956  
3957         def to_vc(xs, ys): 
3958             # convert arguments to verts and codes, append (0, 0) (ignored). 
3959             verts = np.append(np.column_stack([xs, ys]), [(0, 0)], 0) 
3960             codes = ([mpath.Path.MOVETO] 
3961                      + [mpath.Path.LINETO] * (len(verts) - 2) 
3962                      + [mpath.Path.CLOSEPOLY]) 
3963             return verts, codes 
3964  
3965         def patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3966             verts, codes = to_vc(xs, ys) 
3967             path = mpath.Path(verts, codes) 
3968             patch = mpatches.PathPatch(path, **kwargs) 
3969             self.add_artist(patch) 
3970             return [patch] 
3971  
3972         # vertical or horizontal plot? 
3973         if vert: 
3974             def doplot(*args, **kwargs): 
3975                 return self.plot(*args, **kwargs) 
3976  
3977             def dopatch(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3978                 return patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs) 
3979  
3980         else: 
3981             def doplot(*args, **kwargs): 
3982                 shuffled = [] 
3983                 for i in range(0, len(args), 2): 
3984                     shuffled.extend([args[i + 1], args[i]]) 
3985                 return self.plot(*shuffled, **kwargs) 
3986  
3987             def dopatch(xs, ys, **kwargs): 
3988                 xs, ys = ys, xs  # flip X, Y 
3989                 return patch_list(xs, ys, **kwargs) 
3990  
3991         # input validation 
3992         N = len(bxpstats) 
3993         datashape_message = ("List of boxplot statistics and `{0}` " 
3994                              "values must have same the length") 
3995         # check position 
3996         if positions is None: 
3997             positions = list(range(1, N + 1)) 
3998         elif len(positions) != N: 
3999             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("positions")) 
4000  
4001         positions = np.array(positions) 
4002         if len(positions) > 0 and not isinstance(positions[0], Number): 
4003             raise TypeError("positions should be an iterable of numbers") 
4004  
4005         # width 
4006         if widths is None: 
4007             widths = [np.clip(0.15 * np.ptp(positions), 0.15, 0.5)] * N 
4008         elif np.isscalar(widths): 
4009             widths = [widths] * N 
4010         elif len(widths) != N: 
4011             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("widths")) 
4012  
4013         for pos, width, stats in zip(positions, widths, bxpstats): 
4014             # try to find a new label 
4015             datalabels.append(stats.get('label', pos)) 
4016  
4017             # whisker coords 
4018             whisker_x = np.ones(2) * pos 
4019             whiskerlo_y = np.array([stats['q1'], stats['whislo']]) 
4020             whiskerhi_y = np.array([stats['q3'], stats['whishi']]) 
4021  
4022             # cap coords 
4023             cap_left = pos - width * 0.25 
4024             cap_right = pos + width * 0.25 
4025             cap_x = np.array([cap_left, cap_right]) 
4026             cap_lo = np.ones(2) * stats['whislo'] 
4027             cap_hi = np.ones(2) * stats['whishi'] 
4028  
4029             # box and median coords 
4030             box_left = pos - width * 0.5 
4031             box_right = pos + width * 0.5 
4032             med_y = [stats['med'], stats['med']] 
4033  
4034             # notched boxes 
4035             if shownotches: 
4036                 box_x = [box_left, box_right, box_right, cap_right, box_right, 
4037                          box_right, box_left, box_left, cap_left, box_left, 
4038                          box_left] 
4039                 box_y = [stats['q1'], stats['q1'], stats['cilo'], 
4040                          stats['med'], stats['cihi'], stats['q3'], 
4041                          stats['q3'], stats['cihi'], stats['med'], 
4042                          stats['cilo'], stats['q1']] 
4043                 med_x = cap_x 
4044  
4045             # plain boxes 
4046             else: 
4047                 box_x = [box_left, box_right, box_right, box_left, box_left] 
4048                 box_y = [stats['q1'], stats['q1'], stats['q3'], stats['q3'], 
4049                          stats['q1']] 
4050                 med_x = [box_left, box_right] 
4051  
4052             # maybe draw the box: 
4053             if showbox: 
4054                 if patch_artist: 
4055                     boxes.extend(dopatch(box_x, box_y, **final_boxprops)) 
4056                 else: 
4057                     boxes.extend(doplot(box_x, box_y, **final_boxprops)) 
4058  
4059             # draw the whiskers 
4060             whiskers.extend(doplot( 
4061                 whisker_x, whiskerlo_y, **final_whiskerprops 
4062             )) 
4063             whiskers.extend(doplot( 
4064                 whisker_x, whiskerhi_y, **final_whiskerprops 
4065             )) 
4066  
4067             # maybe draw the caps: 
4068             if showcaps: 
4069                 caps.extend(doplot(cap_x, cap_lo, **final_capprops)) 
4070                 caps.extend(doplot(cap_x, cap_hi, **final_capprops)) 
4071  
4072             # draw the medians 
4073             medians.extend(doplot(med_x, med_y, **final_medianprops)) 
4074  
4075             # maybe draw the means 
4076             if showmeans: 
4077                 if meanline: 
4078                     means.extend(doplot( 
4079                         [box_left, box_right], [stats['mean'], stats['mean']], 
4080                         **final_meanprops 
4081                     )) 
4082                 else: 
4083                     means.extend(doplot( 
4084                         [pos], [stats['mean']], **final_meanprops 
4085                     )) 
4086  
4087             # maybe draw the fliers 
4088             if showfliers: 
4089                 # fliers coords 
4090                 flier_x = np.full(len(stats['fliers']), pos, dtype=np.float64) 
4091                 flier_y = stats['fliers'] 
4092  
4093                 fliers.extend(doplot( 
4094                     flier_x, flier_y, **final_flierprops 
4095                 )) 
4096  
4097         if manage_ticks: 
4098             axis_name = "x" if vert else "y" 
4099             interval = getattr(self.dataLim, f"interval{axis_name}") 
4100             axis = getattr(self, f"{axis_name}axis") 
4101             positions = axis.convert_units(positions) 
4102             # The 0.5 additional padding ensures reasonable-looking boxes 
4103             # even when drawing a single box.  We set the sticky edge to 
4104             # prevent margins expansion, in order to match old behavior (back 
4105             # when separate calls to boxplot() would completely reset the axis 
4106             # limits regardless of what was drawn before).  The sticky edges 
4107             # are attached to the median lines, as they are always present. 
4108             interval[:] = (min(interval[0], min(positions) - .5), 
4109                            max(interval[1], max(positions) + .5)) 
4110             for median, position in zip(medians, positions): 
4111                 getattr(median.sticky_edges, axis_name).extend( 
4112                     [position - .5, position + .5]) 
4113             # Modified from Axis.set_ticks and Axis.set_ticklabels. 
4114             locator = axis.get_major_locator() 
4115             if not isinstance(axis.get_major_locator(), 
4116                               mticker.FixedLocator): 
4117                 locator = mticker.FixedLocator([]) 
4118                 axis.set_major_locator(locator) 
4119             locator.locs = np.array([*locator.locs, *positions]) 
4120             formatter = axis.get_major_formatter() 
4121             if not isinstance(axis.get_major_formatter(), 
4122                               mticker.FixedFormatter): 
4123                 formatter = mticker.FixedFormatter([]) 
4124                 axis.set_major_formatter(formatter) 
4125             formatter.seq = [*formatter.seq, *datalabels] 
4126  
4127             self._request_autoscale_view( 
4128                 scalex=self._autoscaleXon, scaley=self._autoscaleYon) 
4129  
4130         return dict(whiskers=whiskers, caps=caps, boxes=boxes, 
4131                     medians=medians, fliers=fliers, means=means) 
4132  
4133     @staticmethod 
4134     def _parse_scatter_color_args(c, edgecolors, kwargs, xsize, 
4135                                   get_next_color_func): 
4136         """ 
4137         Helper function to process color related arguments of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4138  
4139         Argument precedence for facecolors: 
4140  
4141         - c (if not None) 
4142         - kwargs['facecolors'] 
4143         - kwargs['facecolor'] 
4144         - kwargs['color'] (==kwcolor) 
4145         - 'b' if in classic mode else the result of ``get_next_color_func()`` 
4146  
4147         Argument precedence for edgecolors: 
4148  
4149         - edgecolors (is an explicit kw argument in scatter()) 
4150         - kwargs['edgecolor'] 
4151         - kwargs['color'] (==kwcolor) 
4152         - 'face' if not in classic mode else None 
4153  
4154         Parameters 
4155         ---------- 
4156         c : color or sequence or sequence of color or None 
4157             See argument description of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4158         edgecolors : color or sequence of color or {'face', 'none'} or None 
4159             See argument description of `.Axes.scatter`. 
4160         kwargs : dict 
4161             Additional kwargs. If these keys exist, we pop and process them: 
4162             'facecolors', 'facecolor', 'edgecolor', 'color' 
4163             Note: The dict is modified by this function. 
4164         xsize : int 
4165             The size of the x and y arrays passed to `.Axes.scatter`. 
4166         get_next_color_func : callable 
4167             A callable that returns a color. This color is used as facecolor 
4168             if no other color is provided. 
4169  
4170             Note, that this is a function rather than a fixed color value to 
4171             support conditional evaluation of the next color.  As of the 
4172             current implementation obtaining the next color from the 
4173             property cycle advances the cycle. This must only happen if we 
4174             actually use the color, which will only be decided within this 
4175             method. 
4176  
4177         Returns 
4178         ------- 
4179         c 
4180             The input *c* if it was not *None*, else a color derived from the 
4181             other inputs or defaults. 
4182         colors : array(N, 4) or None 
4183             The facecolors as RGBA values, or *None* if a colormap is used. 
4184         edgecolors 
4185             The edgecolor. 
4186  
4187         """ 
4188         facecolors = kwargs.pop('facecolors', None) 
4189         facecolors = kwargs.pop('facecolor', facecolors) 
4190         edgecolors = kwargs.pop('edgecolor', edgecolors) 
4191  
4192         kwcolor = kwargs.pop('color', None) 
4193  
4194         if kwcolor is not None and c is not None: 
4195             raise ValueError("Supply a 'c' argument or a 'color'" 
4196                              " kwarg but not both; they differ but" 
4197                              " their functionalities overlap.") 
4198  
4199         if kwcolor is not None: 
4200             try: 
4201                 mcolors.to_rgba_array(kwcolor) 
4202             except ValueError: 
4203                 raise ValueError( 
4204                     "'color' kwarg must be an color or sequence of color " 
4205                     "specs.  For a sequence of values to be color-mapped, use " 
4206                     "the 'c' argument instead.") 
4207             if edgecolors is None: 
4208                 edgecolors = kwcolor 
4209             if facecolors is None: 
4210                 facecolors = kwcolor 
4211  
4212         if edgecolors is None and not rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
4213             edgecolors = rcParams['scatter.edgecolors'] 
4214  
4215         c_was_none = c is None 
4216         if c is None: 
4217             c = (facecolors if facecolors is not None 
4218                  else "b" if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] 
4219                  else get_next_color_func()) 
4220         c_is_string_or_strings = ( 
4221             isinstance(c, str) 
4222             or (isinstance(c, collections.abc.Iterable) and len(c) > 0 
4223                 and isinstance(cbook.safe_first_element(c), str))) 
4224  
4225         def invalid_shape_exception(csize, xsize): 
4226             return ValueError( 
4227                 f"'c' argument has {csize} elements, which is inconsistent " 
4228                 f"with 'x' and 'y' with size {xsize}.") 
4229  
4230         c_is_mapped = False  # Unless proven otherwise below. 
4231         valid_shape = True  # Unless proven otherwise below. 
4232         if not c_was_none and kwcolor is None and not c_is_string_or_strings: 
4233             try:  # First, does 'c' look suitable for value-mapping? 
4234                 c = np.asanyarray(c, dtype=float) 
4235             except ValueError: 
4236                 pass  # Failed to convert to float array; must be color specs. 
4237             else: 
4238                 # If c can be either mapped values or a RGB(A) color, prefer 
4239                 # the former if shapes match, the latter otherwise. 
4240                 if c.size == xsize: 
4241                     c = c.ravel() 
4242                     c_is_mapped = True 
4243                 else:  # Wrong size; it must not be intended for mapping. 
4244                     if c.shape in ((3,), (4,)): 
4245                         _log.warning( 
4246                             "'c' argument looks like a single numeric RGB or " 
4247                             "RGBA sequence, which should be avoided as value-" 
4248                             "mapping will have precedence in case its length " 
4249                             "matches with 'x' & 'y'.  Please use a 2-D array " 
4250                             "with a single row if you really want to specify " 
4251                             "the same RGB or RGBA value for all points.") 
4252                     valid_shape = False 
4253         if not c_is_mapped: 
4254             try:  # Is 'c' acceptable as PathCollection facecolors? 
4255                 colors = mcolors.to_rgba_array(c) 
4256             except ValueError: 
4257                 if not valid_shape: 
4258                     raise invalid_shape_exception(c.size, xsize) 
4259                 # Both the mapping *and* the RGBA conversion failed: pretty 
4260                 # severe failure => one may appreciate a verbose feedback. 
4261                 raise ValueError( 
4262                     f"'c' argument must be a color, a sequence of colors, or " 
4263                     f"a sequence of numbers, not {c}") 
4264             else: 
4265                 if len(colors) not in (0, 1, xsize): 
4266                     # NB: remember that a single color is also acceptable. 
4267                     # Besides *colors* will be an empty array if c == 'none'. 
4268                     raise invalid_shape_exception(len(colors), xsize) 
4269         else: 
4270             colors = None  # use cmap, norm after collection is created 
4271         return c, colors, edgecolors 
4272  
4273     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y", "s", "linewidths", 
4274                                      "edgecolors", "c", "facecolor", 
4275                                      "facecolors", "color"], 
4276                       label_namer="y") 
4277     @cbook._delete_parameter("3.2", "verts") 
4278     def scatter(self, x, y, s=None, c=None, marker=None, cmap=None, norm=None, 
4279                 vmin=None, vmax=None, alpha=None, linewidths=None, 
4280                 verts=None, edgecolors=None, *, plotnonfinite=False, 
4281                 **kwargs): 
4282         """ 
4283         A scatter plot of *y* vs. *x* with varying marker size and/or color. 
4284  
4285         Parameters 
4286         ---------- 
4287         x, y : scalar or array-like, shape (n, ) 
4288             The data positions. 
4289  
4290         s : scalar or array-like, shape (n, ), optional 
4291             The marker size in points**2. 
4292             Default is ``rcParams['lines.markersize'] ** 2``. 
4293  
4294         c : color, sequence, or sequence of colors, optional 
4295             The marker color. Possible values: 
4296  
4297             - A single color format string. 
4298             - A sequence of colors of length n. 
4299             - A scalar or sequence of n numbers to be mapped to colors using 
4300               *cmap* and *norm*. 
4301             - A 2-D array in which the rows are RGB or RGBA. 
4302  
4303             Note that *c* should not be a single numeric RGB or RGBA sequence 
4304             because that is indistinguishable from an array of values to be 
4305             colormapped. If you want to specify the same RGB or RGBA value for 
4306             all points, use a 2-D array with a single row.  Otherwise, value- 
4307             matching will have precedence in case of a size matching with *x* 
4308             and *y*. 
4309  
4310             Defaults to ``None``. In that case the marker color is determined 
4311             by the value of ``color``, ``facecolor`` or ``facecolors``. In case 
4312             those are not specified or ``None``, the marker color is determined 
4313             by the next color of the ``Axes``' current "shape and fill" color 
4314             cycle. This cycle defaults to :rc:`axes.prop_cycle`. 
4315  
4316         marker : `~matplotlib.markers.MarkerStyle`, optional 
4317             The marker style. *marker* can be either an instance of the class 
4318             or the text shorthand for a particular marker. 
4319             Defaults to ``None``, in which case it takes the value of 
4320             :rc:`scatter.marker` = 'o'. 
4321             See `~matplotlib.markers` for more information about marker styles. 
4322  
4323         cmap : `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
4324             A `.Colormap` instance or registered colormap name. *cmap* is only 
4325             used if *c* is an array of floats. If ``None``, defaults to 
4326             :rc:`image.cmap`. 
4327  
4328         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, default: None 
4329             A `.Normalize` instance is used to scale luminance data to 0, 1. 
4330             *norm* is only used if *c* is an array of floats. If *None*, use 
4331             the default `.colors.Normalize`. 
4332  
4333         vmin, vmax : scalar, default: None 
4334             *vmin* and *vmax* are used in conjunction with *norm* to normalize 
4335             luminance data. If None, the respective min and max of the color 
4336             array is used. *vmin* and *vmax* are ignored if you pass a *norm* 
4337             instance. 
4338  
4339         alpha : scalar, default: None 
4340             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
4341  
4342         linewidths : scalar or array-like, default: None 
4343             The linewidth of the marker edges. Note: The default *edgecolors* 
4344             is 'face'. You may want to change this as well. 
4345             If *None*, defaults to :rc:`lines.linewidth`. 
4346  
4347         edgecolors : {'face', 'none', *None*} or color or sequence of color, \ 
4348 optional. 
4349             The edge color of the marker. Possible values: 
4350  
4351             - 'face': The edge color will always be the same as the face color. 
4352             - 'none': No patch boundary will be drawn. 
4353             - A color or sequence of colors. 
4354  
4355             Defaults to ``None``, in which case it takes the value of 
4356             :rc:`scatter.edgecolors` = 'face'. 
4357  
4358             For non-filled markers, the *edgecolors* kwarg is ignored and 
4359             forced to 'face' internally. 
4360  
4361         plotnonfinite : bool, default: False 
4362             Set to plot points with nonfinite *c*, in conjunction with 
4363             `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap.set_bad`. 
4364  
4365         Returns 
4366         ------- 
4367         paths : `~matplotlib.collections.PathCollection` 
4368  
4369         Other Parameters 
4370         ---------------- 
4371         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.collections.Collection` properties 
4372  
4373         See Also 
4374         -------- 
4375         plot : To plot scatter plots when markers are identical in size and 
4376             color. 
4377  
4378         Notes 
4379         ----- 
4380         * The `.plot` function will be faster for scatterplots where markers 
4381           don't vary in size or color. 
4382  
4383         * Any or all of *x*, *y*, *s*, and *c* may be masked arrays, in which 
4384           case all masks will be combined and only unmasked points will be 
4385           plotted. 
4386  
4387         * Fundamentally, scatter works with 1-D arrays; *x*, *y*, *s*, and *c* 
4388           may be input as N-D arrays, but within scatter they will be 
4389           flattened. The exception is *c*, which will be flattened only if its 
4390           size matches the size of *x* and *y*. 
4391  
4392         """ 
4393         # Process **kwargs to handle aliases, conflicts with explicit kwargs: 
4394  
4395         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
4396         x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
4397         y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
4398  
4399         # np.ma.ravel yields an ndarray, not a masked array, 
4400         # unless its argument is a masked array. 
4401         x = np.ma.ravel(x) 
4402         y = np.ma.ravel(y) 
4403         if x.size != y.size: 
4404             raise ValueError("x and y must be the same size") 
4405  
4406         if s is None: 
4407             s = (20 if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'] else 
4408                  rcParams['lines.markersize'] ** 2.0) 
4409         s = np.ma.ravel(s) 
4410         if len(s) not in (1, x.size): 
4411             raise ValueError("s must be a scalar, or the same size as x and y") 
4412  
4413         c, colors, edgecolors = \ 
4414             self._parse_scatter_color_args( 
4415                 c, edgecolors, kwargs, x.size, 
4416                 get_next_color_func=self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color) 
4417  
4418         if plotnonfinite and colors is None: 
4419             c = np.ma.masked_invalid(c) 
4420             x, y, s, edgecolors, linewidths = \ 
4421                 cbook._combine_masks(x, y, s, edgecolors, linewidths) 
4422         else: 
4423             x, y, s, c, colors, edgecolors, linewidths = \ 
4424                 cbook._combine_masks( 
4425                     x, y, s, c, colors, edgecolors, linewidths) 
4426  
4427         scales = s   # Renamed for readability below. 
4428  
4429         # load default marker from rcParams 
4430         if marker is None: 
4431             marker = rcParams['scatter.marker'] 
4432  
4433         if isinstance(marker, mmarkers.MarkerStyle): 
4434             marker_obj = marker 
4435         else: 
4436             marker_obj = mmarkers.MarkerStyle(marker) 
4437  
4438         path = marker_obj.get_path().transformed( 
4439             marker_obj.get_transform()) 
4440         if not marker_obj.is_filled(): 
4441             edgecolors = 'face' 
4442             linewidths = rcParams['lines.linewidth'] 
4443  
4444         offsets = np.ma.column_stack([x, y]) 
4445  
4446         collection = mcoll.PathCollection( 
4447                 (path,), scales, 
4448                 facecolors=colors, 
4449                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4450                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4451                 offsets=offsets, 
4452                 transOffset=kwargs.pop('transform', self.transData), 
4453                 alpha=alpha 
4454                 ) 
4455         collection.set_transform(mtransforms.IdentityTransform()) 
4456         collection.update(kwargs) 
4457  
4458         if colors is None: 
4459             collection.set_array(c) 
4460             collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
4461             collection.set_norm(norm) 
4462  
4463             if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
4464                 collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
4465             else: 
4466                 collection.autoscale_None() 
4467  
4468         # Classic mode only: 
4469         # ensure there are margins to allow for the 
4470         # finite size of the symbols.  In v2.x, margins 
4471         # are present by default, so we disable this 
4472         # scatter-specific override. 
4473         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
4474             if self._xmargin < 0.05 and x.size > 0: 
4475                 self.set_xmargin(0.05) 
4476             if self._ymargin < 0.05 and x.size > 0: 
4477                 self.set_ymargin(0.05) 
4478  
4479         self.add_collection(collection) 
4480         self._request_autoscale_view() 
4481  
4482         return collection
