4484     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y") 
4485     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
4486     def hexbin(self, x, y, C=None, gridsize=100, bins=None, 
4487                xscale='linear', yscale='linear', extent=None, 
4488                cmap=None, norm=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, 
4489                alpha=None, linewidths=None, edgecolors='face', 
4490                reduce_C_function=np.mean, mincnt=None, marginals=False, 
4491                **kwargs): 
4492         """ 
4493         Make a 2D hexagonal binning plot of points *x*, *y*. 
4494  
4495         If *C* is *None*, the value of the hexagon is determined by the number 
4496         of points in the hexagon. Otherwise, *C* specifies values at the 
4497         coordinate (x[i], y[i]). For each hexagon, these values are reduced 
4498         using *reduce_C_function*. 
4499  
4500         Parameters 
4501         ---------- 
4502         x, y : array-like 
4503             The data positions. *x* and *y* must be of the same length. 
4504  
4505         C : array-like, optional 
4506             If given, these values are accumulated in the bins. Otherwise, 
4507             every point has a value of 1. Must be of the same length as *x* 
4508             and *y*. 
4509  
4510         gridsize : int or (int, int), default: 100 
4511             If a single int, the number of hexagons in the *x*-direction. 
4512             The number of hexagons in the *y*-direction is chosen such that 
4513             the hexagons are approximately regular. 
4514  
4515             Alternatively, if a tuple (*nx*, *ny*), the number of hexagons 
4516             in the *x*-direction and the *y*-direction. 
4517  
4518         bins : 'log' or int or sequence, default: None 
4519             Discretization of the hexagon values. 
4520  
4521             - If *None*, no binning is applied; the color of each hexagon 
4522               directly corresponds to its count value. 
4523             - If 'log', use a logarithmic scale for the color map. 
4524               Internally, :math:`log_{10}(i+1)` is used to determine the 
4525               hexagon color. This is equivalent to ``norm=LogNorm()``. 
4526             - If an integer, divide the counts in the specified number 
4527               of bins, and color the hexagons accordingly. 
4528             - If a sequence of values, the values of the lower bound of 
4529               the bins to be used. 
4530  
4531         xscale : {'linear', 'log'}, default: 'linear' 
4532             Use a linear or log10 scale on the horizontal axis. 
4533  
4534         yscale : {'linear', 'log'}, default: 'linear' 
4535             Use a linear or log10 scale on the vertical axis. 
4536  
4537         mincnt : int > 0, default: *None* 
4538             If not *None*, only display cells with more than *mincnt* 
4539             number of points in the cell. 
4540  
4541         marginals : bool, default: *False* 
4542             If marginals is *True*, plot the marginal density as 
4543             colormapped rectangles along the bottom of the x-axis and 
4544             left of the y-axis. 
4545  
4546         extent : float, default: *None* 
4547             The limits of the bins. The default assigns the limits 
4548             based on *gridsize*, *x*, *y*, *xscale* and *yscale*. 
4549  
4550             If *xscale* or *yscale* is set to 'log', the limits are 
4551             expected to be the exponent for a power of 10. E.g. for 
4552             x-limits of 1 and 50 in 'linear' scale and y-limits 
4553             of 10 and 1000 in 'log' scale, enter (1, 50, 1, 3). 
4554  
4555             Order of scalars is (left, right, bottom, top). 
4556  
4557         Other Parameters 
4558         ---------------- 
4559         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
4560             The Colormap instance or registered colormap name used to map 
4561             the bin values to colors. Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
4562  
4563         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
4564             The Normalize instance scales the bin values to the canonical 
4565             colormap range [0, 1] for mapping to colors. By default, the data 
4566             range is mapped to the colorbar range using linear scaling. 
4567  
4568         vmin, vmax : float, default: None 
4569             The colorbar range. If *None*, suitable min/max values are 
4570             automatically chosen by the `~.Normalize` instance (defaults to 
4571             the respective min/max values of the bins in case of the default 
4572             linear scaling). This is ignored if *norm* is given. 
4573  
4574         alpha : float between 0 and 1, optional 
4575             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
4576  
4577         linewidths : float, default: *None* 
4578             If *None*, defaults to 1.0. 
4579  
4580         edgecolors : {'face', 'none', *None*} or color, default: 'face' 
4581             The color of the hexagon edges. Possible values are: 
4582  
4583             - 'face': Draw the edges in the same color as the fill color. 
4584             - 'none': No edges are drawn. This can sometimes lead to unsightly 
4585               unpainted pixels between the hexagons. 
4586             - *None*: Draw outlines in the default color. 
4587             - An explicit color. 
4588  
4589         reduce_C_function : callable, default: `numpy.mean` 
4590             The function to aggregate *C* within the bins. It is ignored if 
4591             *C* is not given. This must have the signature:: 
4592  
4593                 def reduce_C_function(C: array) -> float 
4594  
4595             Commonly used functions are: 
4596  
4597             - `numpy.mean`: average of the points 
4598             - `numpy.sum`: integral of the point values 
4599             - `numpy.max`: value taken from the largest point 
4600  
4601         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.collections.PolyCollection` properties 
4602             All other keyword arguments are passed on to `.PolyCollection`: 
4603  
4604             %(PolyCollection)s 
4605  
4606         Returns 
4607         ------- 
4608         polycollection : `~matplotlib.collections.PolyCollection` 
4609             A `.PolyCollection` defining the hexagonal bins. 
4610  
4611             - `.PolyCollection.get_offset` contains a Mx2 array containing 
4612               the x, y positions of the M hexagon centers. 
4613             - `.PolyCollection.get_array` contains the values of the M 
4614               hexagons. 
4615  
4616             If *marginals* is *True*, horizontal 
4617             bar and vertical bar (both PolyCollections) will be attached 
4618             to the return collection as attributes *hbar* and *vbar*. 
4619  
4620         """ 
4621         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kwargs) 
4622  
4623         x, y, C = cbook.delete_masked_points(x, y, C) 
4624  
4625         # Set the size of the hexagon grid 
4626         if np.iterable(gridsize): 
4627             nx, ny = gridsize 
4628         else: 
4629             nx = gridsize 
4630             ny = int(nx / math.sqrt(3)) 
4631         # Count the number of data in each hexagon 
4632         x = np.array(x, float) 
4633         y = np.array(y, float) 
4634         if xscale == 'log': 
4635             if np.any(x <= 0.0): 
4636                 raise ValueError("x contains non-positive values, so can not" 
4637                                  " be log-scaled") 
4638             x = np.log10(x) 
4639         if yscale == 'log': 
4640             if np.any(y <= 0.0): 
4641                 raise ValueError("y contains non-positive values, so can not" 
4642                                  " be log-scaled") 
4643             y = np.log10(y) 
4644         if extent is not None: 
4645             xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax = extent 
4646         else: 
4647             xmin, xmax = (np.min(x), np.max(x)) if len(x) else (0, 1) 
4648             ymin, ymax = (np.min(y), np.max(y)) if len(y) else (0, 1) 
4649  
4650             # to avoid issues with singular data, expand the min/max pairs 
4651             xmin, xmax = mtransforms.nonsingular(xmin, xmax, expander=0.1) 
4652             ymin, ymax = mtransforms.nonsingular(ymin, ymax, expander=0.1) 
4653  
4654         # In the x-direction, the hexagons exactly cover the region from 
4655         # xmin to xmax. Need some padding to avoid roundoff errors. 
4656         padding = 1.e-9 * (xmax - xmin) 
4657         xmin -= padding 
4658         xmax += padding 
4659         sx = (xmax - xmin) / nx 
4660         sy = (ymax - ymin) / ny 
4661  
4662         if marginals: 
4663             xorig = x.copy() 
4664             yorig = y.copy() 
4665  
4666         x = (x - xmin) / sx 
4667         y = (y - ymin) / sy 
4668         ix1 = np.round(x).astype(int) 
4669         iy1 = np.round(y).astype(int) 
4670         ix2 = np.floor(x).astype(int) 
4671         iy2 = np.floor(y).astype(int) 
4672  
4673         nx1 = nx + 1 
4674         ny1 = ny + 1 
4675         nx2 = nx 
4676         ny2 = ny 
4677         n = nx1 * ny1 + nx2 * ny2 
4678  
4679         d1 = (x - ix1) ** 2 + 3.0 * (y - iy1) ** 2 
4680         d2 = (x - ix2 - 0.5) ** 2 + 3.0 * (y - iy2 - 0.5) ** 2 
4681         bdist = (d1 < d2) 
4682         if C is None: 
4683             lattice1 = np.zeros((nx1, ny1)) 
4684             lattice2 = np.zeros((nx2, ny2)) 
4685             c1 = (0 <= ix1) & (ix1 < nx1) & (0 <= iy1) & (iy1 < ny1) & bdist 
4686             c2 = (0 <= ix2) & (ix2 < nx2) & (0 <= iy2) & (iy2 < ny2) & ~bdist 
4687             np.add.at(lattice1, (ix1[c1], iy1[c1]), 1) 
4688             np.add.at(lattice2, (ix2[c2], iy2[c2]), 1) 
4689             if mincnt is not None: 
4690                 lattice1[lattice1 < mincnt] = np.nan 
4691                 lattice2[lattice2 < mincnt] = np.nan 
4692             accum = np.concatenate([lattice1.ravel(), lattice2.ravel()]) 
4693             good_idxs = ~np.isnan(accum) 
4694  
4695         else: 
4696             if mincnt is None: 
4697                 mincnt = 0 
4698  
4699             # create accumulation arrays 
4700             lattice1 = np.empty((nx1, ny1), dtype=object) 
4701             for i in range(nx1): 
4702                 for j in range(ny1): 
4703                     lattice1[i, j] = [] 
4704             lattice2 = np.empty((nx2, ny2), dtype=object) 
4705             for i in range(nx2): 
4706                 for j in range(ny2): 
4707                     lattice2[i, j] = [] 
4708  
4709             for i in range(len(x)): 
4710                 if bdist[i]: 
4711                     if 0 <= ix1[i] < nx1 and 0 <= iy1[i] < ny1: 
4712                         lattice1[ix1[i], iy1[i]].append(C[i]) 
4713                 else: 
4714                     if 0 <= ix2[i] < nx2 and 0 <= iy2[i] < ny2: 
4715                         lattice2[ix2[i], iy2[i]].append(C[i]) 
4716  
4717             for i in range(nx1): 
4718                 for j in range(ny1): 
4719                     vals = lattice1[i, j] 
4720                     if len(vals) > mincnt: 
4721                         lattice1[i, j] = reduce_C_function(vals) 
4722                     else: 
4723                         lattice1[i, j] = np.nan 
4724             for i in range(nx2): 
4725                 for j in range(ny2): 
4726                     vals = lattice2[i, j] 
4727                     if len(vals) > mincnt: 
4728                         lattice2[i, j] = reduce_C_function(vals) 
4729                     else: 
4730                         lattice2[i, j] = np.nan 
4731  
4732             accum = np.hstack((lattice1.astype(float).ravel(), 
4733                                lattice2.astype(float).ravel())) 
4734             good_idxs = ~np.isnan(accum) 
4735  
4736         offsets = np.zeros((n, 2), float) 
4737         offsets[:nx1 * ny1, 0] = np.repeat(np.arange(nx1), ny1) 
4738         offsets[:nx1 * ny1, 1] = np.tile(np.arange(ny1), nx1) 
4739         offsets[nx1 * ny1:, 0] = np.repeat(np.arange(nx2) + 0.5, ny2) 
4740         offsets[nx1 * ny1:, 1] = np.tile(np.arange(ny2), nx2) + 0.5 
4741         offsets[:, 0] *= sx 
4742         offsets[:, 1] *= sy 
4743         offsets[:, 0] += xmin 
4744         offsets[:, 1] += ymin 
4745         # remove accumulation bins with no data 
4746         offsets = offsets[good_idxs, :] 
4747         accum = accum[good_idxs] 
4748  
4749         polygon = [sx, sy / 3] * np.array( 
4750             [[.5, -.5], [.5, .5], [0., 1.], [-.5, .5], [-.5, -.5], [0., -1.]]) 
4751  
4752         if linewidths is None: 
4753             linewidths = [1.0] 
4754  
4755         if xscale == 'log' or yscale == 'log': 
4756             polygons = np.expand_dims(polygon, 0) + np.expand_dims(offsets, 1) 
4757             if xscale == 'log': 
4758                 polygons[:, :, 0] = 10.0 ** polygons[:, :, 0] 
4759                 xmin = 10.0 ** xmin 
4760                 xmax = 10.0 ** xmax 
4761                 self.set_xscale(xscale) 
4762             if yscale == 'log': 
4763                 polygons[:, :, 1] = 10.0 ** polygons[:, :, 1] 
4764                 ymin = 10.0 ** ymin 
4765                 ymax = 10.0 ** ymax 
4766                 self.set_yscale(yscale) 
4767             collection = mcoll.PolyCollection( 
4768                 polygons, 
4769                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4770                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4771                 ) 
4772         else: 
4773             collection = mcoll.PolyCollection( 
4774                 [polygon], 
4775                 edgecolors=edgecolors, 
4776                 linewidths=linewidths, 
4777                 offsets=offsets, 
4778                 transOffset=mtransforms.IdentityTransform(), 
4779                 offset_position="data" 
4780                 ) 
4781  
4782         # Set normalizer if bins is 'log' 
4783         if bins == 'log': 
4784             if norm is not None: 
4785                 cbook._warn_external("Only one of 'bins' and 'norm' " 
4786                                      "arguments can be supplied, ignoring " 
4787                                      "bins={}".format(bins)) 
4788             else: 
4789                 norm = mcolors.LogNorm() 
4790             bins = None 
4791  
4792         if isinstance(norm, mcolors.LogNorm): 
4793             if (accum == 0).any(): 
4794                 # make sure we have no zeros 
4795                 accum += 1 
4796  
4797         # autoscale the norm with curren accum values if it hasn't 
4798         # been set 
4799         if norm is not None: 
4800             if norm.vmin is None and norm.vmax is None: 
4801                 norm.autoscale(accum) 
4802  
4803         if bins is not None: 
4804             if not np.iterable(bins): 
4805                 minimum, maximum = min(accum), max(accum) 
4806                 bins -= 1  # one less edge than bins 
4807                 bins = minimum + (maximum - minimum) * np.arange(bins) / bins 
4808             bins = np.sort(bins) 
4809             accum = bins.searchsorted(accum) 
4810  
4811         collection.set_array(accum) 
4812         collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
4813         collection.set_norm(norm) 
4814         collection.set_alpha(alpha) 
4815         collection.update(kwargs) 
4816  
4817         if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
4818             collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
4819         else: 
4820             collection.autoscale_None() 
4821  
4822         corners = ((xmin, ymin), (xmax, ymax)) 
4823         self.update_datalim(corners) 
4824         self._request_autoscale_view(tight=True) 
4825  
4826         # add the collection last 
4827         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
4828         if not marginals: 
4829             return collection 
4830  
4831         if C is None: 
4832             C = np.ones(len(x)) 
4833  
4834         def coarse_bin(x, y, coarse): 
4835             ind = coarse.searchsorted(x).clip(0, len(coarse) - 1) 
4836             mus = np.zeros(len(coarse)) 
4837             for i in range(len(coarse)): 
4838                 yi = y[ind == i] 
4839                 if len(yi) > 0: 
4840                     mu = reduce_C_function(yi) 
4841                 else: 
4842                     mu = np.nan 
4843                 mus[i] = mu 
4844             return mus 
4845  
4846         coarse = np.linspace(xmin, xmax, gridsize) 
4847  
4848         xcoarse = coarse_bin(xorig, C, coarse) 
4849         valid = ~np.isnan(xcoarse) 
4850         verts, values = [], [] 
4851         for i, val in enumerate(xcoarse): 
4852             thismin = coarse[i] 
4853             if i < len(coarse) - 1: 
4854                 thismax = coarse[i + 1] 
4855             else: 
4856                 thismax = thismin + np.diff(coarse)[-1] 
4857  
4858             if not valid[i]: 
4859                 continue 
4860  
4861             verts.append([(thismin, 0), 
4862                           (thismin, 0.05), 
4863                           (thismax, 0.05), 
4864                           (thismax, 0)]) 
4865             values.append(val) 
4866  
4867         values = np.array(values) 
4868         trans = self.get_xaxis_transform(which='grid') 
4869  
4870         hbar = mcoll.PolyCollection(verts, transform=trans, edgecolors='face') 
4871  
4872         hbar.set_array(values) 
4873         hbar.set_cmap(cmap) 
4874         hbar.set_norm(norm) 
4875         hbar.set_alpha(alpha) 
4876         hbar.update(kwargs) 
4877         self.add_collection(hbar, autolim=False) 
4878  
4879         coarse = np.linspace(ymin, ymax, gridsize) 
4880         ycoarse = coarse_bin(yorig, C, coarse) 
4881         valid = ~np.isnan(ycoarse) 
4882         verts, values = [], [] 
4883         for i, val in enumerate(ycoarse): 
4884             thismin = coarse[i] 
4885             if i < len(coarse) - 1: 
4886                 thismax = coarse[i + 1] 
4887             else: 
4888                 thismax = thismin + np.diff(coarse)[-1] 
4889             if not valid[i]: 
4890                 continue 
4891             verts.append([(0, thismin), (0.0, thismax), 
4892                           (0.05, thismax), (0.05, thismin)]) 
4893             values.append(val) 
4894  
4895         values = np.array(values) 
4896  
4897         trans = self.get_yaxis_transform(which='grid') 
4898  
4899         vbar = mcoll.PolyCollection(verts, transform=trans, edgecolors='face') 
4900         vbar.set_array(values) 
4901         vbar.set_cmap(cmap) 
4902         vbar.set_norm(norm) 
4903         vbar.set_alpha(alpha) 
4904         vbar.update(kwargs) 
4905         self.add_collection(vbar, autolim=False) 
4906  
4907         collection.hbar = hbar 
4908         collection.vbar = vbar 
4909  
4910         def on_changed(collection): 
4911             hbar.set_cmap(collection.get_cmap()) 
4912             hbar.set_clim(collection.get_clim()) 
4913             vbar.set_cmap(collection.get_cmap()) 
4914             vbar.set_clim(collection.get_clim()) 
4915  
4916         collection.callbacksSM.connect('changed', on_changed) 
4917  
4918         return collection

4921     def arrow(self, x, y, dx, dy, **kwargs): 
4922         """ 
4923         Add an arrow to the axes. 
4924  
4925         This draws an arrow from ``(x, y)`` to ``(x+dx, y+dy)``. 
4926  
4927         Parameters 
4928         ---------- 
4929         x, y : float 
4930             The x and y coordinates of the arrow base. 
4931  
4932         dx, dy : float 
4933             The length of the arrow along x and y direction. 
4934  
4935         %(FancyArrow)s 
4936  
4937         Returns 
4938         ------- 
4939         arrow : `.FancyArrow` 
4940             The created `.FancyArrow` object. 
4941  
4942         Notes 
4943         ----- 
4944         The resulting arrow is affected by the axes aspect ratio and limits. 
4945         This may produce an arrow whose head is not square with its stem. To 
4946         create an arrow whose head is square with its stem, 
4947         use :meth:`annotate` for example: 
4948  
4949         >>> ax.annotate("", xy=(0.5, 0.5), xytext=(0, 0), 
4950         ...             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->")) 
4951  
4952         """ 
4953         # Strip away units for the underlying patch since units 
4954         # do not make sense to most patch-like code 
4955         x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
4956         y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
4957         dx = self.convert_xunits(dx) 
4958         dy = self.convert_yunits(dy) 
4959  
4960         a = mpatches.FancyArrow(x, y, dx, dy, **kwargs) 
4961         self.add_artist(a) 
4962         return a

4970     # Handle units for x and y, if they've been passed 
4971     def _quiver_units(self, args, kw): 
4972         if len(args) > 3: 
4973             x, y = args[0:2] 
4974             self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y, kwargs=kw) 
4975             x = self.convert_xunits(x) 
4976             y = self.convert_yunits(y) 
4977             return (x, y) + args[2:] 
4978         return args

5008     # Uses a custom implementation of data-kwarg handling in 
5009     # _process_plot_var_args. 
5010     def fill(self, *args, data=None, **kwargs): 
5011         """ 
5012         Plot filled polygons. 
5013  
5014         Parameters 
5015         ---------- 
5016         *args : sequence of x, y, [color] 
5017             Each polygon is defined by the lists of *x* and *y* positions of 
5018             its nodes, optionally followed by a *color* specifier. See 
5019             :mod:`matplotlib.colors` for supported color specifiers. The 
5020             standard color cycle is used for polygons without a color 
5021             specifier. 
5022  
5023             You can plot multiple polygons by providing multiple *x*, *y*, 
5024             *[color]* groups. 
5025  
5026             For example, each of the following is legal:: 
5027  
5028                 ax.fill(x, y)                    # a polygon with default color 
5029                 ax.fill(x, y, "b")               # a blue polygon 
5030                 ax.fill(x, y, x2, y2)            # two polygons 
5031                 ax.fill(x, y, "b", x2, y2, "r")  # a blue and a red polygon 
5032  
5033         data : indexable object, optional 
5034             An object with labelled data. If given, provide the label names to 
5035             plot in *x* and *y*, e.g.:: 
5036  
5037                 ax.fill("time", "signal", 
5038                         data={"time": [0, 1, 2], "signal": [0, 1, 0]}) 
5039  
5040         Returns 
5041         ------- 
5042         a list of :class:`~matplotlib.patches.Polygon` 
5043  
5044         Other Parameters 
5045         ---------------- 
5046         **kwargs : :class:`~matplotlib.patches.Polygon` properties 
5047  
5048         Notes 
5049         ----- 
5050         Use :meth:`fill_between` if you would like to fill the region between 
5051         two curves. 
5052         """ 
5053         # For compatibility(!), get aliases from Line2D rather than Patch. 
5054         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D) 
5055         # _get_patches_for_fill returns a generator, convert it to a list. 
5056         patches = [*self._get_patches_for_fill(*args, data=data, **kwargs)] 
5057         for poly in patches: 
5058             self.add_patch(poly) 
5059         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5060         return patches

5062     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y1", "y2", "where"]) 
5063     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
5064     def fill_between(self, x, y1, y2=0, where=None, interpolate=False, 
5065                      step=None, **kwargs): 
5066         """ 
5067         Fill the area between two horizontal curves. 
5068  
5069         The curves are defined by the points (*x*, *y1*) and (*x*, *y2*). This 
5070         creates one or multiple polygons describing the filled area. 
5071  
5072         You may exclude some horizontal sections from filling using *where*. 
5073  
5074         By default, the edges connect the given points directly. Use *step* if 
5075         the filling should be a step function, i.e. constant in between *x*. 
5076  
5077  
5078         Parameters 
5079         ---------- 
5080         x : array (length N) 
5081             The x coordinates of the nodes defining the curves. 
5082  
5083         y1 : array (length N) or scalar 
5084             The y coordinates of the nodes defining the first curve. 
5085  
5086         y2 : array (length N) or scalar, default: 0 
5087             The y coordinates of the nodes defining the second curve. 
5088  
5089         where : array of bool (length N), optional 
5090             Define *where* to exclude some horizontal regions from being 
5091             filled. The filled regions are defined by the coordinates 
5092             ``x[where]``.  More precisely, fill between ``x[i]`` and ``x[i+1]`` 
5093             if ``where[i] and where[i+1]``.  Note that this definition implies 
5094             that an isolated *True* value between two *False* values in 
5095             *where* will not result in filling.  Both sides of the *True* 
5096             position remain unfilled due to the adjacent *False* values. 
5097  
5098         interpolate : bool, default: False 
5099             This option is only relevant if *where* is used and the two curves 
5100             are crossing each other. 
5101  
5102             Semantically, *where* is often used for *y1* > *y2* or similar. 
5103             By default, the nodes of the polygon defining the filled region 
5104             will only be placed at the positions in the *x* array.  Such a 
5105             polygon cannot describe the above semantics close to the 
5106             intersection.  The x-sections containing the intersection are 
5107             simply clipped. 
5108  
5109             Setting *interpolate* to *True* will calculate the actual 
5110             intersection point and extend the filled region up to this point. 
5111  
5112         step : {'pre', 'post', 'mid'}, optional 
5113             Define *step* if the filling should be a step function, 
5114             i.e. constant in between *x*. The value determines where the 
5115             step will occur: 
5116  
5117             - 'pre': The y value is continued constantly to the left from 
5118               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``(x[i-1], x[i]]`` has the 
5119               value ``y[i]``. 
5120             - 'post': The y value is continued constantly to the right from 
5121               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``[x[i], x[i+1])`` has the 
5122               value ``y[i]``. 
5123             - 'mid': Steps occur half-way between the *x* positions. 
5124  
5125         Other Parameters 
5126         ---------------- 
5127         **kwargs 
5128             All other keyword arguments are passed on to `.PolyCollection`. 
5129             They control the `.Polygon` properties: 
5130  
5131             %(PolyCollection)s 
5132  
5133         Returns 
5134         ------- 
5135         `.PolyCollection` 
5136             A `.PolyCollection` containing the plotted polygons. 
5137  
5138         See Also 
5139         -------- 
5140         fill_betweenx : Fill between two sets of x-values. 
5141  
5142         Notes 
5143         ----- 
5144         .. [notes section required to get data note injection right] 
5145  
5146         """ 
5147         if not rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
5148             kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mcoll.Collection) 
5149             if not any(c in kwargs for c in ('color', 'facecolor')): 
5150                 kwargs['facecolor'] = \ 
5151                     self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color() 
5152  
5153         # Handle united data, such as dates 
5154         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x, ydata=y1, kwargs=kwargs) 
5155         self._process_unit_info(ydata=y2) 
5156  
5157         # Convert the arrays so we can work with them 
5158         x = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_xunits(x)) 
5159         y1 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_yunits(y1)) 
5160         y2 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_yunits(y2)) 
5161  
5162         for name, array in [('x', x), ('y1', y1), ('y2', y2)]: 
5163             if array.ndim > 1: 
5164                 raise ValueError('Input passed into argument "%r"' % name + 
5165                                  'is not 1-dimensional.') 
5166  
5167         if where is None: 
5168             where = True 
5169         else: 
5170             where = np.asarray(where, dtype=bool) 
5171             if where.size != x.size: 
5172                 cbook.warn_deprecated( 
5173                     "3.2", 
5174                     message="The parameter where must have the same size as x " 
5175                             "in fill_between(). This will become an error in " 
5176                             "future versions of Matplotlib.") 
5177         where = where & ~functools.reduce(np.logical_or, 
5178                                           map(np.ma.getmask, [x, y1, y2])) 
5179  
5180         x, y1, y2 = np.broadcast_arrays(np.atleast_1d(x), y1, y2) 
5181  
5182         polys = [] 
5183         for ind0, ind1 in cbook.contiguous_regions(where): 
5184             xslice = x[ind0:ind1] 
5185             y1slice = y1[ind0:ind1] 
5186             y2slice = y2[ind0:ind1] 
5187             if step is not None: 
5188                 step_func = cbook.STEP_LOOKUP_MAP["steps-" + step] 
5189                 xslice, y1slice, y2slice = step_func(xslice, y1slice, y2slice) 
5190  
5191             if not len(xslice): 
5192                 continue 
5193  
5194             N = len(xslice) 
5195             X = np.zeros((2 * N + 2, 2), float) 
5196  
5197             if interpolate: 
5198                 def get_interp_point(ind): 
5199                     im1 = max(ind - 1, 0) 
5200                     x_values = x[im1:ind + 1] 
5201                     diff_values = y1[im1:ind + 1] - y2[im1:ind + 1] 
5202                     y1_values = y1[im1:ind + 1] 
5203  
5204                     if len(diff_values) == 2: 
5205                         if np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[1]): 
5206                             return x[im1], y1[im1] 
5207                         elif np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[0]): 
5208                             return x[ind], y1[ind] 
5209  
5210                     diff_order = diff_values.argsort() 
5211                     diff_root_x = np.interp( 
5212                         0, diff_values[diff_order], x_values[diff_order]) 
5213                     x_order = x_values.argsort() 
5214                     diff_root_y = np.interp(diff_root_x, x_values[x_order], 
5215                                             y1_values[x_order]) 
5216                     return diff_root_x, diff_root_y 
5217  
5218                 start = get_interp_point(ind0) 
5219                 end = get_interp_point(ind1) 
5220             else: 
5221                 # the purpose of the next two lines is for when y2 is a 
5222                 # scalar like 0 and we want the fill to go all the way 
5223                 # down to 0 even if none of the y1 sample points do 
5224                 start = xslice[0], y2slice[0] 
5225                 end = xslice[-1], y2slice[-1] 
5226  
5227             X[0] = start 
5228             X[N + 1] = end 
5229  
5230             X[1:N + 1, 0] = xslice 
5231             X[1:N + 1, 1] = y1slice 
5232             X[N + 2:, 0] = xslice[::-1] 
5233             X[N + 2:, 1] = y2slice[::-1] 
5234  
5235             polys.append(X) 
5236  
5237         collection = mcoll.PolyCollection(polys, **kwargs) 
5238  
5239         # now update the datalim and autoscale 
5240         XY1 = np.array([x[where], y1[where]]).T 
5241         XY2 = np.array([x[where], y2[where]]).T 
5242         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(XY1, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5243                                          updatex=True, updatey=True) 
5244         self.ignore_existing_data_limits = False 
5245         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(XY2, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5246                                          updatex=False, updatey=True) 
5247         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
5248         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5249         return collection

5251     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["y", "x1", "x2", "where"]) 
5252     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
5253     def fill_betweenx(self, y, x1, x2=0, where=None, 
5254                       step=None, interpolate=False, **kwargs): 
5255         """ 
5256         Fill the area between two vertical curves. 
5257  
5258         The curves are defined by the points (*x1*, *y*) and (*x2*, *y*). This 
5259         creates one or multiple polygons describing the filled area. 
5260  
5261         You may exclude some vertical sections from filling using *where*. 
5262  
5263         By default, the edges connect the given points directly. Use *step* if 
5264         the filling should be a step function, i.e. constant in between *y*. 
5265  
5266  
5267         Parameters 
5268         ---------- 
5269         y : array (length N) 
5270             The y coordinates of the nodes defining the curves. 
5271  
5272         x1 : array (length N) or scalar 
5273             The x coordinates of the nodes defining the first curve. 
5274  
5275         x2 : array (length N) or scalar, default: 0 
5276             The x coordinates of the nodes defining the second curve. 
5277  
5278         where : array of bool (length N), optional 
5279             Define *where* to exclude some vertical regions from being 
5280             filled. The filled regions are defined by the coordinates 
5281             ``y[where]``.  More precisely, fill between ``y[i]`` and ``y[i+1]`` 
5282             if ``where[i] and where[i+1]``.  Note that this definition implies 
5283             that an isolated *True* value between two *False* values in 
5284             *where* will not result in filling.  Both sides of the *True* 
5285             position remain unfilled due to the adjacent *False* values. 
5286  
5287         interpolate : bool, optional 
5288             This option is only relevant if *where* is used and the two curves 
5289             are crossing each other. 
5290  
5291             Semantically, *where* is often used for *x1* > *x2* or similar. 
5292             By default, the nodes of the polygon defining the filled region 
5293             will only be placed at the positions in the *y* array.  Such a 
5294             polygon cannot describe the above semantics close to the 
5295             intersection.  The y-sections containing the intersection are 
5296             simply clipped. 
5297  
5298             Setting *interpolate* to *True* will calculate the actual 
5299             intersection point and extend the filled region up to this point. 
5300  
5301         step : {'pre', 'post', 'mid'}, optional 
5302             Define *step* if the filling should be a step function, 
5303             i.e. constant in between *y*. The value determines where the 
5304             step will occur: 
5305  
5306             - 'pre': The y value is continued constantly to the left from 
5307               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``(x[i-1], x[i]]`` has the 
5308               value ``y[i]``. 
5309             - 'post': The y value is continued constantly to the right from 
5310               every *x* position, i.e. the interval ``[x[i], x[i+1])`` has the 
5311               value ``y[i]``. 
5312             - 'mid': Steps occur half-way between the *x* positions. 
5313  
5314         Other Parameters 
5315         ---------------- 
5316         **kwargs 
5317             All other keyword arguments are passed on to `.PolyCollection`. 
5318             They control the `.Polygon` properties: 
5319  
5320             %(PolyCollection)s 
5321  
5322         Returns 
5323         ------- 
5324         `.PolyCollection` 
5325             A `.PolyCollection` containing the plotted polygons. 
5326  
5327         See Also 
5328         -------- 
5329         fill_between : Fill between two sets of y-values. 
5330  
5331         Notes 
5332         ----- 
5333         .. [notes section required to get data note injection right] 
5334  
5335         """ 
5336         if not rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
5337             kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mcoll.Collection) 
5338             if not any(c in kwargs for c in ('color', 'facecolor')): 
5339                 kwargs['facecolor'] = \ 
5340                     self._get_patches_for_fill.get_next_color() 
5341  
5342         # Handle united data, such as dates 
5343         self._process_unit_info(ydata=y, xdata=x1, kwargs=kwargs) 
5344         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x2) 
5345  
5346         # Convert the arrays so we can work with them 
5347         y = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_yunits(y)) 
5348         x1 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_xunits(x1)) 
5349         x2 = ma.masked_invalid(self.convert_xunits(x2)) 
5350  
5351         for name, array in [('y', y), ('x1', x1), ('x2', x2)]: 
5352             if array.ndim > 1: 
5353                 raise ValueError('Input passed into argument "%r"' % name + 
5354                                  'is not 1-dimensional.') 
5355  
5356         if where is None: 
5357             where = True 
5358         else: 
5359             where = np.asarray(where, dtype=bool) 
5360             if where.size != y.size: 
5361                 cbook.warn_deprecated( 
5362                     "3.2", 
5363                     message="The parameter where must have the same size as y " 
5364                             "in fill_between(). This will become an error in " 
5365                             "future versions of Matplotlib.") 
5366         where = where & ~functools.reduce(np.logical_or, 
5367                                           map(np.ma.getmask, [y, x1, x2])) 
5368  
5369         y, x1, x2 = np.broadcast_arrays(np.atleast_1d(y), x1, x2) 
5370  
5371         polys = [] 
5372         for ind0, ind1 in cbook.contiguous_regions(where): 
5373             yslice = y[ind0:ind1] 
5374             x1slice = x1[ind0:ind1] 
5375             x2slice = x2[ind0:ind1] 
5376             if step is not None: 
5377                 step_func = cbook.STEP_LOOKUP_MAP["steps-" + step] 
5378                 yslice, x1slice, x2slice = step_func(yslice, x1slice, x2slice) 
5379  
5380             if not len(yslice): 
5381                 continue 
5382  
5383             N = len(yslice) 
5384             Y = np.zeros((2 * N + 2, 2), float) 
5385             if interpolate: 
5386                 def get_interp_point(ind): 
5387                     im1 = max(ind - 1, 0) 
5388                     y_values = y[im1:ind + 1] 
5389                     diff_values = x1[im1:ind + 1] - x2[im1:ind + 1] 
5390                     x1_values = x1[im1:ind + 1] 
5391  
5392                     if len(diff_values) == 2: 
5393                         if np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[1]): 
5394                             return x1[im1], y[im1] 
5395                         elif np.ma.is_masked(diff_values[0]): 
5396                             return x1[ind], y[ind] 
5397  
5398                     diff_order = diff_values.argsort() 
5399                     diff_root_y = np.interp( 
5400                         0, diff_values[diff_order], y_values[diff_order]) 
5401                     y_order = y_values.argsort() 
5402                     diff_root_x = np.interp(diff_root_y, y_values[y_order], 
5403                                             x1_values[y_order]) 
5404                     return diff_root_x, diff_root_y 
5405  
5406                 start = get_interp_point(ind0) 
5407                 end = get_interp_point(ind1) 
5408             else: 
5409                 # the purpose of the next two lines is for when x2 is a 
5410                 # scalar like 0 and we want the fill to go all the way 
5411                 # down to 0 even if none of the x1 sample points do 
5412                 start = x2slice[0], yslice[0] 
5413                 end = x2slice[-1], yslice[-1] 
5414  
5415             Y[0] = start 
5416             Y[N + 1] = end 
5417  
5418             Y[1:N + 1, 0] = x1slice 
5419             Y[1:N + 1, 1] = yslice 
5420             Y[N + 2:, 0] = x2slice[::-1] 
5421             Y[N + 2:, 1] = yslice[::-1] 
5422  
5423             polys.append(Y) 
5424  
5425         collection = mcoll.PolyCollection(polys, **kwargs) 
5426  
5427         # now update the datalim and autoscale 
5428         X1Y = np.array([x1[where], y[where]]).T 
5429         X2Y = np.array([x2[where], y[where]]).T 
5430         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(X1Y, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5431                                          updatex=True, updatey=True) 
5432         self.ignore_existing_data_limits = False 
5433         self.dataLim.update_from_data_xy(X2Y, self.ignore_existing_data_limits, 
5434                                          updatex=True, updatey=False) 
5435         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
5436         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5437         return collection

5439     #### plotting z(x, y): imshow, pcolor and relatives, contour 
5440     @_preprocess_data() 
5441     @cbook._delete_parameter("3.1", "shape") 
5442     @cbook._delete_parameter("3.1", "imlim") 
5443     def imshow(self, X, cmap=None, norm=None, aspect=None, 
5444                interpolation=None, alpha=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, 
5445                origin=None, extent=None, shape=None, filternorm=True, 
5446                filterrad=4.0, imlim=None, resample=None, url=None, **kwargs): 
5447         """ 
5448         Display data as an image; i.e. on a 2D regular raster. 
5449  
5450         The input may either be actual RGB(A) data, or 2D scalar data, which 
5451         will be rendered as a pseudocolor image. Note: For actually displaying 
5452         a grayscale image set up the color mapping using the parameters 
5453         ``cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255``. 
5454  
5455         Parameters 
5456         ---------- 
5457         X : array-like or PIL image 
5458             The image data. Supported array shapes are: 
5459  
5460             - (M, N): an image with scalar data. The values are mapped to 
5461               colors using normalization and a colormap. See parameters *norm*, 
5462               *cmap*, *vmin*, *vmax*. 
5463             - (M, N, 3): an image with RGB values (0-1 float or 0-255 int). 
5464             - (M, N, 4): an image with RGBA values (0-1 float or 0-255 int), 
5465               i.e. including transparency. 
5466  
5467             The first two dimensions (M, N) define the rows and columns of 
5468             the image. 
5469  
5470             Out-of-range RGB(A) values are clipped. 
5471  
5472         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
5473             The Colormap instance or registered colormap name used to map 
5474             scalar data to colors. This parameter is ignored for RGB(A) data. 
5475             Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
5476  
5477         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
5478             The `Normalize` instance used to scale scalar data to the [0, 1] 
5479             range before mapping to colors using *cmap*. By default, a linear 
5480             scaling mapping the lowest value to 0 and the highest to 1 is used. 
5481             This parameter is ignored for RGB(A) data. 
5482  
5483         aspect : {'equal', 'auto'} or float, optional 
5484             The aspect ratio of the axes.  This parameter is particularly 
5485             relevant for images since it determines whether data pixels are 
5486             square. 
5487  
5488             This parameter is a shortcut for explicitly calling 
5489             `.Axes.set_aspect`. See there for further details. 
5490  
5491             - 'equal': Ensures an aspect ratio of 1. Pixels will be square 
5492               (unless pixel sizes are explicitly made non-square in data 
5493               coordinates using *extent*). 
5494             - 'auto': The axes is kept fixed and the aspect is adjusted so 
5495               that the data fit in the axes. In general, this will result in 
5496               non-square pixels. 
5497  
5498             If not given, use :rc:`image.aspect`. 
5499  
5500         interpolation : str, optional 
5501             The interpolation method used. If *None*, :rc:`image.interpolation` 
5502             is used. 
5503  
5504             Supported values are 'none', 'antialiased', 'nearest', 'bilinear', 
5505             'bicubic', 'spline16', 'spline36', 'hanning', 'hamming', 'hermite', 
5506             'kaiser', 'quadric', 'catrom', 'gaussian', 'bessel', 'mitchell', 
5507             'sinc', 'lanczos'. 
5508  
5509             If *interpolation* is 'none', then no interpolation is performed 
5510             on the Agg, ps, pdf and svg backends. Other backends will fall back 
5511             to 'nearest'. Note that most SVG renders perform interpolation at 
5512             rendering and that the default interpolation method they implement 
5513             may differ. 
5514  
5515             If *interpolation* is the default 'antialiased', then 'nearest' 
5516             interpolation is used if the image is upsampled by more than a 
5517             factor of three (i.e. the number of display pixels is at least 
5518             three times the size of the data array).  If the upsampling rate is 
5519             smaller than 3, or the image is downsampled, then 'hanning' 
5520             interpolation is used to act as an anti-aliasing filter, unless the 
5521             image happens to be upsampled by exactly a factor of two or one. 
5522  
5523             See 
5524             :doc:`/gallery/images_contours_and_fields/interpolation_methods` 
5525             for an overview of the supported interpolation methods, and 
5526             :doc:`/gallery/images_contours_and_fields/image_antialiasing` for 
5527             a discussion of image antialiasing. 
5528  
5529             Some interpolation methods require an additional radius parameter, 
5530             which can be set by *filterrad*. Additionally, the antigrain image 
5531             resize filter is controlled by the parameter *filternorm*. 
5532  
5533         alpha : scalar or array-like, optional 
5534             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
5535             If *alpha* is an array, the alpha blending values are applied pixel 
5536             by pixel, and *alpha* must have the same shape as *X*. 
5537  
5538         vmin, vmax : scalar, optional 
5539             When using scalar data and no explicit *norm*, *vmin* and *vmax* 
5540             define the data range that the colormap covers. By default, 
5541             the colormap covers the complete value range of the supplied 
5542             data. *vmin*, *vmax* are ignored if the *norm* parameter is used. 
5543  
5544         origin : {'upper', 'lower'}, optional 
5545             Place the [0, 0] index of the array in the upper left or lower left 
5546             corner of the axes. The convention 'upper' is typically used for 
5547             matrices and images. 
5548             If not given, :rc:`image.origin` is used, defaulting to 'upper'. 
5549  
5550             Note that the vertical axes points upward for 'lower' 
5551             but downward for 'upper'. 
5552  
5553             See the :doc:`/tutorials/intermediate/imshow_extent` tutorial for 
5554             examples and a more detailed description. 
5555  
5556         extent : scalars (left, right, bottom, top), optional 
5557             The bounding box in data coordinates that the image will fill. 
5558             The image is stretched individually along x and y to fill the box. 
5559  
5560             The default extent is determined by the following conditions. 
5561             Pixels have unit size in data coordinates. Their centers are on 
5562             integer coordinates, and their center coordinates range from 0 to 
5563             columns-1 horizontally and from 0 to rows-1 vertically. 
5564  
5565             Note that the direction of the vertical axis and thus the default 
5566             values for top and bottom depend on *origin*: 
5567  
5568             - For ``origin == 'upper'`` the default is 
5569               ``(-0.5, numcols-0.5, numrows-0.5, -0.5)``. 
5570             - For ``origin == 'lower'`` the default is 
5571               ``(-0.5, numcols-0.5, -0.5, numrows-0.5)``. 
5572  
5573             See the :doc:`/tutorials/intermediate/imshow_extent` tutorial for 
5574             examples and a more detailed description. 
5575  
5576         filternorm : bool, default: True 
5577             A parameter for the antigrain image resize filter (see the 
5578             antigrain documentation).  If *filternorm* is set, the filter 
5579             normalizes integer values and corrects the rounding errors. It 
5580             doesn't do anything with the source floating point values, it 
5581             corrects only integers according to the rule of 1.0 which means 
5582             that any sum of pixel weights must be equal to 1.0.  So, the 
5583             filter function must produce a graph of the proper shape. 
5584  
5585         filterrad : float > 0, default: 4.0 
5586             The filter radius for filters that have a radius parameter, i.e. 
5587             when interpolation is one of: 'sinc', 'lanczos' or 'blackman'. 
5588  
5589         resample : bool, optional 
5590             When *True*, use a full resampling method.  When *False*, only 
5591             resample when the output image is larger than the input image. 
5592  
5593         url : str, optional 
5594             Set the url of the created `.AxesImage`. See `.Artist.set_url`. 
5595  
5596         Returns 
5597         ------- 
5598         image : `~matplotlib.image.AxesImage` 
5599  
5600         Other Parameters 
5601         ---------------- 
5602         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.artist.Artist` properties 
5603             These parameters are passed on to the constructor of the 
5604             `.AxesImage` artist. 
5605  
5606         See also 
5607         -------- 
5608         matshow : Plot a matrix or an array as an image. 
5609  
5610         Notes 
5611         ----- 
5612         Unless *extent* is used, pixel centers will be located at integer 
5613         coordinates. In other words: the origin will coincide with the center 
5614         of pixel (0, 0). 
5615  
5616         There are two common representations for RGB images with an alpha 
5617         channel: 
5618  
5619         -   Straight (unassociated) alpha: R, G, and B channels represent the 
5620             color of the pixel, disregarding its opacity. 
5621         -   Premultiplied (associated) alpha: R, G, and B channels represent 
5622             the color of the pixel, adjusted for its opacity by multiplication. 
5623  
5624         `~matplotlib.pyplot.imshow` expects RGB images adopting the straight 
5625         (unassociated) alpha representation. 
5626         """ 
5627         if aspect is None: 
5628             aspect = rcParams['image.aspect'] 
5629         self.set_aspect(aspect) 
5630         im = mimage.AxesImage(self, cmap, norm, interpolation, origin, extent, 
5631                               filternorm=filternorm, filterrad=filterrad, 
5632                               resample=resample, **kwargs) 
5633  
5634         im.set_data(X) 
5635         im.set_alpha(alpha) 
5636         if im.get_clip_path() is None: 
5637             # image does not already have clipping set, clip to axes patch 
5638             im.set_clip_path(self.patch) 
5639         if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
5640             im.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
5641         else: 
5642             im.autoscale_None() 
5643         im.set_url(url) 
5644  
5645         # update ax.dataLim, and, if autoscaling, set viewLim 
5646         # to tightly fit the image, regardless of dataLim. 
5647         im.set_extent(im.get_extent()) 
5648  
5649         self.add_image(im) 
5650         return im
