5652     @staticmethod 
5653     def _pcolorargs(funcname, *args, allmatch=False): 
5654         # If allmatch is True, then the incoming X, Y, C must have matching 
5655         # dimensions, taking into account that X and Y can be 1-D rather than 
5656         # 2-D.  This perfect match is required for Gouraud shading.  For flat 
5657         # shading, X and Y specify boundaries, so we need one more boundary 
5658         # than color in each direction.  For convenience, and consistent with 
5659         # Matlab, we discard the last row and/or column of C if necessary to 
5660         # meet this condition.  This is done if allmatch is False. 
5661  
5662         if len(args) == 1: 
5663             C = np.asanyarray(args[0]) 
5664             nrows, ncols = C.shape 
5665             if allmatch: 
5666                 X, Y = np.meshgrid(np.arange(ncols), np.arange(nrows)) 
5667             else: 
5668                 X, Y = np.meshgrid(np.arange(ncols + 1), np.arange(nrows + 1)) 
5669             C = cbook.safe_masked_invalid(C) 
5670             return X, Y, C 
5671  
5672         if len(args) == 3: 
5673             # Check x and y for bad data... 
5674             C = np.asanyarray(args[2]) 
5675             X, Y = [cbook.safe_masked_invalid(a) for a in args[:2]] 
5676             if funcname == 'pcolormesh': 
5677                 if np.ma.is_masked(X) or np.ma.is_masked(Y): 
5678                     raise ValueError( 
5679                         'x and y arguments to pcolormesh cannot have ' 
5680                         'non-finite values or be of type ' 
5681                         'numpy.ma.core.MaskedArray with masked values') 
5682                 # safe_masked_invalid() returns an ndarray for dtypes other 
5683                 # than floating point. 
5684                 if isinstance(X, np.ma.core.MaskedArray): 
5685                     X = X.data  # strip mask as downstream doesn't like it... 
5686                 if isinstance(Y, np.ma.core.MaskedArray): 
5687                     Y = Y.data 
5688             nrows, ncols = C.shape 
5689         else: 
5690             raise TypeError( 
5691                 'Illegal arguments to %s; see help(%s)' % (funcname, funcname)) 
5692  
5693         Nx = X.shape[-1] 
5694         Ny = Y.shape[0] 
5695         if X.ndim != 2 or X.shape[0] == 1: 
5696             x = X.reshape(1, Nx) 
5697             X = x.repeat(Ny, axis=0) 
5698         if Y.ndim != 2 or Y.shape[1] == 1: 
5699             y = Y.reshape(Ny, 1) 
5700             Y = y.repeat(Nx, axis=1) 
5701         if X.shape != Y.shape: 
5702             raise TypeError( 
5703                 'Incompatible X, Y inputs to %s; see help(%s)' % ( 
5704                 funcname, funcname)) 
5705         if allmatch: 
5706             if (Nx, Ny) != (ncols, nrows): 
5707                 raise TypeError('Dimensions of C %s are incompatible with' 
5708                                 ' X (%d) and/or Y (%d); see help(%s)' % ( 
5709                                     C.shape, Nx, Ny, funcname)) 
5710         else: 
5711             if not (ncols in (Nx, Nx - 1) and nrows in (Ny, Ny - 1)): 
5712                 raise TypeError('Dimensions of C %s are incompatible with' 
5713                                 ' X (%d) and/or Y (%d); see help(%s)' % ( 
5714                                     C.shape, Nx, Ny, funcname)) 
5715             C = C[:Ny - 1, :Nx - 1] 
5716         C = cbook.safe_masked_invalid(C) 
5717         return X, Y, C 
5718  
5719     @_preprocess_data() 
5720     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
5721     def pcolor(self, *args, alpha=None, norm=None, cmap=None, vmin=None, 
5722                vmax=None, **kwargs): 
5723         r""" 
5724         Create a pseudocolor plot with a non-regular rectangular grid. 
5725  
5726         Call signature:: 
5727  
5728             pcolor([X, Y,] C, **kwargs) 
5729  
5730         *X* and *Y* can be used to specify the corners of the quadrilaterals. 
5731  
5732         .. hint:: 
5733  
5734             ``pcolor()`` can be very slow for large arrays. In most 
5735             cases you should use the similar but much faster 
5736             `~.Axes.pcolormesh` instead. See there for a discussion of the 
5737             differences. 
5738  
5739         Parameters 
5740         ---------- 
5741         C : array-like 
5742             A scalar 2-D array. The values will be color-mapped. 
5743  
5744         X, Y : array-like, optional 
5745             The coordinates of the quadrilateral corners. The quadrilateral 
5746             for ``C[i, j]`` has corners at:: 
5747  
5748                 (X[i+1, j], Y[i+1, j])           (X[i+1, j+1], Y[i+1, j+1]) 
5749                                       +---------+ 
5750                                       | C[i, j] | 
5751                                       +---------+ 
5752                     (X[i, j], Y[i, j])           (X[i, j+1], Y[i, j+1]) 
5753  
5754             Note that the column index corresponds to the 
5755             x-coordinate, and the row index corresponds to y. For 
5756             details, see the :ref:`Notes <axes-pcolor-grid-orientation>` 
5757             section below. 
5758  
5759             The dimensions of *X* and *Y* should be one greater than those of 
5760             *C*. Alternatively, *X*, *Y* and *C* may have equal dimensions, in 
5761             which case the last row and column of *C* will be ignored. 
5762  
5763             If *X* and/or *Y* are 1-D arrays or column vectors they will be 
5764             expanded as needed into the appropriate 2-D arrays, making a 
5765             rectangular grid. 
5766  
5767         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
5768             A Colormap instance or registered colormap name. The colormap 
5769             maps the *C* values to colors. Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
5770  
5771         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
5772             The Normalize instance scales the data values to the canonical 
5773             colormap range [0, 1] for mapping to colors. By default, the data 
5774             range is mapped to the colorbar range using linear scaling. 
5775  
5776         vmin, vmax : scalar, default: None 
5777             The colorbar range. If *None*, suitable min/max values are 
5778             automatically chosen by the `~.Normalize` instance (defaults to 
5779             the respective min/max values of *C* in case of the default linear 
5780             scaling). 
5781  
5782         edgecolors : {'none', None, 'face', color, color sequence}, optional 
5783             The color of the edges. Defaults to 'none'. Possible values: 
5784  
5785             - 'none' or '': No edge. 
5786             - *None*: :rc:`patch.edgecolor` will be used. Note that currently 
5787               :rc:`patch.force_edgecolor` has to be True for this to work. 
5788             - 'face': Use the adjacent face color. 
5789             - A color or sequence of colors will set the edge color. 
5790  
5791             The singular form *edgecolor* works as an alias. 
5792  
5793         alpha : scalar, default: None 
5794             The alpha blending value of the face color, between 0 (transparent) 
5795             and 1 (opaque). Note: The edgecolor is currently not affected by 
5796             this. 
5797  
5798         snap : bool, default: False 
5799             Whether to snap the mesh to pixel boundaries. 
5800  
5801         Returns 
5802         ------- 
5803         collection : `matplotlib.collections.Collection` 
5804  
5805         Other Parameters 
5806         ---------------- 
5807         antialiaseds : bool, default: False 
5808             The default *antialiaseds* is False if the default 
5809             *edgecolors*\ ="none" is used.  This eliminates artificial lines 
5810             at patch boundaries, and works regardless of the value of alpha. 
5811             If *edgecolors* is not "none", then the default *antialiaseds* 
5812             is taken from :rc:`patch.antialiased`. 
5813             Stroking the edges may be preferred if *alpha* is 1, but will 
5814             cause artifacts otherwise. 
5815  
5816         **kwargs 
5817             Additionally, the following arguments are allowed. They are passed 
5818             along to the `~matplotlib.collections.PolyCollection` constructor: 
5819  
5820         %(PolyCollection)s 
5821  
5822         See Also 
5823         -------- 
5824         pcolormesh : for an explanation of the differences between 
5825             pcolor and pcolormesh. 
5826         imshow : If *X* and *Y* are each equidistant, `~.Axes.imshow` can be a 
5827             faster alternative. 
5828  
5829         Notes 
5830         ----- 
5831         **Masked arrays** 
5832  
5833         *X*, *Y* and *C* may be masked arrays. If either ``C[i, j]``, or one 
5834         of the vertices surrounding ``C[i, j]`` (*X* or *Y* at 
5835         ``[i, j], [i+1, j], [i, j+1], [i+1, j+1]``) is masked, nothing is 
5836         plotted. 
5837  
5838         .. _axes-pcolor-grid-orientation: 
5839  
5840         **Grid orientation** 
5841  
5842         The grid orientation follows the standard matrix convention: An array 
5843         *C* with shape (nrows, ncolumns) is plotted with the column number as 
5844         *X* and the row number as *Y*. 
5845  
5846         **Handling of pcolor() end-cases** 
5847  
5848         ``pcolor()`` displays all columns of *C* if *X* and *Y* are not 
5849         specified, or if *X* and *Y* have one more column than *C*. 
5850         If *X* and *Y* have the same number of columns as *C* then the last 
5851         column of *C* is dropped. Similarly for the rows. 
5852  
5853         Note: This behavior is different from MATLAB's ``pcolor()``, which 
5854         always discards the last row and column of *C*. 
5855         """ 
5856         X, Y, C = self._pcolorargs('pcolor', *args, allmatch=False) 
5857         Ny, Nx = X.shape 
5858  
5859         # unit conversion allows e.g. datetime objects as axis values 
5860         self._process_unit_info(xdata=X, ydata=Y, kwargs=kwargs) 
5861         X = self.convert_xunits(X) 
5862         Y = self.convert_yunits(Y) 
5863  
5864         # convert to MA, if necessary. 
5865         C = ma.asarray(C) 
5866         X = ma.asarray(X) 
5867         Y = ma.asarray(Y) 
5868  
5869         mask = ma.getmaskarray(X) + ma.getmaskarray(Y) 
5870         xymask = (mask[0:-1, 0:-1] + mask[1:, 1:] + 
5871                   mask[0:-1, 1:] + mask[1:, 0:-1]) 
5872         # don't plot if C or any of the surrounding vertices are masked. 
5873         mask = ma.getmaskarray(C) + xymask 
5874  
5875         unmask = ~mask 
5876         X1 = ma.filled(X[:-1, :-1])[unmask] 
5877         Y1 = ma.filled(Y[:-1, :-1])[unmask] 
5878         X2 = ma.filled(X[1:, :-1])[unmask] 
5879         Y2 = ma.filled(Y[1:, :-1])[unmask] 
5880         X3 = ma.filled(X[1:, 1:])[unmask] 
5881         Y3 = ma.filled(Y[1:, 1:])[unmask] 
5882         X4 = ma.filled(X[:-1, 1:])[unmask] 
5883         Y4 = ma.filled(Y[:-1, 1:])[unmask] 
5884         npoly = len(X1) 
5885  
5886         xy = np.stack([X1, Y1, X2, Y2, X3, Y3, X4, Y4, X1, Y1], axis=-1) 
5887         verts = xy.reshape((npoly, 5, 2)) 
5888  
5889         C = ma.filled(C[:Ny - 1, :Nx - 1])[unmask] 
5890  
5891         linewidths = (0.25,) 
5892         if 'linewidth' in kwargs: 
5893             kwargs['linewidths'] = kwargs.pop('linewidth') 
5894         kwargs.setdefault('linewidths', linewidths) 
5895  
5896         if 'edgecolor' in kwargs: 
5897             kwargs['edgecolors'] = kwargs.pop('edgecolor') 
5898         ec = kwargs.setdefault('edgecolors', 'none') 
5899  
5900         # aa setting will default via collections to patch.antialiased 
5901         # unless the boundary is not stroked, in which case the 
5902         # default will be False; with unstroked boundaries, aa 
5903         # makes artifacts that are often disturbing. 
5904         if 'antialiased' in kwargs: 
5905             kwargs['antialiaseds'] = kwargs.pop('antialiased') 
5906         if 'antialiaseds' not in kwargs and cbook._str_lower_equal(ec, "none"): 
5907             kwargs['antialiaseds'] = False 
5908  
5909         kwargs.setdefault('snap', False) 
5910  
5911         collection = mcoll.PolyCollection(verts, **kwargs) 
5912  
5913         collection.set_alpha(alpha) 
5914         collection.set_array(C) 
5915         collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
5916         collection.set_norm(norm) 
5917         collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
5918         collection.autoscale_None() 
5919         self.grid(False) 
5920  
5921         x = X.compressed() 
5922         y = Y.compressed() 
5923  
5924         # Transform from native to data coordinates? 
5925         t = collection._transform 
5926         if (not isinstance(t, mtransforms.Transform) and 
5927             hasattr(t, '_as_mpl_transform')): 
5928             t = t._as_mpl_transform(self.axes) 
5929  
5930         if t and any(t.contains_branch_seperately(self.transData)): 
5931             trans_to_data = t - self.transData 
5932             pts = np.vstack([x, y]).T.astype(float) 
5933             transformed_pts = trans_to_data.transform(pts) 
5934             x = transformed_pts[..., 0] 
5935             y = transformed_pts[..., 1] 
5936  
5937         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
5938  
5939         minx = np.min(x) 
5940         maxx = np.max(x) 
5941         miny = np.min(y) 
5942         maxy = np.max(y) 
5943         collection.sticky_edges.x[:] = [minx, maxx] 
5944         collection.sticky_edges.y[:] = [miny, maxy] 
5945         corners = (minx, miny), (maxx, maxy) 
5946         self.update_datalim(corners) 
5947         self._request_autoscale_view() 
5948         return collection 
5949  
5950     @_preprocess_data() 
5951     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
5952     def pcolormesh(self, *args, alpha=None, norm=None, cmap=None, vmin=None, 
5953                    vmax=None, shading='flat', antialiased=False, **kwargs): 
5954         """ 
5955         Create a pseudocolor plot with a non-regular rectangular grid. 
5956  
5957         Call signature:: 
5958  
5959             pcolor([X, Y,] C, **kwargs) 
5960  
5961         *X* and *Y* can be used to specify the corners of the quadrilaterals. 
5962  
5963         .. note:: 
5964  
5965            `~Axes.pcolormesh` is similar to `~Axes.pcolor`. It's much faster 
5966            and preferred in most cases. For a detailed discussion on the 
5967            differences see :ref:`Differences between pcolor() and pcolormesh() 
5968            <differences-pcolor-pcolormesh>`. 
5969  
5970         Parameters 
5971         ---------- 
5972         C : array-like 
5973             A scalar 2-D array. The values will be color-mapped. 
5974  
5975         X, Y : array-like, optional 
5976             The coordinates of the quadrilateral corners. The quadrilateral 
5977             for ``C[i, j]`` has corners at:: 
5978  
5979                 (X[i+1, j], Y[i+1, j])           (X[i+1, j+1], Y[i+1, j+1]) 
5980                                       +---------+ 
5981                                       | C[i, j] | 
5982                                       +---------+ 
5983                     (X[i, j], Y[i, j])           (X[i, j+1], Y[i, j+1]) 
5984  
5985             Note that the column index corresponds to the 
5986             x-coordinate, and the row index corresponds to y. For 
5987             details, see the :ref:`Notes <axes-pcolormesh-grid-orientation>` 
5988             section below. 
5989  
5990             The dimensions of *X* and *Y* should be one greater than those of 
5991             *C*. Alternatively, *X*, *Y* and *C* may have equal dimensions, in 
5992             which case the last row and column of *C* will be ignored. 
5993  
5994             If *X* and/or *Y* are 1-D arrays or column vectors they will be 
5995             expanded as needed into the appropriate 2-D arrays, making a 
5996             rectangular grid. 
5997  
5998         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
5999             A Colormap instance or registered colormap name. The colormap 
6000             maps the *C* values to colors. Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
6001  
6002         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
6003             The Normalize instance scales the data values to the canonical 
6004             colormap range [0, 1] for mapping to colors. By default, the data 
6005             range is mapped to the colorbar range using linear scaling. 
6006  
6007         vmin, vmax : scalar, default: None 
6008             The colorbar range. If *None*, suitable min/max values are 
6009             automatically chosen by the `~.Normalize` instance (defaults to 
6010             the respective min/max values of *C* in case of the default linear 
6011             scaling). 
6012  
6013         edgecolors : {'none', None, 'face', color, color sequence}, optional 
6014             The color of the edges. Defaults to 'none'. Possible values: 
6015  
6016             - 'none' or '': No edge. 
6017             - *None*: :rc:`patch.edgecolor` will be used. Note that currently 
6018               :rc:`patch.force_edgecolor` has to be True for this to work. 
6019             - 'face': Use the adjacent face color. 
6020             - A color or sequence of colors will set the edge color. 
6021  
6022             The singular form *edgecolor* works as an alias. 
6023  
6024         alpha : scalar, default: None 
6025             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
6026  
6027         shading : {'flat', 'gouraud'}, optional 
6028             The fill style, Possible values: 
6029  
6030             - 'flat': A solid color is used for each quad. The color of the 
6031               quad (i, j), (i+1, j), (i, j+1), (i+1, j+1) is given by 
6032               ``C[i, j]``. 
6033             - 'gouraud': Each quad will be Gouraud shaded: The color of the 
6034               corners (i', j') are given by ``C[i',j']``. The color values of 
6035               the area in between is interpolated from the corner values. 
6036               When Gouraud shading is used, *edgecolors* is ignored. 
6037  
6038         snap : bool, default: False 
6039             Whether to snap the mesh to pixel boundaries. 
6040  
6041         Returns 
6042         ------- 
6043         mesh : `matplotlib.collections.QuadMesh` 
6044  
6045         Other Parameters 
6046         ---------------- 
6047         **kwargs 
6048             Additionally, the following arguments are allowed. They are passed 
6049             along to the `~matplotlib.collections.QuadMesh` constructor: 
6050  
6051         %(QuadMesh)s 
6052  
6053         See Also 
6054         -------- 
6055         pcolor : An alternative implementation with slightly different 
6056             features. For a detailed discussion on the differences see 
6057             :ref:`Differences between pcolor() and pcolormesh() 
6058             <differences-pcolor-pcolormesh>`. 
6059         imshow : If *X* and *Y* are each equidistant, `~.Axes.imshow` can be a 
6060             faster alternative. 
6061  
6062         Notes 
6063         ----- 
6064         **Masked arrays** 
6065  
6066         *C* may be a masked array. If ``C[i, j]`` is masked, the corresponding 
6067         quadrilateral will be transparent. Masking of *X* and *Y* is not 
6068         supported. Use `~.Axes.pcolor` if you need this functionality. 
6069  
6070         .. _axes-pcolormesh-grid-orientation: 
6071  
6072         **Grid orientation** 
6073  
6074         The grid orientation follows the standard matrix convention: An array 
6075         *C* with shape (nrows, ncolumns) is plotted with the column number as 
6076         *X* and the row number as *Y*. 
6077  
6078         .. _differences-pcolor-pcolormesh: 
6079  
6080         **Differences between pcolor() and pcolormesh()** 
6081  
6082         Both methods are used to create a pseudocolor plot of a 2-D array 
6083         using quadrilaterals. 
6084  
6085         The main difference lies in the created object and internal data 
6086         handling: 
6087         While `~.Axes.pcolor` returns a `.PolyCollection`, `~.Axes.pcolormesh` 
6088         returns a `.QuadMesh`. The latter is more specialized for the given 
6089         purpose and thus is faster. It should almost always be preferred. 
6090  
6091         There is also a slight difference in the handling of masked arrays. 
6092         Both `~.Axes.pcolor` and `~.Axes.pcolormesh` support masked arrays 
6093         for *C*. However, only `~.Axes.pcolor` supports masked arrays for *X* 
6094         and *Y*. The reason lies in the internal handling of the masked values. 
6095         `~.Axes.pcolor` leaves out the respective polygons from the 
6096         PolyCollection. `~.Axes.pcolormesh` sets the facecolor of the masked 
6097         elements to transparent. You can see the difference when using 
6098         edgecolors. While all edges are drawn irrespective of masking in a 
6099         QuadMesh, the edge between two adjacent masked quadrilaterals in 
6100         `~.Axes.pcolor` is not drawn as the corresponding polygons do not 
6101         exist in the PolyCollection. 
6102  
6103         Another difference is the support of Gouraud shading in 
6104         `~.Axes.pcolormesh`, which is not available with `~.Axes.pcolor`. 
6105  
6106         """ 
6107         shading = shading.lower() 
6108         kwargs.setdefault('edgecolors', 'None') 
6109  
6110         allmatch = (shading == 'gouraud') 
6111  
6112         X, Y, C = self._pcolorargs('pcolormesh', *args, allmatch=allmatch) 
6113         Ny, Nx = X.shape 
6114         X = X.ravel() 
6115         Y = Y.ravel() 
6116         # unit conversion allows e.g. datetime objects as axis values 
6117         self._process_unit_info(xdata=X, ydata=Y, kwargs=kwargs) 
6118         X = self.convert_xunits(X) 
6119         Y = self.convert_yunits(Y) 
6120  
6121         # convert to one dimensional arrays 
6122         C = C.ravel() 
6123         coords = np.column_stack((X, Y)).astype(float, copy=False) 
6124         collection = mcoll.QuadMesh(Nx - 1, Ny - 1, coords, 
6125                                     antialiased=antialiased, shading=shading, 
6126                                     **kwargs) 
6127         collection.set_alpha(alpha) 
6128         collection.set_array(C) 
6129         collection.set_cmap(cmap) 
6130         collection.set_norm(norm) 
6131         collection.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
6132         collection.autoscale_None() 
6133  
6134         self.grid(False) 
6135  
6136         # Transform from native to data coordinates? 
6137         t = collection._transform 
6138         if (not isinstance(t, mtransforms.Transform) and 
6139             hasattr(t, '_as_mpl_transform')): 
6140             t = t._as_mpl_transform(self.axes) 
6141  
6142         if t and any(t.contains_branch_seperately(self.transData)): 
6143             trans_to_data = t - self.transData 
6144             coords = trans_to_data.transform(coords) 
6145  
6146         self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
6147  
6148         minx, miny = np.min(coords, axis=0) 
6149         maxx, maxy = np.max(coords, axis=0) 
6150         collection.sticky_edges.x[:] = [minx, maxx] 
6151         collection.sticky_edges.y[:] = [miny, maxy] 
6152         corners = (minx, miny), (maxx, maxy) 
6153         self.update_datalim(corners) 
6154         self._request_autoscale_view() 
6155         return collection 
6156  
6157     @_preprocess_data() 
6158     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
6159     def pcolorfast(self, *args, alpha=None, norm=None, cmap=None, vmin=None, 
6160                    vmax=None, **kwargs): 
6161         """ 
6162         Create a pseudocolor plot with a non-regular rectangular grid. 
6163  
6164         Call signature:: 
6165  
6166           ax.pcolorfast([X, Y], C, /, **kwargs) 
6167  
6168         This method is similar to ~.Axes.pcolor` and `~.Axes.pcolormesh`. 
6169         It's designed to provide the fastest pcolor-type plotting with the 
6170         Agg backend. To achieve this, it uses different algorithms internally 
6171         depending on the complexity of the input grid (regular rectangular, 
6172         non-regular rectangular or arbitrary quadrilateral). 
6173  
6174         .. warning:: 
6175  
6176            This method is experimental. Compared to `~.Axes.pcolor` or 
6177            `~.Axes.pcolormesh` it has some limitations: 
6178  
6179            - It supports only flat shading (no outlines) 
6180            - It lacks support for log scaling of the axes. 
6181            - It does not have a have a pyplot wrapper. 
6182  
6183         Parameters 
6184         ---------- 
6185         C : array-like(M, N) 
6186             The image data. Supported array shapes are: 
6187  
6188             - (M, N): an image with scalar data. The data is visualized 
6189               using a colormap. 
6190             - (M, N, 3): an image with RGB values (0-1 float or 0-255 int). 
6191             - (M, N, 4): an image with RGBA values (0-1 float or 0-255 int), 
6192               i.e. including transparency. 
6193  
6194             The first two dimensions (M, N) define the rows and columns of 
6195             the image. 
6196  
6197             This parameter can only be passed positionally. 
6198  
6199         X, Y : tuple or array-like, default: ``(0, N)``, ``(0, M)`` 
6200             *X* and *Y* are used to specify the coordinates of the 
6201             quadrilaterals. There are different ways to do this: 
6202  
6203             - Use tuples ``X=(xmin, xmax)`` and ``Y=(ymin, ymax)`` to define 
6204               a *uniform rectangular grid*. 
6205  
6206               The tuples define the outer edges of the grid. All individual 
6207               quadrilaterals will be of the same size. This is the fastest 
6208               version. 
6209  
6210             - Use 1D arrays *X*, *Y* to specify a *non-uniform rectangular 
6211               grid*. 
6212  
6213               In this case *X* and *Y* have to be monotonic 1D arrays of length 
6214               *N+1* and *M+1*, specifying the x and y boundaries of the cells. 
6215  
6216               The speed is intermediate. Note: The grid is checked, and if 
6217               found to be uniform the fast version is used. 
6218  
6219             - Use 2D arrays *X*, *Y* if you need an *arbitrary quadrilateral 
6220               grid* (i.e. if the quadrilaterals are not rectangular). 
6221  
6222               In this case *X* and *Y* are 2D arrays with shape (M + 1, N + 1), 
6223               specifying the x and y coordinates of the corners of the colored 
6224               quadrilaterals. 
6225  
6226               This is the most general, but the slowest to render.  It may 
6227               produce faster and more compact output using ps, pdf, and 
6228               svg backends, however. 
6229  
6230             These arguments can only be passed positionally. 
6231  
6232         cmap : str or `~matplotlib.colors.Colormap`, optional 
6233             A Colormap instance or registered colormap name. The colormap 
6234             maps the *C* values to colors. Defaults to :rc:`image.cmap`. 
6235  
6236         norm : `~matplotlib.colors.Normalize`, optional 
6237             The Normalize instance scales the data values to the canonical 
6238             colormap range [0, 1] for mapping to colors. By default, the data 
6239             range is mapped to the colorbar range using linear scaling. 
6240  
6241         vmin, vmax : scalar, default: None 
6242             The colorbar range. If *None*, suitable min/max values are 
6243             automatically chosen by the `~.Normalize` instance (defaults to 
6244             the respective min/max values of *C* in case of the default linear 
6245             scaling). 
6246  
6247         alpha : scalar, default: None 
6248             The alpha blending value, between 0 (transparent) and 1 (opaque). 
6249  
6250         snap : bool, default: False 
6251             Whether to snap the mesh to pixel boundaries. 
6252  
6253         Returns 
6254         ------- 
6255         image : `.AxesImage` or `.PcolorImage` or `.QuadMesh` 
6256             The return type depends on the type of grid: 
6257  
6258             - `.AxesImage` for a regular rectangular grid. 
6259             - `.PcolorImage` for a non-regular rectangular grid. 
6260             - `.QuadMesh` for a non-rectangular grid. 
6261  
6262         Notes 
6263         ----- 
6264         .. [notes section required to get data note injection right] 
6265         """ 
6266  
6267         C = args[-1] 
6268         nr, nc = np.shape(C)[:2] 
6269         if len(args) == 1: 
6270             style = "image" 
6271             x = [0, nc] 
6272             y = [0, nr] 
6273         elif len(args) == 3: 
6274             x, y = args[:2] 
6275             x = np.asarray(x) 
6276             y = np.asarray(y) 
6277             if x.ndim == 1 and y.ndim == 1: 
6278                 if x.size == 2 and y.size == 2: 
6279                     style = "image" 
6280                 else: 
6281                     dx = np.diff(x) 
6282                     dy = np.diff(y) 
6283                     if (np.ptp(dx) < 0.01 * np.abs(dx.mean()) and 
6284                         np.ptp(dy) < 0.01 * np.abs(dy.mean())): 
6285                         style = "image" 
6286                     else: 
6287                         style = "pcolorimage" 
6288             elif x.ndim == 2 and y.ndim == 2: 
6289                 style = "quadmesh" 
6290             else: 
6291                 raise TypeError("arguments do not match valid signatures") 
6292         else: 
6293             raise TypeError("need 1 argument or 3 arguments") 
6294  
6295         if style == "quadmesh": 
6296             # data point in each cell is value at lower left corner 
6297             coords = np.stack([x, y], axis=-1) 
6298             if np.ndim(C) == 2: 
6299                 qm_kwargs = {"array": np.ma.ravel(C)} 
6300             elif np.ndim(C) == 3: 
6301                 qm_kwargs = {"color": np.ma.reshape(C, (-1, C.shape[-1]))} 
6302             else: 
6303                 raise ValueError("C must be 2D or 3D") 
6304             collection = mcoll.QuadMesh( 
6305                 nc, nr, coords, **qm_kwargs, 
6306                 alpha=alpha, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, 
6307                 antialiased=False, edgecolors="none") 
6308             self.add_collection(collection, autolim=False) 
6309             xl, xr, yb, yt = x.min(), x.max(), y.min(), y.max() 
6310             ret = collection 
6311  
6312         else:  # It's one of the two image styles. 
6313             extent = xl, xr, yb, yt = x[0], x[-1], y[0], y[-1] 
6314             if style == "image": 
6315                 im = mimage.AxesImage( 
6316                     self, cmap, norm, 
6317                     data=C, alpha=alpha, extent=extent, 
6318                     interpolation='nearest', origin='lower', 
6319                     **kwargs) 
6320             elif style == "pcolorimage": 
6321                 im = mimage.PcolorImage( 
6322                     self, x, y, C, 
6323                     cmap=cmap, norm=norm, alpha=alpha, extent=extent, 
6324                     **kwargs) 
6325             self.add_image(im) 
6326             ret = im 
6327  
6328         if vmin is not None or vmax is not None: 
6329             ret.set_clim(vmin, vmax) 
6330         elif np.ndim(C) == 2:  # C.ndim == 3 is RGB(A) so doesn't need scaling. 
6331             ret.autoscale_None() 
6332         if ret.get_clip_path() is None: 
6333             # image does not already have clipping set, clip to axes patch 
6334             ret.set_clip_path(self.patch) 
6335  
6336         ret.sticky_edges.x[:] = [xl, xr] 
6337         ret.sticky_edges.y[:] = [yb, yt] 
6338         self.update_datalim(np.array([[xl, yb], [xr, yt]])) 
6339         self._request_autoscale_view(tight=True) 
6340         return ret 
6341

6346         self._request_autoscale_view()

6364     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", 'weights'], label_namer="x") 
6365     def hist(self, x, bins=None, range=None, density=False, weights=None, 
6366              cumulative=False, bottom=None, histtype='bar', align='mid', 
6367              orientation='vertical', rwidth=None, log=False, 
6368              color=None, label=None, stacked=False, **kwargs): 
6369         """ 
6370         Plot a histogram. 
6371  
6372         Compute and draw the histogram of *x*.  The return value is a tuple 
6373         (*n*, *bins*, *patches*) or ([*n0*, *n1*, ...], *bins*, [*patches0*, 
6374         *patches1*,...]) if the input contains multiple data.  See the 
6375         documentation of the *weights* parameter to draw a histogram of 
6376         already-binned data. 
6377  
6378         Multiple data can be provided via *x* as a list of datasets 
6379         of potentially different length ([*x0*, *x1*, ...]), or as 
6380         a 2-D ndarray in which each column is a dataset.  Note that 
6381         the ndarray form is transposed relative to the list form. 
6382  
6383         Masked arrays are not supported. 
6384  
6385         The *bins*, *range*, *weights*, and *density* parameters behave as in 
6386         `numpy.histogram`. 
6387  
6388         Parameters 
6389         ---------- 
6390         x : (n,) array or sequence of (n,) arrays 
6391             Input values, this takes either a single array or a sequence of 
6392             arrays which are not required to be of the same length. 
6393  
6394         bins : int or sequence or str, optional 
6395             If *bins* is an integer, it defines the number of equal-width bins 
6396             in the range. 
6397  
6398             If *bins* is a sequence, it defines the bin edges, including the 
6399             left edge of the first bin and the right edge of the last bin; 
6400             in this case, bins may be unequally spaced.  All but the last 
6401             (righthand-most) bin is half-open.  In other words, if *bins* is:: 
6402  
6403                 [1, 2, 3, 4] 
6404  
6405             then the first bin is ``[1, 2)`` (including 1, but excluding 2) and 
6406             the second ``[2, 3)``.  The last bin, however, is ``[3, 4]``, which 
6407             *includes* 4. 
6408  
6409             If *bins* is a string, it is one of the binning strategies 
6410             supported by `numpy.histogram_bin_edges`: 'auto', 'fd', 'doane', 
6411             'scott', 'stone', 'rice', 'sturges', or 'sqrt'. 
6412  
6413             The default is :rc:`hist.bins`. 
6414  
6415         range : tuple or None, optional 
6416             The lower and upper range of the bins. Lower and upper outliers 
6417             are ignored. If not provided, *range* is ``(x.min(), x.max())``. 
6418             Range has no effect if *bins* is a sequence. 
6419  
6420             If *bins* is a sequence or *range* is specified, autoscaling 
6421             is based on the specified bin range instead of the 
6422             range of x. 
6423  
6424             Default is ``None`` 
6425  
6426         density : bool, optional 
6427             If ``True``, the first element of the return tuple will 
6428             be the counts normalized to form a probability density, i.e., 
6429             the area (or integral) under the histogram will sum to 1. 
6430             This is achieved by dividing the count by the number of 
6431             observations times the bin width and not dividing by the total 
6432             number of observations. If *stacked* is also ``True``, the sum of 
6433             the histograms is normalized to 1. 
6434  
6435             Default is ``False``. 
6436  
6437         weights : (n, ) array-like or None, optional 
6438             An array of weights, of the same shape as *x*.  Each value in *x* 
6439             only contributes its associated weight towards the bin count 
6440             (instead of 1).  If *normed* or *density* is ``True``, 
6441             the weights are normalized, so that the integral of the density 
6442             over the range remains 1. 
6443  
6444             Default is ``None``. 
6445  
6446             This parameter can be used to draw a histogram of data that has 
6447             already been binned, e.g. using `np.histogram` (by treating each 
6448             bin as a single point with a weight equal to its count) :: 
6449  
6450                 counts, bins = np.histogram(data) 
6451                 plt.hist(bins[:-1], bins, weights=counts) 
6452  
6453             (or you may alternatively use `~.bar()`). 
6454  
6455         cumulative : bool or -1, optional 
6456             If ``True``, then a histogram is computed where each bin gives the 
6457             counts in that bin plus all bins for smaller values. The last bin 
6458             gives the total number of datapoints. 
6459  
6460             If *density* is also ``True`` then the histogram is normalized such 
6461             that the last bin equals 1. 
6462  
6463             If *cumulative* is a number less than 0 (e.g., -1), the direction 
6464             of accumulation is reversed.  In this case, if *density* is also 
6465             ``True``, then the histogram is normalized such that the first bin 
6466             equals 1. 
6467  
6468             Default is ``False`` 
6469  
6470         bottom : array-like, scalar, or None 
6471             Location of the bottom baseline of each bin.  If a scalar, 
6472             the base line for each bin is shifted by the same amount. 
6473             If an array, each bin is shifted independently and the length 
6474             of bottom must match the number of bins.  If None, defaults to 0. 
6475  
6476             Default is ``None`` 
6477  
6478         histtype : {'bar', 'barstacked', 'step',  'stepfilled'}, optional 
6479             The type of histogram to draw. 
6480  
6481             - 'bar' is a traditional bar-type histogram.  If multiple data 
6482               are given the bars are arranged side by side. 
6483             - 'barstacked' is a bar-type histogram where multiple 
6484               data are stacked on top of each other. 
6485             - 'step' generates a lineplot that is by default unfilled. 
6486             - 'stepfilled' generates a lineplot that is by default filled. 
6487  
6488             Default is 'bar' 
6489  
6490         align : {'left', 'mid', 'right'}, optional 
6491             The horizontal alignment of the histogram bars. 
6492  
6493             - 'left': bars are centered on the left bin edges. 
6494             - 'mid': bars are centered between the bin edges. 
6495             - 'right': bars are centered on the right bin edges. 
6496  
6497             Default is 'mid' 
6498  
6499         orientation : {'horizontal', 'vertical'}, optional 
6500             If 'horizontal', `~matplotlib.pyplot.barh` will be used for 
6501             bar-type histograms and the *bottom* kwarg will be the left edges. 
6502  
6503         rwidth : scalar or None, optional 
6504             The relative width of the bars as a fraction of the bin width.  If 
6505             ``None``, automatically compute the width. 
6506  
6507             Ignored if *histtype* is 'step' or 'stepfilled'. 
6508  
6509             Default is ``None`` 
6510  
6511         log : bool, optional 
6512             If ``True``, the histogram axis will be set to a log scale. If 
6513             *log* is ``True`` and *x* is a 1D array, empty bins will be 
6514             filtered out and only the non-empty ``(n, bins, patches)`` 
6515             will be returned. 
6516  
6517             Default is ``False`` 
6518  
6519         color : color or array-like of colors or None, optional 
6520             Color or sequence of colors, one per dataset.  Default (``None``) 
6521             uses the standard line color sequence. 
6522  
6523             Default is ``None`` 
6524  
6525         label : str or None, optional 
6526             String, or sequence of strings to match multiple datasets.  Bar 
6527             charts yield multiple patches per dataset, but only the first gets 
6528             the label, so that the legend command will work as expected. 
6529  
6530             default is ``None`` 
6531  
6532         stacked : bool, optional 
6533             If ``True``, multiple data are stacked on top of each other If 
6534             ``False`` multiple data are arranged side by side if histtype is 
6535             'bar' or on top of each other if histtype is 'step' 
6536  
6537             Default is ``False`` 
6538  
6539         Returns 
6540         ------- 
6541         n : array or list of arrays 
6542             The values of the histogram bins. See *density* and *weights* for a 
6543             description of the possible semantics.  If input *x* is an array, 
6544             then this is an array of length *nbins*. If input is a sequence of 
6545             arrays ``[data1, data2, ...]``, then this is a list of arrays with 
6546             the values of the histograms for each of the arrays in the same 
6547             order.  The dtype of the array *n* (or of its element arrays) will 
6548             always be float even if no weighting or normalization is used. 
6549  
6550         bins : array 
6551             The edges of the bins. Length nbins + 1 (nbins left edges and right 
6552             edge of last bin).  Always a single array even when multiple data 
6553             sets are passed in. 
6554  
6555         patches : list or list of lists 
6556             Silent list of individual patches used to create the histogram 
6557             or list of such list if multiple input datasets. 
6558  
6559         Other Parameters 
6560         ---------------- 
6561         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.patches.Patch` properties 
6562  
6563         See also 
6564         -------- 
6565         hist2d : 2D histograms 
6566  
6567         Notes 
6568         ----- 
6569         For large numbers of bins (>1000), 'step' and 'stepfilled' can be 
6570         significantly faster than 'bar' and 'barstacked'. 
6571  
6572         """ 
6573         # Avoid shadowing the builtin. 
6574         bin_range = range 
6575         from builtins import range 
6576  
6577         if np.isscalar(x): 
6578             x = [x] 
6579  
6580         if bins is None: 
6581             bins = rcParams['hist.bins'] 
6582  
6583         # Validate string inputs here to avoid cluttering subsequent code. 
6584         cbook._check_in_list(['bar', 'barstacked', 'step', 'stepfilled'], 
6585                              histtype=histtype) 
6586         cbook._check_in_list(['left', 'mid', 'right'], align=align) 
6587         cbook._check_in_list(['horizontal', 'vertical'], 
6588                              orientation=orientation) 
6589  
6590         if histtype == 'barstacked' and not stacked: 
6591             stacked = True 
6592  
6593         # basic input validation 
6594         input_empty = np.size(x) == 0 
6595         # Massage 'x' for processing. 
6596         x = cbook._reshape_2D(x, 'x') 
6597         nx = len(x)  # number of datasets 
6598  
6599         # Process unit information 
6600         # Unit conversion is done individually on each dataset 
6601         self._process_unit_info(xdata=x[0], kwargs=kwargs) 
6602         x = [self.convert_xunits(xi) for xi in x] 
6603  
6604         if bin_range is not None: 
6605             bin_range = self.convert_xunits(bin_range) 
6606  
6607         if not cbook.is_scalar_or_string(bins): 
6608             bins = self.convert_xunits(bins) 
6609  
6610         # We need to do to 'weights' what was done to 'x' 
6611         if weights is not None: 
6612             w = cbook._reshape_2D(weights, 'weights') 
6613         else: 
6614             w = [None] * nx 
6615  
6616         if len(w) != nx: 
6617             raise ValueError('weights should have the same shape as x') 
6618  
6619         for xi, wi in zip(x, w): 
6620             if wi is not None and len(wi) != len(xi): 
6621                 raise ValueError( 
6622                     'weights should have the same shape as x') 
6623  
6624         if color is None: 
6625             color = [self._get_lines.get_next_color() for i in range(nx)] 
6626         else: 
6627             color = mcolors.to_rgba_array(color) 
6628             if len(color) != nx: 
6629                 error_message = ( 
6630                     "color kwarg must have one color per data set. %d data " 
6631                     "sets and %d colors were provided" % (nx, len(color))) 
6632                 raise ValueError(error_message) 
6633  
6634         hist_kwargs = dict() 
6635  
6636         # if the bin_range is not given, compute without nan numpy 
6637         # does not do this for us when guessing the range (but will 
6638         # happily ignore nans when computing the histogram). 
6639         if bin_range is None: 
6640             xmin = np.inf 
6641             xmax = -np.inf 
6642             for xi in x: 
6643                 if len(xi): 
6644                     # python's min/max ignore nan, 
6645                     # np.minnan returns nan for all nan input 
6646                     xmin = min(xmin, np.nanmin(xi)) 
6647                     xmax = max(xmax, np.nanmax(xi)) 
6648             # make sure we have seen at least one non-nan and finite 
6649             # value before we reset the bin range 
6650             if not np.isnan([xmin, xmax]).any() and not (xmin > xmax): 
6651                 bin_range = (xmin, xmax) 
6652  
6653         # If bins are not specified either explicitly or via range, 
6654         # we need to figure out the range required for all datasets, 
6655         # and supply that to np.histogram. 
6656         if not input_empty and len(x) > 1: 
6657             if weights is not None: 
6658                 _w = np.concatenate(w) 
6659             else: 
6660                 _w = None 
6661             bins = np.histogram_bin_edges( 
6662                 np.concatenate(x), bins, bin_range, _w) 
6663         else: 
6664             hist_kwargs['range'] = bin_range 
6665  
6666         density = bool(density) 
6667         if density and not stacked: 
6668             hist_kwargs['density'] = density 
6669  
6670         # List to store all the top coordinates of the histograms 
6671         tops = []  # Will have shape (n_datasets, n_bins). 
6672         # Loop through datasets 
6673         for i in range(nx): 
6674             # this will automatically overwrite bins, 
6675             # so that each histogram uses the same bins 
6676             m, bins = np.histogram(x[i], bins, weights=w[i], **hist_kwargs) 
6677             tops.append(m) 
6678         tops = np.array(tops, float)  # causes problems later if it's an int 
6679         if stacked: 
6680             tops = tops.cumsum(axis=0) 
6681             # If a stacked density plot, normalize so the area of all the 
6682             # stacked histograms together is 1 
6683             if density: 
6684                 tops = (tops / np.diff(bins)) / tops[-1].sum() 
6685         if cumulative: 
6686             slc = slice(None) 
6687             if isinstance(cumulative, Number) and cumulative < 0: 
6688                 slc = slice(None, None, -1) 
6689             if density: 
6690                 tops = (tops * np.diff(bins))[:, slc].cumsum(axis=1)[:, slc] 
6691             else: 
6692                 tops = tops[:, slc].cumsum(axis=1)[:, slc] 
6693  
6694         patches = [] 
6695  
6696         # Save autoscale state for later restoration; turn autoscaling 
6697         # off so we can do it all a single time at the end, instead 
6698         # of having it done by bar or fill and then having to be redone. 
6699         _saved_autoscalex = self.get_autoscalex_on() 
6700         _saved_autoscaley = self.get_autoscaley_on() 
6701         self.set_autoscalex_on(False) 
6702         self.set_autoscaley_on(False) 
6703  
6704         if histtype.startswith('bar'): 
6705  
6706             totwidth = np.diff(bins) 
6707  
6708             if rwidth is not None: 
6709                 dr = np.clip(rwidth, 0, 1) 
6710             elif (len(tops) > 1 and 
6711                   ((not stacked) or rcParams['_internal.classic_mode'])): 
6712                 dr = 0.8 
6713             else: 
6714                 dr = 1.0 
6715  
6716             if histtype == 'bar' and not stacked: 
6717                 width = dr * totwidth / nx 
6718                 dw = width 
6719                 boffset = -0.5 * dr * totwidth * (1 - 1 / nx) 
6720             elif histtype == 'barstacked' or stacked: 
6721                 width = dr * totwidth 
6722                 boffset, dw = 0.0, 0.0 
6723  
6724             if align == 'mid': 
6725                 boffset += 0.5 * totwidth 
6726             elif align == 'right': 
6727                 boffset += totwidth 
6728  
6729             if orientation == 'horizontal': 
6730                 _barfunc = self.barh 
6731                 bottom_kwarg = 'left' 
6732             else:  # orientation == 'vertical' 
6733                 _barfunc = self.bar 
6734                 bottom_kwarg = 'bottom' 
6735  
6736             for m, c in zip(tops, color): 
6737                 if bottom is None: 
6738                     bottom = np.zeros(len(m)) 
6739                 if stacked: 
6740                     height = m - bottom 
6741                 else: 
6742                     height = m 
6743                 patch = _barfunc(bins[:-1]+boffset, height, width, 
6744                                  align='center', log=log, 
6745                                  color=c, **{bottom_kwarg: bottom}) 
6746                 patches.append(patch) 
6747                 if stacked: 
6748                     bottom[:] = m 
6749                 boffset += dw 
6750  
6751         elif histtype.startswith('step'): 
6752             # these define the perimeter of the polygon 
6753             x = np.zeros(4 * len(bins) - 3) 
6754             y = np.zeros(4 * len(bins) - 3) 
6755  
6756             x[0:2*len(bins)-1:2], x[1:2*len(bins)-1:2] = bins, bins[:-1] 
6757             x[2*len(bins)-1:] = x[1:2*len(bins)-1][::-1] 
6758  
6759             if bottom is None: 
6760                 bottom = np.zeros(len(bins) - 1) 
6761  
6762             y[1:2*len(bins)-1:2], y[2:2*len(bins):2] = bottom, bottom 
6763             y[2*len(bins)-1:] = y[1:2*len(bins)-1][::-1] 
6764  
6765             if log: 
6766                 if orientation == 'horizontal': 
6767                     self.set_xscale('log', nonposx='clip') 
6768                 else:  # orientation == 'vertical' 
6769                     self.set_yscale('log', nonposy='clip') 
6770  
6771             if align == 'left': 
6772                 x -= 0.5*(bins[1]-bins[0]) 
6773             elif align == 'right': 
6774                 x += 0.5*(bins[1]-bins[0]) 
6775  
6776             # If fill kwarg is set, it will be passed to the patch collection, 
6777             # overriding this 
6778             fill = (histtype == 'stepfilled') 
6779  
6780             xvals, yvals = [], [] 
6781             for m in tops: 
6782                 if stacked: 
6783                     # top of the previous polygon becomes the bottom 
6784                     y[2*len(bins)-1:] = y[1:2*len(bins)-1][::-1] 
6785                 # set the top of this polygon 
6786                 y[1:2*len(bins)-1:2], y[2:2*len(bins):2] = (m + bottom, 
6787                                                             m + bottom) 
6788  
6789                 # The starting point of the polygon has not yet been 
6790                 # updated. So far only the endpoint was adjusted. This 
6791                 # assignment closes the polygon. The redundant endpoint is 
6792                 # later discarded (for step and stepfilled). 
6793                 y[0] = y[-1] 
6794  
6795                 if orientation == 'horizontal': 
6796                     xvals.append(y.copy()) 
6797                     yvals.append(x.copy()) 
6798                 else: 
6799                     xvals.append(x.copy()) 
6800                     yvals.append(y.copy()) 
6801  
6802             # stepfill is closed, step is not 
6803             split = -1 if fill else 2 * len(bins) 
6804             # add patches in reverse order so that when stacking, 
6805             # items lower in the stack are plotted on top of 
6806             # items higher in the stack 
6807             for x, y, c in reversed(list(zip(xvals, yvals, color))): 
6808                 patches.append(self.fill( 
6809                     x[:split], y[:split], 
6810                     closed=True if fill else None, 
6811                     facecolor=c, 
6812                     edgecolor=None if fill else c, 
6813                     fill=fill if fill else None)) 
6814             for patch_list in patches: 
6815                 for patch in patch_list: 
6816                     if orientation == 'vertical': 
6817                         patch.sticky_edges.y.append(0) 
6818                     elif orientation == 'horizontal': 
6819                         patch.sticky_edges.x.append(0) 
6820  
6821             # we return patches, so put it back in the expected order 
6822             patches.reverse() 
6823  
6824         self.set_autoscalex_on(_saved_autoscalex) 
6825         self.set_autoscaley_on(_saved_autoscaley) 
6826         self._request_autoscale_view() 
6827  
6828         if label is None: 
6829             labels = [None] 
6830         elif isinstance(label, str): 
6831             labels = [label] 
6832         elif not np.iterable(label): 
6833             labels = [str(label)] 
6834         else: 
6835             labels = [str(lab) for lab in label] 
6836  
6837         for patch, lbl in itertools.zip_longest(patches, labels): 
6838             if patch: 
6839                 p = patch[0] 
6840                 p.update(kwargs) 
6841                 if lbl is not None: 
6842                     p.set_label(lbl) 
6843  
6844                 for p in patch[1:]: 
6845                     p.update(kwargs) 
6846                     p.set_label('_nolegend_') 
6847  
6848         if nx == 1: 
6849             return tops[0], bins, cbook.silent_list('Patch', patches[0]) 
6850         else: 
6851             return tops, bins, cbook.silent_list('Lists of Patches', patches) 
6852  
6853     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y", "weights"]) 
6854     @cbook._rename_parameter("3.1", "normed", "density") 
6855     def hist2d(self, x, y, bins=10, range=None, density=False, weights=None, 
6856                cmin=None, cmax=None, **kwargs): 
6857         """ 
6858         Make a 2D histogram plot. 
6859  
6860         Parameters 
6861         ---------- 
6862         x, y : array-like, shape (n, ) 
6863             Input values 
6864  
6865         bins : None or int or [int, int] or array-like or [array, array] 
6866  
6867             The bin specification: 
6868  
6869             - If int, the number of bins for the two dimensions 
6870               (nx=ny=bins). 
6871             - If ``[int, int]``, the number of bins in each dimension 
6872               (nx, ny = bins). 
6873             - If array-like, the bin edges for the two dimensions 
6874               (x_edges=y_edges=bins). 
6875             - If ``[array, array]``, the bin edges in each dimension 
6876               (x_edges, y_edges = bins). 
6877  
6878             The default value is 10. 
6879  
6880         range : array-like shape(2, 2), optional 
6881             The leftmost and rightmost edges of the bins along each dimension 
6882             (if not specified explicitly in the bins parameters): ``[[xmin, 
6883             xmax], [ymin, ymax]]``. All values outside of this range will be 
6884             considered outliers and not tallied in the histogram. 
6885  
6886         density : bool, default: False 
6887             Normalize histogram.  *normed* is a deprecated synonym for this 
6888             parameter. 
6889  
6890         weights : array-like, shape (n, ), optional 
6891             An array of values w_i weighing each sample (x_i, y_i). 
6892  
6893         cmin : scalar, optional, default: None 
6894             All bins that has count less than cmin will not be displayed (set 
6895             to NaN before passing to imshow) and these count values in the 
6896             return value count histogram will also be set to nan upon return. 
6897  
6898         cmax : scalar, optional, default: None 
6899             All bins that has count more than cmax will not be displayed (set 
6900             to NaN before passing to imshow) and these count values in the 
6901             return value count histogram will also be set to nan upon return. 
6902  
6903         Returns 
6904         ------- 
6905         h : 2D array 
6906             The bi-dimensional histogram of samples x and y. Values in x are 
6907             histogrammed along the first dimension and values in y are 
6908             histogrammed along the second dimension. 
6909         xedges : 1D array 
6910             The bin edges along the x axis. 
6911         yedges : 1D array 
6912             The bin edges along the y axis. 
6913         image : `~.matplotlib.collections.QuadMesh` 
6914  
6915         Other Parameters 
6916         ---------------- 
6917         cmap : Colormap or str, optional 
6918             A `.colors.Colormap` instance.  If not set, use rc settings. 
6919  
6920         norm : Normalize, optional 
6921             A `.colors.Normalize` instance is used to 
6922             scale luminance data to ``[0, 1]``. If not set, defaults to 
6923             `.colors.Normalize()`. 
6924  
6925         vmin/vmax : None or scalar, optional 
6926             Arguments passed to the `~.colors.Normalize` instance. 
6927  
6928         alpha : ``0 <= scalar <= 1`` or ``None``, optional 
6929             The alpha blending value. 
6930  
6931         See also 
6932         -------- 
6933         hist : 1D histogram plotting 
6934  
6935         Notes 
6936         ----- 
6937         - Currently ``hist2d`` calculates its own axis limits, and any limits 
6938           previously set are ignored. 
6939         - Rendering the histogram with a logarithmic color scale is 
6940           accomplished by passing a `.colors.LogNorm` instance to the *norm* 
6941           keyword argument. Likewise, power-law normalization (similar 
6942           in effect to gamma correction) can be accomplished with 
6943           `.colors.PowerNorm`. 
6944         """ 
6945  
6946         h, xedges, yedges = np.histogram2d(x, y, bins=bins, range=range, 
6947                                            normed=density, weights=weights) 
6948  
6949         if cmin is not None: 
6950             h[h < cmin] = None 
6951         if cmax is not None: 
6952             h[h > cmax] = None 
6953  
6954         pc = self.pcolormesh(xedges, yedges, h.T, **kwargs) 
6955         self.set_xlim(xedges[0], xedges[-1]) 
6956         self.set_ylim(yedges[0], yedges[-1]) 
6957  
6958         return h, xedges, yedges, pc 
6959  
6960     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x"]) 
6961     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
6962     def psd(self, x, NFFT=None, Fs=None, Fc=None, detrend=None, 
6963             window=None, noverlap=None, pad_to=None, 
6964             sides=None, scale_by_freq=None, return_line=None, **kwargs): 
6965         r""" 
6966         Plot the power spectral density. 
6967  
6968         The power spectral density :math:`P_{xx}` by Welch's average 
6969         periodogram method.  The vector *x* is divided into *NFFT* length 
6970         segments.  Each segment is detrended by function *detrend* and 
6971         windowed by function *window*.  *noverlap* gives the length of 
6972         the overlap between segments.  The :math:`|\mathrm{fft}(i)|^2` 
6973         of each segment :math:`i` are averaged to compute :math:`P_{xx}`, 
6974         with a scaling to correct for power loss due to windowing. 
6975  
6976         If len(*x*) < *NFFT*, it will be zero padded to *NFFT*. 
6977  
6978         Parameters 
6979         ---------- 
6980         x : 1-D array or sequence 
6981             Array or sequence containing the data 
6982  
6983         %(Spectral)s 
6984  
6985         %(PSD)s 
6986  
6987         noverlap : int 
6988             The number of points of overlap between segments. 
6989             The default value is 0 (no overlap). 
6990  
6991         Fc : int 
6992             The center frequency of *x* (defaults to 0), which offsets 
6993             the x extents of the plot to reflect the frequency range used 
6994             when a signal is acquired and then filtered and downsampled to 
6995             baseband. 
6996  
6997         return_line : bool, default: False 
6998             Whether to include the line object plotted in the returned values. 
6999  
7000         Returns 
7001         ------- 
7002         Pxx : 1-D array 
7003             The values for the power spectrum :math:`P_{xx}` before scaling 
7004             (real valued). 
7005  
7006         freqs : 1-D array 
7007             The frequencies corresponding to the elements in *Pxx*. 
7008  
7009         line : `~matplotlib.lines.Line2D` 
7010             The line created by this function. 
7011             Only returned if *return_line* is True. 
7012  
7013         Other Parameters 
7014         ---------------- 
7015         **kwargs 
7016             Keyword arguments control the `.Line2D` properties: 
7017  
7018             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
7019  
7020         See Also 
7021         -------- 
7022         :func:`specgram` 
7023             :func:`specgram` differs in the default overlap; in not returning 
7024             the mean of the segment periodograms; in returning the times of the 
7025             segments; and in plotting a colormap instead of a line. 
7026  
7027         :func:`magnitude_spectrum` 
7028             :func:`magnitude_spectrum` plots the magnitude spectrum. 
7029  
7030         :func:`csd` 
7031             :func:`csd` plots the spectral density between two signals. 
7032  
7033         Notes 
7034         ----- 
7035         For plotting, the power is plotted as 
7036         :math:`10\log_{10}(P_{xx})` for decibels, though *Pxx* itself 
7037         is returned. 
7038  
7039         References 
7040         ---------- 
7041         Bendat & Piersol -- Random Data: Analysis and Measurement Procedures, 
7042         John Wiley & Sons (1986) 
7043         """ 
7044         if Fc is None: 
7045             Fc = 0 
7046  
7047         pxx, freqs = mlab.psd(x=x, NFFT=NFFT, Fs=Fs, detrend=detrend, 
7048                               window=window, noverlap=noverlap, pad_to=pad_to, 
7049                               sides=sides, scale_by_freq=scale_by_freq) 
7050         freqs += Fc 
7051  
7052         if scale_by_freq in (None, True): 
7053             psd_units = 'dB/Hz' 
7054         else: 
7055             psd_units = 'dB' 
7056  
7057         line = self.plot(freqs, 10 * np.log10(pxx), **kwargs) 
7058         self.set_xlabel('Frequency') 
7059         self.set_ylabel('Power Spectral Density (%s)' % psd_units) 
7060         self.grid(True) 
7061         vmin, vmax = self.viewLim.intervaly 
7062         intv = vmax - vmin 
7063         logi = int(np.log10(intv)) 
7064         if logi == 0: 
7065             logi = .1 
7066         step = 10 * logi 
7067         ticks = np.arange(math.floor(vmin), math.ceil(vmax) + 1, step) 
7068         self.set_yticks(ticks) 
7069  
7070         if return_line is None or not return_line: 
7071             return pxx, freqs 
7072         else: 
7073             return pxx, freqs, line 
7074  
7075     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y") 
7076     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
7077     def csd(self, x, y, NFFT=None, Fs=None, Fc=None, detrend=None, 
7078             window=None, noverlap=None, pad_to=None, 
7079             sides=None, scale_by_freq=None, return_line=None, **kwargs): 
7080         r""" 
7081         Plot the cross-spectral density. 
7082  
7083         The cross spectral density :math:`P_{xy}` by Welch's average 
7084         periodogram method.  The vectors *x* and *y* are divided into 
7085         *NFFT* length segments.  Each segment is detrended by function 
7086         *detrend* and windowed by function *window*.  *noverlap* gives 
7087         the length of the overlap between segments.  The product of 
7088         the direct FFTs of *x* and *y* are averaged over each segment 
7089         to compute :math:`P_{xy}`, with a scaling to correct for power 
7090         loss due to windowing. 
7091  
7092         If len(*x*) < *NFFT* or len(*y*) < *NFFT*, they will be zero 
7093         padded to *NFFT*. 
7094  
7095         Parameters 
7096         ---------- 
7097         x, y : 1-D arrays or sequences 
7098             Arrays or sequences containing the data. 
7099  
7100         %(Spectral)s 
7101  
7102         %(PSD)s 
7103  
7104         noverlap : int 
7105             The number of points of overlap between segments. 
7106             The default value is 0 (no overlap). 
7107  
7108         Fc : int 
7109             The center frequency of *x* (defaults to 0), which offsets 
7110             the x extents of the plot to reflect the frequency range used 
7111             when a signal is acquired and then filtered and downsampled to 
7112             baseband. 
7113  
7114         return_line : bool, default: False 
7115             Whether to include the line object plotted in the returned values. 
7116  
7117         Returns 
7118         ------- 
7119         Pxy : 1-D array 
7120             The values for the cross spectrum :math:`P_{xy}` before scaling 
7121             (complex valued). 
7122  
7123         freqs : 1-D array 
7124             The frequencies corresponding to the elements in *Pxy*. 
7125  
7126         line : `~matplotlib.lines.Line2D` 
7127             The line created by this function. 
7128             Only returned if *return_line* is True. 
7129  
7130         Other Parameters 
7131         ---------------- 
7132         **kwargs 
7133             Keyword arguments control the `.Line2D` properties: 
7134  
7135             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
7136  
7137         See Also 
7138         -------- 
7139         :func:`psd` 
7140             :func:`psd` is the equivalent to setting y=x. 
7141  
7142         Notes 
7143         ----- 
7144         For plotting, the power is plotted as 
7145         :math:`10 \log_{10}(P_{xy})` for decibels, though :math:`P_{xy}` itself 
7146         is returned. 
7147  
7148         References 
7149         ---------- 
7150         Bendat & Piersol -- Random Data: Analysis and Measurement Procedures, 
7151         John Wiley & Sons (1986) 
7152         """ 
7153         if Fc is None: 
7154             Fc = 0 
7155  
7156         pxy, freqs = mlab.csd(x=x, y=y, NFFT=NFFT, Fs=Fs, detrend=detrend, 
7157                               window=window, noverlap=noverlap, pad_to=pad_to, 
7158                               sides=sides, scale_by_freq=scale_by_freq) 
7159         # pxy is complex 
7160         freqs += Fc 
7161  
7162         line = self.plot(freqs, 10 * np.log10(np.abs(pxy)), **kwargs) 
7163         self.set_xlabel('Frequency') 
7164         self.set_ylabel('Cross Spectrum Magnitude (dB)') 
7165         self.grid(True) 
7166         vmin, vmax = self.viewLim.intervaly 
7167  
7168         intv = vmax - vmin 
7169         step = 10 * int(np.log10(intv)) 
7170  
7171         ticks = np.arange(math.floor(vmin), math.ceil(vmax) + 1, step) 
7172         self.set_yticks(ticks) 
7173  
7174         if return_line is None or not return_line: 
7175             return pxy, freqs 
7176         else: 
7177             return pxy, freqs, line 
7178  
7179     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x"]) 
7180     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
7181     def magnitude_spectrum(self, x, Fs=None, Fc=None, window=None, 
7182                            pad_to=None, sides=None, scale=None, 
7183                            **kwargs): 
7184         """ 
7185         Plot the magnitude spectrum. 
7186  
7187         Compute the magnitude spectrum of *x*.  Data is padded to a 
7188         length of *pad_to* and the windowing function *window* is applied to 
7189         the signal. 
7190  
7191         Parameters 
7192         ---------- 
7193         x : 1-D array or sequence 
7194             Array or sequence containing the data. 
7195  
7196         %(Spectral)s 
7197  
7198         %(Single_Spectrum)s 
7199  
7200         scale : {'default', 'linear', 'dB'} 
7201             The scaling of the values in the *spec*.  'linear' is no scaling. 
7202             'dB' returns the values in dB scale, i.e., the dB amplitude 
7203             (20 * log10). 'default' is 'linear'. 
7204  
7205         Fc : int 
7206             The center frequency of *x* (defaults to 0), which offsets 
7207             the x extents of the plot to reflect the frequency range used 
7208             when a signal is acquired and then filtered and downsampled to 
7209             baseband. 
7210  
7211         Returns 
7212         ------- 
7213         spectrum : 1-D array 
7214             The values for the magnitude spectrum before scaling (real valued). 
7215  
7216         freqs : 1-D array 
7217             The frequencies corresponding to the elements in *spectrum*. 
7218  
7219         line : `~matplotlib.lines.Line2D` 
7220             The line created by this function. 
7221  
7222         Other Parameters 
7223         ---------------- 
7224         **kwargs 
7225             Keyword arguments control the `.Line2D` properties: 
7226  
7227             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
7228  
7229         See Also 
7230         -------- 
7231         :func:`psd` 
7232             :func:`psd` plots the power spectral density.`. 
7233  
7234         :func:`angle_spectrum` 
7235             :func:`angle_spectrum` plots the angles of the corresponding 
7236             frequencies. 
7237  
7238         :func:`phase_spectrum` 
7239             :func:`phase_spectrum` plots the phase (unwrapped angle) of the 
7240             corresponding frequencies. 
7241  
7242         :func:`specgram` 
7243             :func:`specgram` can plot the magnitude spectrum of segments within 
7244             the signal in a colormap. 
7245  
7246         """ 
7247         if Fc is None: 
7248             Fc = 0 
7249  
7250         spec, freqs = mlab.magnitude_spectrum(x=x, Fs=Fs, window=window, 
7251                                               pad_to=pad_to, sides=sides) 
7252         freqs += Fc 
7253  
7254         yunits = cbook._check_getitem( 
7255             {None: 'energy', 'default': 'energy', 'linear': 'energy', 
7256              'dB': 'dB'}, 
7257             scale=scale) 
7258         if yunits == 'energy': 
7259             Z = spec 
7260         else:  # yunits == 'dB' 
7261             Z = 20. * np.log10(spec) 
7262  
7263         line, = self.plot(freqs, Z, **kwargs) 
7264         self.set_xlabel('Frequency') 
7265         self.set_ylabel('Magnitude (%s)' % yunits) 
7266  
7267         return spec, freqs, line

7412     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"]) 
7413     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
7414     def cohere(self, x, y, NFFT=256, Fs=2, Fc=0, detrend=mlab.detrend_none, 
7415                window=mlab.window_hanning, noverlap=0, pad_to=None, 
7416                sides='default', scale_by_freq=None, **kwargs): 
7417         r""" 
7418         Plot the coherence between *x* and *y*. 
7419  
7420         Plot the coherence between *x* and *y*.  Coherence is the 
7421         normalized cross spectral density: 
7422  
7423         .. math:: 
7424  
7425           C_{xy} = \frac{|P_{xy}|^2}{P_{xx}P_{yy}} 
7426  
7427         Parameters 
7428         ---------- 
7429         %(Spectral)s 
7430  
7431         %(PSD)s 
7432  
7433         noverlap : int 
7434             The number of points of overlap between blocks.  The 
7435             default value is 0 (no overlap). 
7436  
7437         Fc : int 
7438             The center frequency of *x* (defaults to 0), which offsets 
7439             the x extents of the plot to reflect the frequency range used 
7440             when a signal is acquired and then filtered and downsampled to 
7441             baseband. 
7442  
7443  
7444         Returns 
7445         ------- 
7446         Cxy : 1-D array 
7447             The coherence vector. 
7448  
7449         freqs : 1-D array 
7450             The frequencies for the elements in *Cxy*. 
7451  
7452         Other Parameters 
7453         ---------------- 
7454         **kwargs 
7455             Keyword arguments control the `.Line2D` properties: 
7456  
7457             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
7458  
7459         References 
7460         ---------- 
7461         Bendat & Piersol -- Random Data: Analysis and Measurement Procedures, 
7462         John Wiley & Sons (1986) 
7463         """ 
7464         cxy, freqs = mlab.cohere(x=x, y=y, NFFT=NFFT, Fs=Fs, detrend=detrend, 
7465                                  window=window, noverlap=noverlap, 
7466                                  scale_by_freq=scale_by_freq) 
7467         freqs += Fc 
7468  
7469         self.plot(freqs, cxy, **kwargs) 
7470         self.set_xlabel('Frequency') 
7471         self.set_ylabel('Coherence') 
7472         self.grid(True) 
7473  
7474         return cxy, freqs
