7476     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x"]) 
7477     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
7478     def specgram(self, x, NFFT=None, Fs=None, Fc=None, detrend=None, 
7479                  window=None, noverlap=None, 
7480                  cmap=None, xextent=None, pad_to=None, sides=None, 
7481                  scale_by_freq=None, mode=None, scale=None, 
7482                  vmin=None, vmax=None, **kwargs): 
7483         """ 
7484         Plot a spectrogram. 
7485  
7486         Compute and plot a spectrogram of data in *x*.  Data are split into 
7487         *NFFT* length segments and the spectrum of each section is 
7488         computed.  The windowing function *window* is applied to each 
7489         segment, and the amount of overlap of each segment is 
7490         specified with *noverlap*. The spectrogram is plotted as a colormap 
7491         (using imshow). 
7492  
7493         Parameters 
7494         ---------- 
7495         x : 1-D array or sequence 
7496             Array or sequence containing the data. 
7497  
7498         %(Spectral)s 
7499  
7500         %(PSD)s 
7501  
7502         mode : {'default', 'psd', 'magnitude', 'angle', 'phase'} 
7503             What sort of spectrum to use.  Default is 'psd', which takes the 
7504             power spectral density.  'magnitude' returns the magnitude 
7505             spectrum.  'angle' returns the phase spectrum without unwrapping. 
7506             'phase' returns the phase spectrum with unwrapping. 
7507  
7508         noverlap : int 
7509             The number of points of overlap between blocks.  The 
7510             default value is 128. 
7511  
7512         scale : {'default', 'linear', 'dB'} 
7513             The scaling of the values in the *spec*.  'linear' is no scaling. 
7514             'dB' returns the values in dB scale.  When *mode* is 'psd', 
7515             this is dB power (10 * log10).  Otherwise this is dB amplitude 
7516             (20 * log10). 'default' is 'dB' if *mode* is 'psd' or 
7517             'magnitude' and 'linear' otherwise.  This must be 'linear' 
7518             if *mode* is 'angle' or 'phase'. 
7519  
7520         Fc : int 
7521             The center frequency of *x* (defaults to 0), which offsets 
7522             the x extents of the plot to reflect the frequency range used 
7523             when a signal is acquired and then filtered and downsampled to 
7524             baseband. 
7525  
7526         cmap 
7527             A :class:`matplotlib.colors.Colormap` instance; if *None*, use 
7528             default determined by rc 
7529  
7530         xextent : *None* or (xmin, xmax) 
7531             The image extent along the x-axis. The default sets *xmin* to the 
7532             left border of the first bin (*spectrum* column) and *xmax* to the 
7533             right border of the last bin. Note that for *noverlap>0* the width 
7534             of the bins is smaller than those of the segments. 
7535  
7536         **kwargs 
7537             Additional keyword arguments are passed on to imshow which makes 
7538             the specgram image. 
7539  
7540         Returns 
7541         ------- 
7542         spectrum : 2-D array 
7543             Columns are the periodograms of successive segments. 
7544  
7545         freqs : 1-D array 
7546             The frequencies corresponding to the rows in *spectrum*. 
7547  
7548         t : 1-D array 
7549             The times corresponding to midpoints of segments (i.e., the columns 
7550             in *spectrum*). 
7551  
7552         im : instance of class :class:`~matplotlib.image.AxesImage` 
7553             The image created by imshow containing the spectrogram 
7554  
7555         See Also 
7556         -------- 
7557         :func:`psd` 
7558             :func:`psd` differs in the default overlap; in returning the mean 
7559             of the segment periodograms; in not returning times; and in 
7560             generating a line plot instead of colormap. 
7561  
7562         :func:`magnitude_spectrum` 
7563             A single spectrum, similar to having a single segment when *mode* 
7564             is 'magnitude'. Plots a line instead of a colormap. 
7565  
7566         :func:`angle_spectrum` 
7567             A single spectrum, similar to having a single segment when *mode* 
7568             is 'angle'. Plots a line instead of a colormap. 
7569  
7570         :func:`phase_spectrum` 
7571             A single spectrum, similar to having a single segment when *mode* 
7572             is 'phase'. Plots a line instead of a colormap. 
7573  
7574         Notes 
7575         ----- 
7576         The parameters *detrend* and *scale_by_freq* do only apply when *mode* 
7577         is set to 'psd'. 
7578         """ 
7579         if NFFT is None: 
7580             NFFT = 256  # same default as in mlab.specgram() 
7581         if Fc is None: 
7582             Fc = 0  # same default as in mlab._spectral_helper() 
7583         if noverlap is None: 
7584             noverlap = 128  # same default as in mlab.specgram() 
7585  
7586         if mode == 'complex': 
7587             raise ValueError('Cannot plot a complex specgram') 
7588  
7589         if scale is None or scale == 'default': 
7590             if mode in ['angle', 'phase']: 
7591                 scale = 'linear' 
7592             else: 
7593                 scale = 'dB' 
7594         elif mode in ['angle', 'phase'] and scale == 'dB': 
7595             raise ValueError('Cannot use dB scale with angle or phase mode') 
7596  
7597         spec, freqs, t = mlab.specgram(x=x, NFFT=NFFT, Fs=Fs, 
7598                                        detrend=detrend, window=window, 
7599                                        noverlap=noverlap, pad_to=pad_to, 
7600                                        sides=sides, 
7601                                        scale_by_freq=scale_by_freq, 
7602                                        mode=mode) 
7603  
7604         if scale == 'linear': 
7605             Z = spec 
7606         elif scale == 'dB': 
7607             if mode is None or mode == 'default' or mode == 'psd': 
7608                 Z = 10. * np.log10(spec) 
7609             else: 
7610                 Z = 20. * np.log10(spec) 
7611         else: 
7612             raise ValueError('Unknown scale %s', scale) 
7613  
7614         Z = np.flipud(Z) 
7615  
7616         if xextent is None: 
7617             # padding is needed for first and last segment: 
7618             pad_xextent = (NFFT-noverlap) / Fs / 2 
7619             xextent = np.min(t) - pad_xextent, np.max(t) + pad_xextent 
7620         xmin, xmax = xextent 
7621         freqs += Fc 
7622         extent = xmin, xmax, freqs[0], freqs[-1] 
7623         im = self.imshow(Z, cmap, extent=extent, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, 
7624                          **kwargs) 
7625         self.axis('auto') 
7626  
7627         return spec, freqs, t, im

7629     @docstring.dedent_interpd 
7630     def spy(self, Z, precision=0, marker=None, markersize=None, 
7631             aspect='equal', origin="upper", **kwargs): 
7632         """ 
7633         Plot the sparsity pattern of a 2D array. 
7634  
7635         This visualizes the non-zero values of the array. 
7636  
7637         Two plotting styles are available: image and marker. Both 
7638         are available for full arrays, but only the marker style 
7639         works for `scipy.sparse.spmatrix` instances. 
7640  
7641         **Image style** 
7642  
7643         If *marker* and *markersize* are *None*, `~.Axes.imshow` is used. Any 
7644         extra remaining keyword arguments are passed to this method. 
7645  
7646         **Marker style** 
7647  
7648         If *Z* is a `scipy.sparse.spmatrix` or *marker* or *markersize* are 
7649         *None*, a `.Line2D` object will be returned with the value of marker 
7650         determining the marker type, and any remaining keyword arguments 
7651         passed to `~.Axes.plot`. 
7652  
7653         Parameters 
7654         ---------- 
7655         Z : array-like (M, N) 
7656             The array to be plotted. 
7657  
7658         precision : float or 'present', default: 0 
7659             If *precision* is 0, any non-zero value will be plotted. Otherwise, 
7660             values of :math:`|Z| > precision` will be plotted. 
7661  
7662             For :class:`scipy.sparse.spmatrix` instances, you can also 
7663             pass 'present'. In this case any value present in the array 
7664             will be plotted, even if it is identically zero. 
7665  
7666         origin : {'upper', 'lower'}, default: :rc:`image.origin` 
7667             Place the [0, 0] index of the array in the upper left or lower left 
7668             corner of the axes. The convention 'upper' is typically used for 
7669             matrices and images. 
7670  
7671         aspect : {'equal', 'auto', None} or float, default: 'equal' 
7672             The aspect ratio of the axes.  This parameter is particularly 
7673             relevant for images since it determines whether data pixels are 
7674             square. 
7675  
7676             This parameter is a shortcut for explicitly calling 
7677             `.Axes.set_aspect`. See there for further details. 
7678  
7679             - 'equal': Ensures an aspect ratio of 1. Pixels will be square. 
7680             - 'auto': The axes is kept fixed and the aspect is adjusted so 
7681               that the data fit in the axes. In general, this will result in 
7682               non-square pixels. 
7683             - *None*: Use :rc:`image.aspect`. 
7684  
7685         Returns 
7686         ------- 
7687         ret : `~matplotlib.image.AxesImage` or `.Line2D` 
7688             The return type depends on the plotting style (see above). 
7689  
7690         Other Parameters 
7691         ---------------- 
7692         **kwargs 
7693             The supported additional parameters depend on the plotting style. 
7694  
7695             For the image style, you can pass the following additional 
7696             parameters of `~.Axes.imshow`: 
7697  
7698             - *cmap* 
7699             - *alpha* 
7700             - *url* 
7701             - any `.Artist` properties (passed on to the `.AxesImage`) 
7702  
7703             For the marker style, you can pass any `.Line2D` property except 
7704             for *linestyle*: 
7705  
7706             %(_Line2D_docstr)s 
7707         """ 
7708         if marker is None and markersize is None and hasattr(Z, 'tocoo'): 
7709             marker = 's' 
7710         if marker is None and markersize is None: 
7711             Z = np.asarray(Z) 
7712             mask = np.abs(Z) > precision 
7713  
7714             if 'cmap' not in kwargs: 
7715                 kwargs['cmap'] = mcolors.ListedColormap(['w', 'k'], 
7716                                                         name='binary') 
7717             if 'interpolation' in kwargs: 
7718                 raise TypeError( 
7719                     "spy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'interpolation'") 
7720             ret = self.imshow(mask, interpolation='nearest', aspect=aspect, 
7721                               origin=origin, **kwargs) 
7722         else: 
7723             if hasattr(Z, 'tocoo'): 
7724                 c = Z.tocoo() 
7725                 if precision == 'present': 
7726                     y = c.row 
7727                     x = c.col 
7728                 else: 
7729                     nonzero = np.abs(c.data) > precision 
7730                     y = c.row[nonzero] 
7731                     x = c.col[nonzero] 
7732             else: 
7733                 Z = np.asarray(Z) 
7734                 nonzero = np.abs(Z) > precision 
7735                 y, x = np.nonzero(nonzero) 
7736             if marker is None: 
7737                 marker = 's' 
7738             if markersize is None: 
7739                 markersize = 10 
7740             if 'linestyle' in kwargs: 
7741                 raise TypeError( 
7742                     "spy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'linestyle'") 
7743             marks = mlines.Line2D(x, y, linestyle='None', 
7744                          marker=marker, markersize=markersize, **kwargs) 
7745             self.add_line(marks) 
7746             nr, nc = Z.shape 
7747             self.set_xlim(-0.5, nc - 0.5) 
7748             self.set_ylim(nr - 0.5, -0.5) 
7749             self.set_aspect(aspect) 
7750             ret = marks 
7751         self.title.set_y(1.05) 
7752         self.xaxis.tick_top() 
7753         self.xaxis.set_ticks_position('both') 
7754         self.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=9, 
7755                                                  steps=[1, 2, 5, 10], 
7756                                                  integer=True)) 
7757         self.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=9, 
7758                                                  steps=[1, 2, 5, 10], 
7759                                                  integer=True)) 
7760         return ret 
7761  
7762     def matshow(self, Z, **kwargs): 
7763         """ 
7764         Plot the values of a 2D matrix or array as color-coded image. 
7765  
7766         The matrix will be shown the way it would be printed, with the first 
7767         row at the top.  Row and column numbering is zero-based. 
7768  
7769         Parameters 
7770         ---------- 
7771         Z : array-like(M, N) 
7772             The matrix to be displayed. 
7773  
7774         Returns 
7775         ------- 
7776         image : `~matplotlib.image.AxesImage` 
7777  
7778         Other Parameters 
7779         ---------------- 
7780         **kwargs : `~matplotlib.axes.Axes.imshow` arguments 
7781  
7782         See Also 
7783         -------- 
7784         imshow : More general function to plot data on a 2D regular raster. 
7785  
7786         Notes 
7787         ----- 
7788         This is just a convenience function wrapping `.imshow` to set useful 
7789         defaults for displaying a matrix. In particular: 
7790  
7791         - Set ``origin='upper'``. 
7792         - Set ``interpolation='nearest'``. 
7793         - Set ``aspect='equal'``. 
7794         - Ticks are placed to the left and above. 
7795         - Ticks are formatted to show integer indices. 
7796  
7797         """ 
7798         Z = np.asanyarray(Z) 
7799         kw = {'origin': 'upper', 
7800               'interpolation': 'nearest', 
7801               'aspect': 'equal',          # (already the imshow default) 
7802               **kwargs} 
7803         im = self.imshow(Z, **kw) 
7804         self.title.set_y(1.05) 
7805         self.xaxis.tick_top() 
7806         self.xaxis.set_ticks_position('both') 
7807         self.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=9, 
7808                                                  steps=[1, 2, 5, 10], 
7809                                                  integer=True)) 
7810         self.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=9, 
7811                                                  steps=[1, 2, 5, 10], 
7812                                                  integer=True)) 
7813         return im

7815     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["dataset"]) 
7816     def violinplot(self, dataset, positions=None, vert=True, widths=0.5, 
7817                    showmeans=False, showextrema=True, showmedians=False, 
7818                    quantiles=None, points=100, bw_method=None): 
7819         """ 
7820         Make a violin plot. 
7821  
7822         Make a violin plot for each column of *dataset* or each vector in 
7823         sequence *dataset*.  Each filled area extends to represent the 
7824         entire data range, with optional lines at the mean, the median, 
7825         the minimum, the maximum, and user-specified quantiles. 
7826  
7827         Parameters 
7828         ---------- 
7829         dataset : Array or a sequence of vectors. 
7830           The input data. 
7831  
7832         positions : array-like, default: [1, 2, ..., n] 
7833           Sets the positions of the violins. The ticks and limits are 
7834           automatically set to match the positions. 
7835  
7836         vert : bool, default: True. 
7837           If true, creates a vertical violin plot. 
7838           Otherwise, creates a horizontal violin plot. 
7839  
7840         widths : array-like, default: 0.5 
7841           Either a scalar or a vector that sets the maximal width of 
7842           each violin. The default is 0.5, which uses about half of the 
7843           available horizontal space. 
7844  
7845         showmeans : bool, default: False 
7846           If `True`, will toggle rendering of the means. 
7847  
7848         showextrema : bool, default: True 
7849           If `True`, will toggle rendering of the extrema. 
7850  
7851         showmedians : bool, default: False 
7852           If `True`, will toggle rendering of the medians. 
7853  
7854         quantiles : array-like, default: None 
7855           If not None, set a list of floats in interval [0, 1] for each violin, 
7856           which stands for the quantiles that will be rendered for that 
7857           violin. 
7858  
7859         points : scalar, default: 100 
7860           Defines the number of points to evaluate each of the 
7861           gaussian kernel density estimations at. 
7862  
7863         bw_method : str, scalar or callable, optional 
7864           The method used to calculate the estimator bandwidth.  This can be 
7865           'scott', 'silverman', a scalar constant or a callable.  If a 
7866           scalar, this will be used directly as `kde.factor`.  If a 
7867           callable, it should take a `GaussianKDE` instance as its only 
7868           parameter and return a scalar. If None (default), 'scott' is used. 
7869  
7870         Returns 
7871         ------- 
7872         result : dict 
7873           A dictionary mapping each component of the violinplot to a 
7874           list of the corresponding collection instances created. The 
7875           dictionary has the following keys: 
7876  
7877           - ``bodies``: A list of the `~.collections.PolyCollection` 
7878             instances containing the filled area of each violin. 
7879  
7880           - ``cmeans``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7881             the mean values of each of the violin's distribution. 
7882  
7883           - ``cmins``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7884             the bottom of each violin's distribution. 
7885  
7886           - ``cmaxes``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7887             the top of each violin's distribution. 
7888  
7889           - ``cbars``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7890             the centers of each violin's distribution. 
7891  
7892           - ``cmedians``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that 
7893             marks the median values of each of the violin's distribution. 
7894  
7895           - ``cquantiles``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance created 
7896             to identify the quantile values of each of the violin's 
7897             distribution. 
7898  
7899         """ 
7900  
7901         def _kde_method(X, coords): 
7902             # fallback gracefully if the vector contains only one value 
7903             if np.all(X[0] == X): 
7904                 return (X[0] == coords).astype(float) 
7905             kde = mlab.GaussianKDE(X, bw_method) 
7906             return kde.evaluate(coords) 
7907  
7908         vpstats = cbook.violin_stats(dataset, _kde_method, points=points, 
7909                                      quantiles=quantiles) 
7910         return self.violin(vpstats, positions=positions, vert=vert, 
7911                            widths=widths, showmeans=showmeans, 
7912                            showextrema=showextrema, showmedians=showmedians) 
7913  
7914     def violin(self, vpstats, positions=None, vert=True, widths=0.5, 
7915                showmeans=False, showextrema=True, showmedians=False): 
7916         """Drawing function for violin plots. 
7917  
7918         Draw a violin plot for each column of *vpstats*. Each filled area 
7919         extends to represent the entire data range, with optional lines at the 
7920         mean, the median, the minimum, the maximum, and the quantiles values. 
7921  
7922         Parameters 
7923         ---------- 
7924         vpstats : list of dicts 
7925           A list of dictionaries containing stats for each violin plot. 
7926           Required keys are: 
7927  
7928           - ``coords``: A list of scalars containing the coordinates that 
7929             the violin's kernel density estimate were evaluated at. 
7930  
7931           - ``vals``: A list of scalars containing the values of the 
7932             kernel density estimate at each of the coordinates given 
7933             in *coords*. 
7934  
7935           - ``mean``: The mean value for this violin's dataset. 
7936  
7937           - ``median``: The median value for this violin's dataset. 
7938  
7939           - ``min``: The minimum value for this violin's dataset. 
7940  
7941           - ``max``: The maximum value for this violin's dataset. 
7942  
7943           Optional keys are: 
7944  
7945           - ``quantiles``: A list of scalars containing the quantile values 
7946             for this violin's dataset. 
7947  
7948         positions : array-like, default: [1, 2, ..., n] 
7949           Sets the positions of the violins. The ticks and limits are 
7950           automatically set to match the positions. 
7951  
7952         vert : bool, default: True. 
7953           If true, plots the violins vertically. 
7954           Otherwise, plots the violins horizontally. 
7955  
7956         widths : array-like, default: 0.5 
7957           Either a scalar or a vector that sets the maximal width of 
7958           each violin. The default is 0.5, which uses about half of the 
7959           available horizontal space. 
7960  
7961         showmeans : bool, default: False 
7962           If true, will toggle rendering of the means. 
7963  
7964         showextrema : bool, default: True 
7965           If true, will toggle rendering of the extrema. 
7966  
7967         showmedians : bool, default: False 
7968           If true, will toggle rendering of the medians. 
7969  
7970         Returns 
7971         ------- 
7972         result : dict 
7973           A dictionary mapping each component of the violinplot to a 
7974           list of the corresponding collection instances created. The 
7975           dictionary has the following keys: 
7976  
7977           - ``bodies``: A list of the `~.collections.PolyCollection` 
7978             instances containing the filled area of each violin. 
7979  
7980           - ``cmeans``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7981             the mean values of each of the violin's distribution. 
7982  
7983           - ``cmins``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7984             the bottom of each violin's distribution. 
7985  
7986           - ``cmaxes``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7987             the top of each violin's distribution. 
7988  
7989           - ``cbars``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that marks 
7990             the centers of each violin's distribution. 
7991  
7992           - ``cmedians``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance that 
7993             marks the median values of each of the violin's distribution. 
7994  
7995           - ``cquantiles``: A `~.collections.LineCollection` instance created 
7996             to identify the quantiles values of each of the violin's 
7997             distribution. 
7998  
7999         """ 
8000  
8001         # Statistical quantities to be plotted on the violins 
8002         means = [] 
8003         mins = [] 
8004         maxes = [] 
8005         medians = [] 
8006         quantiles = np.asarray([]) 
8007  
8008         # Collections to be returned 
8009         artists = {} 
8010  
8011         N = len(vpstats) 
8012         datashape_message = ("List of violinplot statistics and `{0}` " 
8013                              "values must have the same length") 
8014  
8015         # Validate positions 
8016         if positions is None: 
8017             positions = range(1, N + 1) 
8018         elif len(positions) != N: 
8019             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("positions")) 
8020  
8021         # Validate widths 
8022         if np.isscalar(widths): 
8023             widths = [widths] * N 
8024         elif len(widths) != N: 
8025             raise ValueError(datashape_message.format("widths")) 
8026  
8027         # Calculate ranges for statistics lines 
8028         pmins = -0.25 * np.array(widths) + positions 
8029         pmaxes = 0.25 * np.array(widths) + positions 
8030  
8031         # Check whether we are rendering vertically or horizontally 
8032         if vert: 
8033             fill = self.fill_betweenx 
8034             perp_lines = self.hlines 
8035             par_lines = self.vlines 
8036         else: 
8037             fill = self.fill_between 
8038             perp_lines = self.vlines 
8039             par_lines = self.hlines 
8040  
8041         if rcParams['_internal.classic_mode']: 
8042             fillcolor = 'y' 
8043             edgecolor = 'r' 
8044         else: 
8045             fillcolor = edgecolor = self._get_lines.get_next_color() 
8046  
8047         # Render violins 
8048         bodies = [] 
8049         for stats, pos, width in zip(vpstats, positions, widths): 
8050             # The 0.5 factor reflects the fact that we plot from v-p to 
8051             # v+p 
8052             vals = np.array(stats['vals']) 
8053             vals = 0.5 * width * vals / vals.max() 
8054             bodies += [fill(stats['coords'], 
8055                             -vals + pos, 
8056                             vals + pos, 
8057                             facecolor=fillcolor, 
8058                             alpha=0.3)] 
8059             means.append(stats['mean']) 
8060             mins.append(stats['min']) 
8061             maxes.append(stats['max']) 
8062             medians.append(stats['median']) 
8063             q = stats.get('quantiles') 
8064             if q is not None: 
8065                 # If exist key quantiles, assume it's a list of floats 
8066                 quantiles = np.concatenate((quantiles, q)) 
8067         artists['bodies'] = bodies 
8068  
8069         # Render means 
8070         if showmeans: 
8071             artists['cmeans'] = perp_lines(means, pmins, pmaxes, 
8072                                            colors=edgecolor) 
8073  
8074         # Render extrema 
8075         if showextrema: 
8076             artists['cmaxes'] = perp_lines(maxes, pmins, pmaxes, 
8077                                            colors=edgecolor) 
8078             artists['cmins'] = perp_lines(mins, pmins, pmaxes, 
8079                                           colors=edgecolor) 
8080             artists['cbars'] = par_lines(positions, mins, maxes, 
8081                                          colors=edgecolor) 
8082  
8083         # Render medians 
8084         if showmedians: 
8085             artists['cmedians'] = perp_lines(medians, 
8086                                              pmins, 
8087                                              pmaxes, 
8088                                              colors=edgecolor) 
8089  
8090         # Render quantile values 
8091         if quantiles.size > 0: 
8092             # Recalculate ranges for statistics lines for quantiles. 
8093             # ppmins are the left end of quantiles lines 
8094             ppmins = np.asarray([]) 
8095             # pmaxes are the right end of quantiles lines 
8096             ppmaxs = np.asarray([]) 
8097             for stats, cmin, cmax in zip(vpstats, pmins, pmaxes): 
8098                 q = stats.get('quantiles') 
8099                 if q is not None: 
8100                     ppmins = np.concatenate((ppmins, [cmin] * np.size(q))) 
8101                     ppmaxs = np.concatenate((ppmaxs, [cmax] * np.size(q))) 
8102             # Start rendering 
8103             artists['cquantiles'] = perp_lines(quantiles, ppmins, ppmaxs, 
8104                                                  colors=edgecolor) 
8105  
8106         return artists
